sources.title: Crypto giant Binance hit by $6.3bn hack suspected to be largest in history - BBC
passages: Cryptocurrency giant Binance said on Thursday that $6.3bn (£4.7bn) of digital assets have been impacted by what is thought to be the biggest crypto hack on record.
The lab's global head of policy Ari Redbord told the BBC the Binance hack is a "watershed moment" that is unlike anything the industry has seen.
Check Point's chief information security officer Jayant Dave said the losses estimated by Binance made it "the largest crypto theft on record".
Two other major crypto platforms, Tether and Circle, said they had frozen a total of about $2.4bn of assets in response to the potential Binance hack.

Binance did not directly respond to BBC questions about the incident's potential links to North Korea but said: "We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice."
Several crypto industry observers had flagged concerns about a potential hack on Binance hours before the exchange confirmed the security issue.
AI-powered investigations company TRM Labs said in a report that several elements of the Binance attack resemble earlier North Korean-linked incidents, including the Bybit hack.
Binance, which was founded in China in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide.
Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said the company's initial investigation suggested the hack started with a compromised engineer's laptop.
Chainalysis, a crypto analytics firm, also said it has "high confidence" that the North Korean group are linked to the hack.
Crypto exchange Coinbase said it was unaffected by the incident and was monitoring the situation.
In a series of posts, Yi He, Binance's co-chief executive, thanked various cryptocurrency issuers for freezing the assets.
The world's biggest crypto exchange said about half of those assets had been frozen but that many remained in the hands of the hackers, adding that it will "cover all losses".

extraction.body: Cryptocurrency giant Binance said on Thursday that $6.3bn (£4.7bn) of digital assets have been impacted by what is thought to be the biggest crypto hack on record. The world's biggest crypto exchange said about half of those assets had been frozen but that many remained in the hands of the hackers, adding that it will "cover all losses". The company said while initial checks suggested an engineer's laptop had been compromised, allowing an attacker to make unauthorised withdrawals, "our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach". Two analytics firms have attributed the incident, which eclipses a record-setting $1.5bn hack on the Bybit exchange in 2025, to a North Korean hacking unit called TraderTraitor. Cyber-security firm Check Point said the unit is also known in the industry as Lazarus Group, which has been blamed for the 2025 hack. Check Point's chief information security officer Jayant Dave said the losses estimated by Binance made it "the largest crypto theft on record". AI-powered investigations company TRM Labs said in a report that several elements of the Binance attack resemble earlier North Korean-linked incidents, including the Bybit hack. The lab's global head of policy Ari Redbord told the BBC the Binance hack is a "watershed moment" that is unlike anything the industry has seen. The attacker still holds an enormous sum of stolen assets, meaning efforts to trace and recover the funds are far from over, Redbord added. Binance, which was founded in China in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide. The company said in 2024 that it has more than $160bn in assets under its custody. The exchange has been subject of regulatory scrutiny around the world. Chainalysis, a crypto analytics firm, also said it has "high confidence" that the North Korean group are linked to the hack. For the last few years North Korea-linked operatives have focussed on attacking cryptocurrency companies for large thefts of digital tokens. The regime has denied any involvement in hacks in the past. Eric Jardine, Chainalysis' Head of Research, urged every exchange to remain vigilant as the platforms are attractive targets for hackers due to the sheer value of assets. Binance did not directly respond to BBC questions about the incident's potential links to North Korea but said: "We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice." The incident concerns Binance.com - while much smaller crypto platform Binance.US, which provides trading services specifically for American residents - said its platform is not affected by the issue. Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said the company's initial investigation suggested the hack started with a compromised engineer's laptop. "That gave an attacker access to a service container, where they submitted unauthorized withdrawal transactions," he said in a statement. In an update, the company said in a statement on X that another investigation found there had been other breach points: "We are still gathering the facts, and will share more directly as we have them." Check Point's Dave said this attack also resembled a hack on crypto exchange platform Bitget in September in which $388m (£289m) was lost: "This implies that attackers no longer need the vault keys. They target the systems and people with authority to use them." In a series of posts, Yi He, Binance's co-chief executive, thanked various cryptocurrency issuers for freezing the assets. "Safety first: withdrawals are currently disabled until the environment is confirmed to be secure," she said. Two other major crypto platforms, Tether and Circle, said they had frozen a total of about $2.4bn of assets in response to the potential Binance hack. World Liberty Financial, a crypto company linked to US President Donald Trump and his family, said it has worked with its partners to freeze stolen funds. Crypto exchange Coinbase said it was unaffected by the incident and was monitoring the situation. Several crypto industry observers had flagged concerns about a potential hack on Binance hours before the exchange confirmed the security issue. Bitcoin dropped by more than 4% following the alerts. The price of other major cryptocurrencies including Ethereum and Solana also fell sharply. The Binance hack has thrust cryptocurrencies back into headlines - but what are they and how do they work? BBC business reporter Archana Shukla explains more about what is suspected to be the largest hack in history. Prosecutors had accused Pleterski of stealing tens of millions of dollars of investor funds to buy himself a range of luxuries.

sources.title: Binance Suspends Withdrawals After $6.3 Billion Cryptocurrency Hack as Bitcoin and Crypto Stocks Fall - Yahoo Finance
passages: Binance temporarily suspended withdrawals after reporting a security breach involving approximately $6.3 billion in stolen digital assets, triggering losses across cryptocurrency markets and shares of companies exposed to the sector.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
Bitcoin fell sharply following the announcement, while Ether, Binance's BNB token and several cryptocurrency-related stocks also recorded significant declines.
The attacker also withdrew 17,985 Bitcoin, valued at approximately $1.45 billion at the time.
Bitcoin, the world's largest cryptocurrency by market capitalisation, fell 2.5% to $78,106.60.
Binance said it had coordinated with industry partners to freeze approximately $3 billion of the assets affected by the attack.
The absence of a reported reduction in BNB holdings contrasted with the substantial losses involving Bitcoin, stablecoins and other cryptocurrencies.
The immediate focus for cryptocurrency markets will be Binance's progress in completing its security checks and restoring withdrawal services.
Binance indicated that it expects the suspension to last no longer than 48 hours, although the resumption of withdrawals remains dependent on the completion of its security procedures.
"It does look like a hack on Binance," Zhao said in a social media post.
Binance said its investigation had found no evidence that private keys associated with cryptocurrency wallets had been exposed.

Binance temporarily suspended withdrawals after reporting a security breach involving approximately $6.3 billion in stolen digital assets, triggering losses across cryptocurrency markets and shares of companies exposed to the sector. The incident, disclosed on Thursday evening, represents the largest reported cryptocurrency theft on record, according to the exchange. Binance said it had worked with industry partners to freeze approximately $3 billion in affected assets and would cover all losses using its own funds. The exchange expects withdrawals to resume within 48 hours, subject to the completion of additional security checks. Bitcoin fell sharply following the announcement, while Ether, Binance's BNB token and several cryptocurrency-related stocks also recorded significant declines. Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, confirmed that an attacker had exploited a security vulnerability to carry out unauthorised withdrawals. The company estimated the total financial impact at $6.3 billion, making the incident substantially larger than previous cryptocurrency exchange hacks. According to Binance, the breach originated from a compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer. The attacker used the compromised device to execute unauthorised withdrawals from the exchange. Binance said its investigation had found no evidence that private keys associated with cryptocurrency wallets had been exposed. The distinction is significant because private keys provide direct control over digital assets held in cryptocurrency wallets. The company has temporarily halted withdrawals while it conducts security checks and works to prevent further unauthorised transactions. Binance indicated that it expects the suspension to last no longer than 48 hours, although the resumption of withdrawals remains dependent on the completion of its security procedures. Binance said it had coordinated with industry partners to freeze approximately $3 billion of the assets affected by the attack. The exchange also committed to reimbursing all losses from its own financial resources. Circle, the company behind the USDC stablecoin, confirmed that it had frozen more than 800 million USDC linked to the breach. Tether separately reported freezing more than 1.567 billion USDT associated with the attack. The measures were intended to prevent the movement of stolen funds and limit the financial consequences of the incident. Binance co-founder and former Chief Executive Changpeng Zhao also commented on the situation. "It does look like a hack on Binance," Zhao said in a social media post. The company's commitment to cover losses and restore withdrawals will remain an important factor in determining how quickly confidence returns among its users. According to its data, the stolen assets included approximately $1.66 billion in Tether's USDT stablecoin. The attacker also withdrew 17,985 Bitcoin, valued at approximately $1.45 billion at the time. A further $767 million in USDC was transferred from the exchange. The figures illustrate the scale and diversity of the digital assets involved in the incident. Glassnode also reported that Binance's holdings of its native BNB token were "left untouched." The absence of a reported reduction in BNB holdings contrasted with the substantial losses involving Bitcoin, stablecoins and other cryptocurrencies. Cryptocurrency prices declined following the disclosure of the security breach, extending losses recorded earlier in the week. Bitcoin, the world's largest cryptocurrency by market capitalisation, fell 2.5% to $78,106.60. During the initial market reaction, the token dropped as low as $76,518 before recovering part of its losses. The selloff reflected concerns about exchange security, the potential impact on market liquidity and uncertainty surrounding the recovery of stolen assets. The temporary suspension of withdrawals also added to investor caution as Binance worked to complete its security review. The market reaction extended beyond cryptocurrencies to publicly traded companies with significant exposure to digital assets. The latest security incident introduced additional uncertainty for businesses whose performance is closely linked to the adoption and trading of digital assets. The immediate focus for cryptocurrency markets will be Binance's progress in completing its security checks and restoring withdrawal services. The exchange has indicated that withdrawals should resume within 48 hours and that it intends to absorb the financial losses associated with the incident.

sources.title: Binance pauses withdrawals as hackers suspected of stealing billions in crypto
passages: Crypto watchers say at least $2 billion has been drained from Binance’s hot wallets, which are internet-connected cryptocurrency wallets that store crypto that are connected to the internet.
By some estimates, Binance may have lost upward of $5.7 billion in crypto , though the numbers have not been confirmed and it’s possible that the theft is ongoing.
Binance spokesperson Ross O’Leary said that Binance has “temporarily suspended withdrawals on multiple networks following a security incident as a precautionary measure.”
“Rest assured that user funds are completely safe,” Binance said in a statement.

“Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information,” the statement added. “Users should remain cautious of scams and should not trust unofficial links, messages, or requests for account information.”
Zhao, who no longer runs the company but is its largest shareholder, said that he expects users’ funds to be “fully covered” but did not provide an explanation for the claim.
If confirmed into the billions, this would likely rank as one of the largest crypto breaches in history, according to leaderboards tracking crypto thefts.

Zhao, who no longer runs the company but is its largest shareholder, said that he expects users’ funds to be “fully covered” but did not provide an explanation for the claim. Financial tech giant Circle froze about $800 million in Tether as it passed through its networks, while crypto giant Tether froze about $1.56 billion related to Binance’s hack. By some estimates, Binance may have lost upward of $5.7 billion in crypto , though the numbers have not been confirmed and it’s possible that the theft is ongoing. In 2025, hackers stole a record $1.4 billion in crypto in a single breach from exchange Bybit, blamed on North Korean hackers. In what appears to be a separate incident earlier on Thursday, prediction market giant Polymarket briefly halted trading after it confirmed that a third-party company was compromised, which led to the company pausing withdrawals. sources.title: Binance targeted in $6.3 billion crypto heist, the largest ever
passages: The digital currency exchange Binance says it was the target of a $6.3 billion crypto heist Thursday, believed to be the largest ever recorded.
The previous record for a crypto heist was $1.5 billion that hackers from North Korea stole from Bybit in February 2025.
Binance is the world’s largest cryptocurrency trading platform by volume, with hundreds of thousands of users who buy, sell and store billions of dollars’ worth of digital currencies on the exchange.

The hack originated from a compromised laptop, it said, which allowed “an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions.” “The estimated total impact sits at around $6.3B,” Binance said late Thursday on X.
About $3 billion of crypto assets that transited through wallets connected to the hackers have so far been identified and frozen, the company said.

Binance’s founder, Changpeng Zhao, said, “As a shareholder, I expect all user funds will be fully covered.” Zhao stepped down as the CEO of Binance in 2023 and pleaded guilty to breaking U.S. anti-money-laundering laws.

Unlike traditional bank deposits, funds kept in accounts with companies like Binance are not automatically insured against losses, potentially leaving any refunds up to the discretion of individual exchanges.
Binance cautioned that the full value of assets affected by the hack, as well as assets recovered or frozen, could change.

The massive breach of Binance occurs at a moment when cybersecurity defenses around the world are on high alert about the possibility of novel attacks facilitated by recent advances in artificial intelligence.

The company has suspended all deposits and withdrawals while it works with law enforcement to secure its infrastructure and locate stolen funds. The hack originated from a compromised laptop, it said, which allowed “an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions.” “The estimated total impact sits at around $6.3B,” Binance said late Thursday on X. About $3 billion of crypto assets that transited through wallets connected to the hackers have so far been identified and frozen, the company said. Binance will “cover all losses” from the hack, it said, adding, “User funds are safe.” “We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice,” it said. Binance is the world’s largest cryptocurrency trading platform by volume, with hundreds of thousands of users who buy, sell and store billions of dollars’ worth of digital currencies on the exchange. Unlike traditional bank deposits, funds kept in accounts with companies like Binance are not automatically insured against losses, potentially leaving any refunds up to the discretion of individual exchanges. The previous record for a crypto heist was $1.5 billion that hackers from North Korea stole from Bybit in February 2025. Binance cautioned that the full value of assets affected by the hack, as well as assets recovered or frozen, could change. “This figure may continue to increase as our teams work closely with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets,” it said. Bitcoin was down about 4.3%, while Ethereum lost 4.6% of its value. Two major stablecoin issuers, Tether and Circle, said they had identified billions of dollars in assets connected to the hackers and had frozen them. Tether froze more than $1.567 billion worth of its digital currency, CEO Paolo Ardoino said on X. Jeremy Allaire, CEO of stablecoin issuer Circle, said the company had also frozen hundreds of millions of dollars of assets and was coordinating with law enforcement. The massive breach of Binance occurs at a moment when cybersecurity defenses around the world are on high alert about the possibility of novel attacks facilitated by recent advances in artificial intelligence. Digital currency has been a primary target of hackers for years. In 2025, Coinbase disclosed that thieves had stolen customers’ personal information and tried to extort the company for $20 million. Binance’s founder, Changpeng Zhao, said, “As a shareholder, I expect all user funds will be fully covered.” Zhao stepped down as the CEO of Binance in 2023 and pleaded guilty to breaking U.S. anti-money-laundering laws.

coreStoryFacts.text: Cryptocurrency giant Binance said on Thursday that $6.3bn (£4.7bn) of digital assets have been impacted by what is thought to be the biggest crypto hack on record.
The lab's global head of policy Ari Redbord told the BBC the Binance hack is a "watershed moment" that is unlike anything the industry has seen.
Check Point's chief information security officer Jayant Dave said the losses estimated by Binance made it "the largest crypto theft on record".
Two other major crypto platforms, Tether and Circle, said they had frozen a total of about $2.4bn of assets in response to the potential Binance hack.

Binance did not directly respond to BBC questions about the incident's potential links to North Korea but said: "We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice."
Several crypto industry observers had flagged concerns about a potential hack on Binance hours before the exchange confirmed the security issue.
AI-powered investigations company TRM Labs said in a report that several elements of the Binance attack resemble earlier North Korean-linked incidents, including the Bybit hack.
Binance, which was founded in China in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide.
Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said the company's initial investigation suggested the hack started with a compromised engineer's laptop.
Chainalysis, a crypto analytics firm, also said it has "high confidence" that the North Korean group are linked to the hack.
Crypto exchange Coinbase said it was unaffected by the incident and was monitoring the situation.
In a series of posts, Yi He, Binance's co-chief executive, thanked various cryptocurrency issuers for freezing the assets.
The world's biggest crypto exchange said about half of those assets had been frozen but that many remained in the hands of the hackers, adding that it will "cover all losses".

Binance temporarily suspended withdrawals after reporting a security breach involving approximately $6.3 billion in stolen digital assets, triggering losses across cryptocurrency markets and shares of companies exposed to the sector.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
Bitcoin fell sharply following the announcement, while Ether, Binance's BNB token and several cryptocurrency-related stocks also recorded significant declines.
The attacker also withdrew 17,985 Bitcoin, valued at approximately $1.45 billion at the time.
Bitcoin, the world's largest cryptocurrency by market capitalisation, fell 2.5% to $78,106.60.
Binance said it had coordinated with industry partners to freeze approximately $3 billion of the assets affected by the attack.
The absence of a reported reduction in BNB holdings contrasted with the substantial losses involving Bitcoin, stablecoins and other cryptocurrencies.
The immediate focus for cryptocurrency markets will be Binance's progress in completing its security checks and restoring withdrawal services.
Binance indicated that it expects the suspension to last no longer than 48 hours, although the resumption of withdrawals remains dependent on the completion of its security procedures.
"It does look like a hack on Binance," Zhao said in a social media post.
Binance said its investigation had found no evidence that private keys associated with cryptocurrency wallets had been exposed.

The company said while initial checks suggested an engineer's laptop had been compromised, allowing an attacker to make unauthorised withdrawals, "our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach". Two analytics firms have attributed the incident, which eclipses a record-setting $1.5bn hack on the Bybit exchange in 2025, to a North Korean hacking unit called TraderTraitor. Cyber-security firm Check Point said the unit is also known in the industry as Lazarus Group, which has been blamed for the 2025 hack. Check Point's chief information security officer Jayant Dave said the losses estimated by Binance made it "the largest crypto theft on record". AI-powered investigations company TRM Labs said in a report that several elements of the Binance attack resemble earlier North Korean-linked incidents, including the Bybit hack. The lab's global head of policy Ari Redbord told the BBC the Binance hack is a "watershed moment" that is unlike anything the industry has seen. The attacker still holds an enormous sum of stolen assets, meaning efforts to trace and recover the funds are far from over, Redbord added. Binance, which was founded in China in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide. The company said in 2024 that it has more than $160bn in assets under its custody. The exchange has been subject of regulatory scrutiny around the world. Chainalysis, a crypto analytics firm, also said it has "high confidence" that the North Korean group are linked to the hack. For the last few years North Korea-linked operatives have focussed on attacking cryptocurrency companies for large thefts of digital tokens. The regime has denied any involvement in hacks in the past. Eric Jardine, Chainalysis' Head of Research, urged every exchange to remain vigilant as the platforms are attractive targets for hackers due to the sheer value of assets. Binance did not directly respond to BBC questions about the incident's potential links to North Korea but said: "We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice." The incident concerns Binance.com - while much smaller crypto platform Binance.US, which provides trading services specifically for American residents - said its platform is not affected by the issue. Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said the company's initial investigation suggested the hack started with a compromised engineer's laptop. "That gave an attacker access to a service container, where they submitted unauthorized withdrawal transactions," he said in a statement. In an update, the company said in a statement on X that another investigation found there had been other breach points: "We are still gathering the facts, and will share more directly as we have them." Check Point's Dave said this attack also resembled a hack on crypto exchange platform Bitget in September in which $388m (£289m) was lost: "This implies that attackers no longer need the vault keys. They target the systems and people with authority to use them." In a series of posts, Yi He, Binance's co-chief executive, thanked various cryptocurrency issuers for freezing the assets. "Safety first: withdrawals are currently disabled until the environment is confirmed to be secure," she said. Two other major crypto platforms, Tether and Circle, said they had frozen a total of about $2.4bn of assets in response to the potential Binance hack. World Liberty Financial, a crypto company linked to US President Donald Trump and his family, said it has worked with its partners to freeze stolen funds. Crypto exchange Coinbase said it was unaffected by the incident and was monitoring the situation. Several crypto industry observers had flagged concerns about a potential hack on Binance hours before the exchange confirmed the security issue. Bitcoin dropped by more than 4% following the alerts. The price of other major cryptocurrencies including Ethereum and Solana also fell sharply. The Binance hack has thrust cryptocurrencies back into headlines - but what are they and how do they work? BBC business reporter Archana Shukla explains more about what is suspected to be the largest hack in history. sources.title: Binance targeted in $6.3 billion crypto heist, the largest ever
passages: The digital currency exchange Binance says it was the target of a $6.3 billion crypto heist Thursday, believed to be the largest ever recorded.
The previous record for a crypto heist was $1.5 billion that hackers from North Korea stole from Bybit in February 2025.
Binance is the world’s largest cryptocurrency trading platform by volume, with hundreds of thousands of users who buy, sell and store billions of dollars’ worth of digital currencies on the exchange.

The hack originated from a compromised laptop, it said, which allowed “an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions.” “The estimated total impact sits at around $6.3B,” Binance said late Thursday on X.
About $3 billion of crypto assets that transited through wallets connected to the hackers have so far been identified and frozen, the company said.

Binance’s founder, Changpeng Zhao, said, “As a shareholder, I expect all user funds will be fully covered.” Zhao stepped down as the CEO of Binance in 2023 and pleaded guilty to breaking U.S. anti-money-laundering laws.

Unlike traditional bank deposits, funds kept in accounts with companies like Binance are not automatically insured against losses, potentially leaving any refunds up to the discretion of individual exchanges.
Binance cautioned that the full value of assets affected by the hack, as well as assets recovered or frozen, could change.

The massive breach of Binance occurs at a moment when cybersecurity defenses around the world are on high alert about the possibility of novel attacks facilitated by recent advances in artificial intelligence.

extraction.body: The digital currency exchange Binance says it was the target of a $6.3 billion crypto heist Thursday, believed to be the largest ever recorded. The company has suspended all deposits and withdrawals while it works with law enforcement to secure its infrastructure and locate stolen funds. The hack originated from a compromised laptop, it said, which allowed “an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions.” “The estimated total impact sits at around $6.3B,” Binance said late Thursday on X. About $3 billion of crypto assets that transited through wallets connected to the hackers have so far been identified and frozen, the company said. Binance will “cover all losses” from the hack, it said, adding, “User funds are safe.” “We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice,” it said. Binance is the world’s largest cryptocurrency trading platform by volume, with hundreds of thousands of users who buy, sell and store billions of dollars’ worth of digital currencies on the exchange. Unlike traditional bank deposits, funds kept in accounts with companies like Binance are not automatically insured against losses, potentially leaving any refunds up to the discretion of individual exchanges. The previous record for a crypto heist was $1.5 billion that hackers from North Korea stole from Bybit in February 2025. Binance cautioned that the full value of assets affected by the hack, as well as assets recovered or frozen, could change. “This figure may continue to increase as our teams work closely with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets,” it said. Bitcoin was down about 4.3%, while Ethereum lost 4.6% of its value. Two major stablecoin issuers, Tether and Circle, said they had identified billions of dollars in assets connected to the hackers and had frozen them. Tether froze more than $1.567 billion worth of its digital currency, CEO Paolo Ardoino said on X. The massive breach of Binance occurs at a moment when cybersecurity defenses around the world are on high alert about the possibility of novel attacks facilitated by recent advances in artificial intelligence. Digital currency has been a primary target of hackers for years. In 2025, Coinbase disclosed that thieves had stolen customers’ personal information and tried to extort the company for $20 million. Binance’s founder, Changpeng Zhao, said, “As a shareholder, I expect all user funds will be fully covered.” Zhao stepped down as the CEO of Binance in 2023 and pleaded guilty to breaking U.S. anti-money-laundering laws.

extraction.body: The crypto world is reeling after a hacker drained billions of dollars from Binance, the world's largest digital currency exchange, on Thursday. The full details of the hack are still emerging, but the broad strokes of what happened are becoming clearer, as everyone from security researchers to Elon Musk to the company itself weighs in with theories. Binance posted on X late Thursday evening Eastern Time stating that a compromised developer laptop is likely to blame for the catastrophe, which is by far the biggest security incident in an industry that has been plagued by hacking since its earliest days. The company plans to provide more extensive details on Friday and, in the meantime, many other big crypto firms—including its biggest rivals—have rushed to aid Binance. Here is a detailed look at what we know so far about the nature and scope of the hack, and what is likely to happen next. Reports of a hack began surfacing on X early on Thursday afternoon. That's when crypto observers, referring to public blockchain data, pointed to large amounts of currency moving out of wallets associated with Binance. Soon after, company founder Changpeng Zhao confirmed the hack. In its post on Thursday evening, Binance stated the hacker appeared to have gained control of a laptop belonging to an employee or a contractor. The company wrote that the "initial investigation suggests that the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions." Reports on X have suggested the hacker made off with anywhere from $2 billion to $8 billion, but in its post, Binance said the estimated total impact sits at around $6.3 billion. The situation is still fluid and it could be days before the scope of the hack is finally determined. Early reports say the hacker took $1.5 billion in Bitcoin and around the same amount in the stablecoin Tether, and slightly under a billion dollars worth of Ethereum and the USDC stablecoin. It is likely the hacker stole various other currencies too. No one has claimed responsibility for the hack and Binance has not pointed to a specific culprit, but the security firm TRM and others have said North Korea is almost certainly behind it. This theory is highly plausible given that the North Korean military has long used crypto hacking to help fund its operations. The sophisticated nature of the hack, which included efforts to move the funds after they were stolen, is also consistent with the tactics of North Korea. For now, though, there is no definitive proof the country is responsible. Soon after news of the hack became public, Tether and Circle—the firms responsible for minting USDT and USDC—announced they would freeze any stablecoins tied to the hack. While this is ostensibly good news, other reports indicate these efforts may only be partially successful at best. That's because there is evidence the hacker immediately took the stolen funds to the online crypto lending platform Aave, and posted them as collateral for a loan in Ethereum. This means the hacker is now in a position to walk off with the borrowed Ethereum. Unsurprisingly, the price of all major cryptocurrencies fell upon news of the hack, though the drop was not dramatic. Bitcoin and Ethereum are down around 3% as of early Friday, but that drop also coincided with a sell-off in the broader financial markets. The relatively muted reaction suggests the market is confident that Binance has deep enough pockets to absorb the loss while also keeping its customers whole. In the immediate wake of the hack, the CEOs of Coinbase, Tether and other big crypto companies all pledged to support Binance in its hour of need. In response, Binance's founder noted that "many industry friends and even competitors (including some previously-not-so-friendly ones) provided very much needed help." Zhao also expressed thanks to Yi He, the company's current CEO, for pulling an all-nighter while she is pregnant. Meanwhile, some on X expressed incredulity that Binance's security could be so flawed as to allow a hacker to steal billions simply by gaining access to a single company laptop. As for Elon Musk, he chimed in with an AI-focused take, saying "Super intelligence agents will at some point do this to gain currency for themselves, not a human." This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

passages: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, is investigating a cyberattack after billions of dollars in cryptocurrency were transferred from its wallets on Thursday, 29 October 2026.Initial reports estimated that $5.5 billion had been moved, while stablecoin issuers froze around $1.8 billion.

The blockchain intelligence firm estimated that around $2.7 billion in affected assets had subsequently been frozen.Binance acknowledged the security incident and temporarily halted trading, deposits and withdrawals.

Co-founder Yi He assured customers that their funds were safe and pledged to cover hacking losses, according to Axios.How Did Attackers Move More Than $6 Billion From Binance?The attack targeted Binance's hot wallets, which are internet-connected cryptocurrency wallets used to process transactions and customer withdrawals.TRM Labs reported that most suspicious transfers occurred within approximately 20 minutes, beginning at 20:05 UTC on 29 October.

Blockchain investigators have since raised the estimated theft to $6.36 billion, potentially making it the largest cryptocurrency heist in history.According to TRM Labs, approximately $6.36 billion left Binance wallets across ten blockchain networks.

TRM estimated that the attacker still controlled more than 420,000 Ether (ETH) and 18,270 Bitcoin (BTC), worth approximately $2.4 billion at the time of its assessment.North Korean Hackers Suspected as Investigators Trace the MoneyTRM Labs has attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, a North Korea-linked hacking operation previously associated with major cryptocurrency thefts.The firm's high-confidence assessment draws on blockchain transactions and other intelligence.

Broader market conditions make it difficult to determine how much of either decline resulted directly from the attack.Customers should monitor Binance's official security updates and avoid suspicious links or unverified recovery offers.Investigators must now establish how the attackers gained access, how much cryptocurrency can ultimately be recovered and whether Binance can demonstrate that its remaining assets are secure.

Separately, Axios reported that Binance's preliminary investigation linked the intrusion to a compromised engineer's laptop.The full sequence of events and the precise extent of the compromise remain under investigation.Billions Frozen as Tether and Circle Race to Stop TransfersThe first warnings emerged on Thursday when blockchain observers identified unusually large transfers from Binance-linked wallets.According to Decrypt, early estimates placed suspicious transfers at approximately $5.57 billion across Ethereum, Bitcoin and Tron. Tether initially froze around $975 million in USDT, while Circle blocked approximately $823 million in USDC.Those restrictions totalled roughly $1.8 billion. Further freezes followed as investigators traced assets across additional networks.TRM subsequently reported that Tether, Circle, Ripple and World Liberty Financial had frozen approximately $2.67 billion in stablecoins.Arbitrum's Security Council also restricted assets worth around $30 million, bringing the total to approximately $2.7 billion as of 00:30 UTC on 30 October. Later reports indicated that roughly $3 billion had been frozen.However, frozen cryptocurrency is not necessarily recovered cryptocurrency. Restrictions can prevent affected tokens from moving, but returning those assets remains a separate process. TRM estimated that the attacker still controlled more than 420,000 Ether (ETH) and 18,270 Bitcoin (BTC), worth approximately $2.4 billion at the time of its assessment.North Korean Hackers Suspected as Investigators Trace the MoneyTRM Labs has attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, a North Korea-linked hacking operation previously associated with major cryptocurrency thefts.The firm's high-confidence assessment draws on blockchain transactions and other intelligence. Investigators identified signs of advance preparation, suspicious wallet activity and transaction patterns resembling earlier attacks.However, responsibility for this incident has not been independently established through a publicly disclosed law enforcement finding. North Korean representatives have previously denied allegations involving cryptocurrency exchange hacks.The estimated theft would substantially exceed the approximately $1.5 billion stolen from cryptocurrency exchange Bybit in February 2025. If TRM's figures are confirmed, the Binance attack would be more than four times larger than that previous record.Are Binance Customers' Funds Safe?For Binance customers, the immediate concerns are whether their holdings remain protected and when normal services will resume.Binance initially said it had not confirmed any impact on customer funds. The exchange subsequently acknowledged approximately $6.3 billion in affected assets, according to Axios.Co-founder Yi He assured users that their funds were safe and promised Binance would cover hacking losses. However, that assurance does not independently establish the status of every customer asset or confirm when compensation might be available.The incident coincided with declines across cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin fell below $79,000 as reports emerged, while Binance's BNB token also dropped. Broader market conditions make it difficult to determine how much of either decline resulted directly from the attack.Customers should monitor Binance's official security updates and avoid suspicious links or unverified recovery offers.Investigators must now establish how the attackers gained access, how much cryptocurrency can ultimately be recovered and whether Binance can demonstrate that its remaining assets are secure.

SINGAPORE, Oct 30 (Reuters) - A security breach at Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, has resulted in an estimated $6.3 billion impact, the biggest crypto heist ever. Binance said it had worked with partners to freeze the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It gave no update on the status of the remaining $3.3 billion, though Binance co-founder Yi He said the company would cover "all hacking losses". The crypto industry has suffered a series of thefts, prompting questions about the security of customer funds and investors to possibly rethink the risks of owning digital assets. Here are some of the other major thefts to have plagued the industry since bitcoin was born in 2008. Time period: February 2025 Company: Cryptocurrency exchange Bybit What was stolen: Digital tokens worth $1.5 billion What happened: The crypto was taken from a "cold wallet" - a digital wallet usually stored offline and so supposedly more secure - that was used for ether tokens. Time period: March 2022 Company: Ronin Network, a network that allows transfer of crypto coins across different blockchains What was stolen: Roughly $540 million from a blockchain project linked to the popular online game Axie Infinity What happened: Hackers stole some 173,600 ether tokens and 25.5 million USD Coin tokens. Time period: February 2022 Company: Wormhole, a DeFi site What was stolen: $320 million What happened: Hackers making off with 120,000 digital tokens connected to the second-largest cryptocurrency, ether. The crypto arm of Chicago-based Jump Trading, which had the year before acquired the developer behind Wormhole, later replaced the funds. Time period: August 2021 Company: Poly Network, a platform that facilitates peer-to-peer token transactions What was stolen: $610 million (Hackers behind the heist later returned nearly all of the stolen funds) What happened: The hack underscored vulnerabilities in the burgeoning decentralised finance, or DeFi, sector, where users lend, borrow and save in digital tokens, bypassing the traditional gatekeepers of finance such as banks and exchanges. Time period: January 2018 Company: Tokyo-based exchange Coincheck What was stolen: $530 million What happened: The thieves attacked one of Coincheck's "hot wallet" - a digital folder stored online - to drain the funds, drawing attention to security at exchanges. South Korea's intelligence agency said at the time that a North Korean hacking group may have been behind the heist. Time period: Between 2011 and 2014 Company: Tokyo-based bitcoin exchange Mt. Gox What was stolen: Bitcoin worth close to $500 million was stolen in one of the earliest and most high-profile crypto hacks. What happened: Mt. Gox, which once handled 80% of the world's bitcoin trade, filed for bankruptcy in early 2014 after the hack was revealed, with some 24,000 customers losing access to their funds. coreStoryFacts.text: Binance posted on X late Thursday evening Eastern Time stating that a compromised developer laptop is likely to blame for the catastrophe, which is by far the biggest security incident in an industry that has been plagued by hacking since its earliest days.
The company plans to provide more extensive details on Friday and, in the meantime, many other big crypto firms—including its biggest rivals—have rushed to aid Binance.
Reports on X have suggested the hacker made off with anywhere from $2 billion to $8 billion, but in its post, Binance said the estimated total impact sits at around $6.3 billion.
The situation is still fluid and it could be days before the scope of the hack is finally determined.
The crypto world is reeling after a hacker drained billions of dollars from Binance, the world's largest digital currency exchange, on Thursday.

In response, Binance's founder noted that "many industry friends and even competitors (including some previously-not-so-friendly ones) provided very much needed help." Zhao also expressed thanks to Yi He, the company's current CEO, for pulling an all-nighter while she is pregnant.

The company wrote that the "initial investigation suggests that the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions."
The relatively muted reaction suggests the market is confident that Binance has deep enough pockets to absorb the loss while also keeping its customers whole.
As for Elon Musk, he chimed in with an AI-focused take, saying "Super intelligence agents will at some point do this to gain currency for themselves, not a human."
This theory is highly plausible given that the North Korean military has long used crypto hacking to help fund its operations.
For now, though, there is no definitive proof the country is responsible.

extraction.body: The crypto world is reeling after a hacker drained billions of dollars from Binance, the world's largest digital currency exchange, on Thursday. The full details of the hack are still emerging, but the broad strokes of what happened are becoming clearer, as everyone from security researchers to Elon Musk to the company itself weighs in with theories. Binance posted on X late Thursday evening Eastern Time stating that a compromised developer laptop is likely to blame for the catastrophe, which is by far the biggest security incident in an industry that has been plagued by hacking since its earliest days. The company plans to provide more extensive details on Friday and, in the meantime, many other big crypto firms—including its biggest rivals—have rushed to aid Binance. Here is a detailed look at what we know so far about the nature and scope of the hack, and what is likely to happen next. Reports of a hack began surfacing on X early on Thursday afternoon. That's when crypto observers, referring to public blockchain data, pointed to large amounts of currency moving out of wallets associated with Binance. Soon after, company founder Changpeng Zhao confirmed the hack. In its post on Thursday evening, Binance stated the hacker appeared to have gained control of a laptop belonging to an employee or a contractor. The company wrote that the "initial investigation suggests that the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions." Reports on X have suggested the hacker made off with anywhere from $2 billion to $8 billion, but in its post, Binance said the estimated total impact sits at around $6.3 billion. The situation is still fluid and it could be days before the scope of the hack is finally determined. Early reports say the hacker took $1.5 billion in Bitcoin and around the same amount in the stablecoin Tether, and slightly under a billion dollars worth of Ethereum and the USDC stablecoin. It is likely the hacker stole various other currencies too. No one has claimed responsibility for the hack and Binance has not pointed to a specific culprit, but the security firm TRM and others have said North Korea is almost certainly behind it. This theory is highly plausible given that the North Korean military has long used crypto hacking to help fund its operations. The sophisticated nature of the hack, which included efforts to move the funds after they were stolen, is also consistent with the tactics of North Korea. For now, though, there is no definitive proof the country is responsible. Soon after news of the hack became public, Tether and Circle—the firms responsible for minting USDT and USDC—announced they would freeze any stablecoins tied to the hack. While this is ostensibly good news, other reports indicate these efforts may only be partially successful at best. That's because there is evidence the hacker immediately took the stolen funds to the online crypto lending platform Aave, and posted them as collateral for a loan in Ethereum. This means the hacker is now in a position to walk off with the borrowed Ethereum. Unsurprisingly, the price of all major cryptocurrencies fell upon news of the hack, though the drop was not dramatic. Bitcoin and Ethereum are down around 3% as of early Friday, but that drop also coincided with a sell-off in the broader financial markets. The relatively muted reaction suggests the market is confident that Binance has deep enough pockets to absorb the loss while also keeping its customers whole. In the immediate wake of the hack, the CEOs of Coinbase, Tether and other big crypto companies all pledged to support Binance in its hour of need. In response, Binance's founder noted that "many industry friends and even competitors (including some previously-not-so-friendly ones) provided very much needed help." Zhao also expressed thanks to Yi He, the company's current CEO, for pulling an all-nighter while she is pregnant. Meanwhile, some on X expressed incredulity that Binance's security could be so flawed as to allow a hacker to steal billions simply by gaining access to a single company laptop. As for Elon Musk, he chimed in with an AI-focused take, saying "Super intelligence agents will at some point do this to gain currency for themselves, not a human." This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

The sophisticated nature of the hack, which included efforts to move the funds after they were stolen, is also consistent with the tactics of North Korea. For now, though, there is no definitive proof the country is responsible.
Soon after news of the hack became public, Tether and Circle—the firms responsible for minting USDT and USDC—announced they would freeze any stablecoins tied to the hack.

While this is ostensibly good news, other reports indicate these efforts may only be partially successful at best. That's because there is evidence the hacker immediately took the stolen funds to the online crypto lending platform Aave, and posted them as collateral for a loan in Ethereum. This means the hacker is now in a position to walk off with the borrowed Ethereum.

Unsurprisingly, the price of all major cryptocurrencies fell upon news of the hack, though the drop was not dramatic. Bitcoin and Ethereum are down around 3% as of early Friday, but that drop also coincided with a sell-off in the broader financial markets.
The relatively muted reaction suggests the market is confident that Binance has deep enough pockets to absorb the loss while also keeping its customers whole.

In the immediate wake of the hack, the CEOs of Coinbase, Tether and other big crypto companies all pledged to support Binance in its hour of need. In response, Binance's founder noted that "many industry friends and even competitors (including some previously-not-so-friendly ones) provided very much needed help." Zhao also expressed thanks to Yi He, the company's current CEO, for pulling an all-nighter while she is pregnant.

Meanwhile, some on X expressed incredulity that Binance's security could be so flawed as to allow a hacker to steal billions simply by gaining access to a single company laptop. As for Elon Musk, he chimed in with an AI-focused take, saying "Super intelligence agents will at some point do this to gain currency for themselves, not a human."
This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

sources.title: Crypto’s Biggest Heist? Binance Faces $5.5 Billion Hack Fears as $1.8 Billion in Assets Frozen
passages: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, is investigating a cyberattack after billions of dollars in cryptocurrency were transferred from its wallets on Thursday, 29 October 2026.Initial reports estimated that $5.5 billion had been moved, while stablecoin issuers froze around $1.8 billion.

The blockchain intelligence firm estimated that around $2.7 billion in affected assets had subsequently been frozen.Binance acknowledged the security incident and temporarily halted trading, deposits and withdrawals.

Co-founder Yi He assured customers that their funds were safe and pledged to cover hacking losses, according to Axios.How Did Attackers Move More Than $6 Billion From Binance?The attack targeted Binance's hot wallets, which are internet-connected cryptocurrency wallets used to process transactions and customer withdrawals.TRM Labs reported that most suspicious transfers occurred within approximately 20 minutes, beginning at 20:05 UTC on 29 October.

Blockchain investigators have since raised the estimated theft to $6.36 billion, potentially making it the largest cryptocurrency heist in history.According to TRM Labs, approximately $6.36 billion left Binance wallets across ten blockchain networks.

TRM estimated that the attacker still controlled more than 420,000 Ether (ETH) and 18,270 Bitcoin (BTC), worth approximately $2.4 billion at the time of its assessment.North Korean Hackers Suspected as Investigators Trace the MoneyTRM Labs has attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, a North Korea-linked hacking operation previously associated with major cryptocurrency thefts.The firm's high-confidence assessment draws on blockchain transactions and other intelligence.

Broader market conditions make it difficult to determine how much of either decline resulted directly from the attack.Customers should monitor Binance's official security updates and avoid suspicious links or unverified recovery offers.Investigators must now establish how the attackers gained access, how much cryptocurrency can ultimately be recovered and whether Binance can demonstrate that its remaining assets are secure.

extraction.body: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, is investigating a cyberattack after billions of dollars in cryptocurrency were transferred from its wallets on Thursday, 29 October 2026.Initial reports estimated that $5.5 billion had been moved, while stablecoin issuers froze around $1.8 billion. Blockchain investigators have since raised the estimated theft to $6.36 billion, potentially making it the largest cryptocurrency heist in history.According to TRM Labs, approximately $6.36 billion left Binance wallets across ten blockchain networks. The blockchain intelligence firm estimated that around $2.7 billion in affected assets had subsequently been frozen.Binance acknowledged the security incident and temporarily halted trading, deposits and withdrawals. Co-founder Yi He assured customers that their funds were safe and pledged to cover hacking losses, according to Axios.How Did Attackers Move More Than $6 Billion From Binance?The attack targeted Binance's hot wallets, which are internet-connected cryptocurrency wallets used to process transactions and customer withdrawals.TRM Labs reported that most suspicious transfers occurred within approximately 20 minutes, beginning at 20:05 UTC on 29 October. The activity affected ten blockchain networks, including Ethereum, Bitcoin and Tron.On Ethereum, investigators identified the use of EIP-7702, a feature that allows wallets to delegate transaction execution to smart-contract code.TRM found that the attacker had prepared 50 signed authorisations. One valid authorisation allowed an attacker-controlled smart contract to execute transactions from a Binance hot wallet.TRM suspects Binance's wallet-signing infrastructure was compromised because suspicious transfers occurred across networks using different signing systems. Separately, Axios reported that Binance's preliminary investigation linked the intrusion to a compromised engineer's laptop.The full sequence of events and the precise extent of the compromise remain under investigation.Billions Frozen as Tether and Circle Race to Stop TransfersThe first warnings emerged on Thursday when blockchain observers identified unusually large transfers from Binance-linked wallets.According to Decrypt, early estimates placed suspicious transfers at approximately $5.57 billion across Ethereum, Bitcoin and Tron. Tether initially froze around $975 million in USDT, while Circle blocked approximately $823 million in USDC.Those restrictions totalled roughly $1.8 billion. Further freezes followed as investigators traced assets across additional networks.TRM subsequently reported that Tether, Circle, Ripple and World Liberty Financial had frozen approximately $2.67 billion in stablecoins.Arbitrum's Security Council also restricted assets worth around $30 million, bringing the total to approximately $2.7 billion as of 00:30 UTC on 30 October. Later reports indicated that roughly $3 billion had been frozen.However, frozen cryptocurrency is not necessarily recovered cryptocurrency. Restrictions can prevent affected tokens from moving, but returning those assets remains a separate process. TRM estimated that the attacker still controlled more than 420,000 Ether (ETH) and 18,270 Bitcoin (BTC), worth approximately $2.4 billion at the time of its assessment.North Korean Hackers Suspected as Investigators Trace the MoneyTRM Labs has attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, a North Korea-linked hacking operation previously associated with major cryptocurrency thefts.The firm's high-confidence assessment draws on blockchain transactions and other intelligence. Investigators identified signs of advance preparation, suspicious wallet activity and transaction patterns resembling earlier attacks.However, responsibility for this incident has not been independently established through a publicly disclosed law enforcement finding. North Korean representatives have previously denied allegations involving cryptocurrency exchange hacks.The estimated theft would substantially exceed the approximately $1.5 billion stolen from cryptocurrency exchange Bybit in February 2025. If TRM's figures are confirmed, the Binance attack would be more than four times larger than that previous record.Are Binance Customers' Funds Safe?For Binance customers, the immediate concerns are whether their holdings remain protected and when normal services will resume.Binance initially said it had not confirmed any impact on customer funds. The exchange subsequently acknowledged approximately $6.3 billion in affected assets, according to Axios.Co-founder Yi He assured users that their funds were safe and promised Binance would cover hacking losses. However, that assurance does not independently establish the status of every customer asset or confirm when compensation might be available.The incident coincided with declines across cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin fell below $79,000 as reports emerged, while Binance's BNB token also dropped. Broader market conditions make it difficult to determine how much of either decline resulted directly from the attack.Customers should monitor Binance's official security updates and avoid suspicious links or unverified recovery offers.Investigators must now establish how the attackers gained access, how much cryptocurrency can ultimately be recovered and whether Binance can demonstrate that its remaining assets are secure.

SINGAPORE, Oct 30 (Reuters) - A security breach at Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, has resulted in an estimated $6.3 billion impact, the biggest crypto heist ever. Binance said it had worked with partners to freeze the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It gave no update on the status of the remaining $3.3 billion, though Binance co-founder Yi He said the company would cover "all hacking losses". The crypto industry has suffered a series of thefts, prompting questions about the security of customer funds and investors to possibly rethink the risks of owning digital assets. Here are some of the other major thefts to have plagued the industry since bitcoin was born in 2008. Time period: February 2025 Company: Cryptocurrency exchange Bybit What was stolen: Digital tokens worth $1.5 billion What happened: The crypto was taken from a "cold wallet" - a digital wallet usually stored offline and so supposedly more secure - that was used for ether tokens. Time period: March 2022 Company: Ronin Network, a network that allows transfer of crypto coins across different blockchains What was stolen: Roughly $540 million from a blockchain project linked to the popular online game Axie Infinity What happened: Hackers stole some 173,600 ether tokens and 25.5 million USD Coin tokens. Time period: February 2022 Company: Wormhole, a DeFi site What was stolen: $320 million What happened: Hackers making off with 120,000 digital tokens connected to the second-largest cryptocurrency, ether. The crypto arm of Chicago-based Jump Trading, which had the year before acquired the developer behind Wormhole, later replaced the funds. Time period: August 2021 Company: Poly Network, a platform that facilitates peer-to-peer token transactions What was stolen: $610 million (Hackers behind the heist later returned nearly all of the stolen funds) What happened: The hack underscored vulnerabilities in the burgeoning decentralised finance, or DeFi, sector, where users lend, borrow and save in digital tokens, bypassing the traditional gatekeepers of finance such as banks and exchanges. Time period: January 2018 Company: Tokyo-based exchange Coincheck What was stolen: $530 million What happened: The thieves attacked one of Coincheck's "hot wallet" - a digital folder stored online - to drain the funds, drawing attention to security at exchanges. South Korea's intelligence agency said at the time that a North Korean hacking group may have been behind the heist. Time period: Between 2011 and 2014 Company: Tokyo-based bitcoin exchange Mt. Gox What was stolen: Bitcoin worth close to $500 million was stolen in one of the earliest and most high-profile crypto hacks. What happened: Mt. Gox, which once handled 80% of the world's bitcoin trade, filed for bankruptcy in early 2014 after the hack was revealed, with some 24,000 customers losing access to their funds. Binance’s estimated $6.3 billion breach is by far the largest crypto theft on record, dwarfing the previous record of $1.4–1.5 billion at Bybit in February 2025. Asset recovery efforts have frozen around half the funds, with Binance pledging to cover all losses.
SINGAPORE, Oct 30 (Reuters) - A security breach at Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, has resulted in an estimated $6.3 billion impact, the biggest crypto heist ever.

Binance said it had worked with partners to freeze the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It gave no update on the status of the remaining $3.3 billion, though Binance co-founder Yi He said the company would cover "all hacking losses".
The crypto industry has suffered a series of thefts, prompting questions about the security of customer funds and investors to possibly rethink the risks of owning digital assets.
Here are some of the other major thefts to have plagued the industry since bitcoin was born in 2008.

Time period: February 2025 Company: Cryptocurrency exchange Bybit What was stolen: Digital tokens worth $1.5 billion What happened: The crypto was taken from a "cold wallet" - a digital wallet usually stored offline and so supposedly more secure - that was used for ether tokens.

Time period: March 2022 Company: Ronin Network, a network that allows transfer of crypto coins across different blockchains What was stolen: Roughly $540 million from a blockchain project linked to the popular online game Axie Infinity What happened: Hackers stole some 173,600 ether tokens and 25.5 million USD Coin tokens.

Time period: February 2022 Company: Wormhole, a DeFi site What was stolen: $320 million What happened: Hackers making off with 120,000 digital tokens connected to the second-largest cryptocurrency, ether. The crypto arm of Chicago-based Jump Trading, which had the year before acquired the developer behind Wormhole, later replaced the funds.

Time period: August 2021 Company: Poly Network, a platform that facilitates peer-to-peer token transactions What was stolen: $610 million (Hackers behind the heist later returned nearly all of the stolen funds) What happened: The hack underscored vulnerabilities in the burgeoning decentralised finance, or DeFi, sector, where users lend, borrow and save in digital tokens, bypassing the traditional gatekeepers of finance such as banks and exchanges.

Time period: January 2018 Company: Tokyo-based exchange Coincheck What was stolen: $530 million What happened: The thieves attacked one of Coincheck's "hot wallet" - a digital folder stored online - to drain the funds, drawing attention to security at exchanges.
South Korea's intelligence agency said at the time that a North Korean hacking group may have been behind the heist.

Time period: Between 2011 and 2014 Company: Tokyo-based bitcoin exchange Mt. Gox What was stolen: Bitcoin worth close to $500 million was stolen in one of the earliest and most high-profile crypto hacks. What happened: Mt. Gox, which once handled 80% of the world's bitcoin trade, filed for bankruptcy in early 2014 after the hack was revealed, with some 24,000 customers losing access to their funds.
(Reporting by Ankur Banerjee in Singapore and Tommy Reggiori Wilkes, Tom Wilson and Elizabeth Howcroft in London; Editing by Jamie Freed)

passages: LOS ANGELES (AP) — Binance , the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, said Thursday it's investigating reports of a potential security issue as its founder said the incident "does look like a hack on Binance." The company said late Thursday the estimated total impact was at more than $6 billion, which could be one of the most significant of such security incidents on record.
It wasn't immediately clear the extent of the damage hackers might have been able to cause, and Binance had not explicitly confirmed that funds had been pilfered.

"Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information," the statement continued.

"Binance's initial investigation suggests that the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions," the company wrote.
Binance also said all deposits and withdrawals are temporarily suspended while it conducts security checks, freezes funds and works with law enforcement.
Binance was founded in 2017 by Changpeng Zhao, who in 2023 pleaded guilty to a felony related to his failure to prevent money laundering on the platform and stepped down as CEO.
Zhao was released from prison last year after being sentenced for violating the Bank Secrecy Act .

He was the first person ever sentenced to prison time for violations of that law, which requires U.S. financial institutions to know who their customers are, to monitor transactions and to file reports of suspicious activity.
Prosecutors said no one had ever violated the regulations to the extent Zhao did.
"Rest assured that user funds are completely safe," a Binance spokesperson said in a statement.
Binance said it will share more technical details once the investigation is complete and when the facts are "fully verified."

U.S.-based blockchain intelligence firm TRM said a North Korea hacking unit was likely behind the theft of more than $6 billion on the world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange, Binance . Binance said late on Thursday that approximately $6.3 billion was impacted, which its founder described as “like a hack.” The company said it worked with blockchain partners to freeze affected assets, and roughly $3 billion was frozen. The cryptocurrency exchange added that it had temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while security checks are completed. TRM, in a post on its website Thursday, attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, which it described as North Korea’s elite hacking unit. “We make this judgment with high confidence,” the firm said. “An attacker moved approximately USD 6.36 billion out of Binance wallets on ten blockchains, most of it in about 20 minutes,” TRM said. That would make the hack the largest cryptocurrency theft on record, it said. In February last year, another cryptocurrency exchange Bybit suffered a $1.5 billion hit when it was hacked. The FBI said North Korea and TraderTraitor were responsible for the hack. “Several features of this attack match earlier North Korea-linked heists, including the Bybit hack,” TRM said. coreStoryFacts.text: LOS ANGELES (AP) — Binance , the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, said Thursday it's investigating reports of a potential security issue as its founder said the incident "does look like a hack on Binance." The company said late Thursday the estimated total impact was at more than $6 billion, which could be one of the most significant of such security incidents on record.
It wasn't immediately clear the extent of the damage hackers might have been able to cause, and Binance had not explicitly confirmed that funds had been pilfered.

"Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information," the statement continued.

"Binance's initial investigation suggests that the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions," the company wrote.
Binance also said all deposits and withdrawals are temporarily suspended while it conducts security checks, freezes funds and works with law enforcement.
Binance was founded in 2017 by Changpeng Zhao, who in 2023 pleaded guilty to a felony related to his failure to prevent money laundering on the platform and stepped down as CEO.
Zhao was released from prison last year after being sentenced for violating the Bank Secrecy Act .

He was the first person ever sentenced to prison time for violations of that law, which requires U.S. financial institutions to know who their customers are, to monitor transactions and to file reports of suspicious activity.
Prosecutors said no one had ever violated the regulations to the extent Zhao did.
"Rest assured that user funds are completely safe," a Binance spokesperson said in a statement.
Binance said it will share more technical details once the investigation is complete and when the facts are "fully verified."

The lab's global head of policy Ari Redbord told the BBC the Binance hack is a "watershed moment" that is unlike anything the industry has seen.

extraction.body: Cryptocurrency giant Binance said on Thursday that $6.3bn (£4.7bn) of digital assets have been impacted by what is thought to be the biggest crypto hack on record. The world's biggest crypto exchange said about half of those assets had been frozen but that many remained in the hands of the hackers, adding that it will "cover all losses". The company said while initial checks suggested an engineer's laptop had been compromised, allowing an attacker to make unauthorised withdrawals, "our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach". Two analytics firms have attributed the incident, which eclipses a record-setting $1.5bn hack on the Bybit exchange in 2025, to a North Korean hacking unit called TraderTraitor. Cyber-security firm Check Point said the unit is also known in the industry as Lazarus Group, which has been blamed for the 2025 hack. Check Point's chief information security officer Jayant Dave said the losses estimated by Binance made it "the largest crypto theft on record". AI-powered investigations company TRM Labs said in a report that several elements of the Binance attack resemble earlier North Korean-linked incidents, including the Bybit hack. The lab's global head of policy Ari Redbord told the BBC the Binance hack is a "watershed moment" that is unlike anything the industry has seen. The attacker still holds an enormous sum of stolen assets, meaning efforts to trace and recover the funds are far from over, Redbord added. Binance, which was founded in China in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide. The company said in 2024 that it has more than $160bn in assets under its custody. The exchange has been subject of regulatory scrutiny around the world. Chainalysis, a crypto analytics firm, also said it has "high confidence" that the North Korean group are linked to the hack. For the last few years North Korea-linked operatives have focussed on attacking cryptocurrency companies for large thefts of digital tokens. Eric Jardine, Chainalysis' Head of Research, urged every exchange to remain vigilant as the platforms are attractive targets for hackers due to the sheer value of assets. Binance did not directly respond to BBC questions about the incident's potential links to North Korea but said: "We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice." The incident concerns Binance.com - while much smaller crypto platform Binance.US, which provides trading services specifically for American residents - said its platform is not affected by the issue. Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said the company's initial investigation suggested the hack started with a compromised engineer's laptop. "That gave an attacker access to a service container, where they submitted unauthorized withdrawal transactions," he said in a statement. "To be clear: the attacker did not simply use one engineer's permissions, and this was not a single 'one-click' action. It involved a more complex attack process. Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual. So far, we have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak." He said a detailed "post-mortem" would be shared once the investigation was complete. In an update, the company said in a statement on X that another investigation found there had been other breach points: "We are still gathering the facts, and will share more directly as we have them." Check Point's Dave said this attack also resembled a hack on crypto exchange platform Bitget in September in which $388m (£289m) was lost: "This implies that attackers no longer need the vault keys. They target the systems and people with authority to use them." In a series of posts, Yi He, Binance's co-chief executive, thanked various cryptocurrency issuers for freezing the assets. "Safety first: withdrawals are currently disabled until the environment is confirmed to be secure," she said. Two other major crypto platforms, Tether and Circle, said they had frozen a total of about $2.4bn of assets in response to the potential Binance hack. World Liberty Financial, a crypto company linked to US President Donald Trump and his family, said it has worked with its partners to freeze stolen funds. Crypto exchange Coinbase said it was unaffected by the incident and was monitoring the situation. Several crypto industry observers had flagged concerns about a potential hack on Binance hours before the exchange confirmed the security issue. Bitcoin dropped by more than 4% following the alerts. The price of other major cryptocurrencies including Ethereum and Solana also fell sharply.
