extraction.body: Cryptocurrency giant Binance said on Thursday that $6.3bn (£4.7bn) of digital assets have been impacted by what is thought to be the biggest crypto hack on record. The world's biggest crypto exchange said about half of those assets had been frozen but that many remained in the hands of the hackers, adding that it will "cover all losses". The company said while initial checks suggested an engineer's laptop had been compromised, allowing an attacker to make unauthorised withdrawals, "our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach". Two analytics firms have attributed the incident, which eclipses a record-setting $1.5bn hack on the Bybit exchange in 2025, to a North Korean hacking unit called TraderTraitor. Cyber-security firm Check Point said the unit is also known in the industry as Lazarus Group, which has been blamed for the 2025 hack. Check Point's chief information security officer Jayant Dave said the losses estimated by Binance made it "the largest crypto theft on record". AI-powered investigations company TRM Labs said in a report that several elements of the Binance attack resemble earlier North Korean-linked incidents, including the Bybit hack. The lab's global head of policy Ari Redbord told the BBC the Binance hack is a "watershed moment" that is unlike anything the industry has seen. The attacker still holds an enormous sum of stolen assets, meaning efforts to trace and recover the funds are far from over, Redbord added. Binance, which was founded in China in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide. The company said in 2024 that it has more than $160bn in assets under its custody. The exchange has been subject of regulatory scrutiny around the world. Chainalysis, a crypto analytics firm, also said it has "high confidence" that the North Korean group are linked to the hack. For the last few years North Korea-linked operatives have focussed on attacking cryptocurrency companies for large thefts of digital tokens. Eric Jardine, Chainalysis' Head of Research, urged every exchange to remain vigilant as the platforms are attractive targets for hackers due to the sheer value of assets. Binance did not directly respond to BBC questions about the incident's potential links to North Korea but said: "We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice." The incident concerns Binance.com - while much smaller crypto platform Binance.US, which provides trading services specifically for American residents - said its platform is not affected by the issue. Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said the company's initial investigation suggested the hack started with a compromised engineer's laptop. "That gave an attacker access to a service container, where they submitted unauthorized withdrawal transactions," he said in a statement. "To be clear: the attacker did not simply use one engineer's permissions, and this was not a single 'one-click' action. It involved a more complex attack process. Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual. So far, we have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak." He said a detailed "post-mortem" would be shared once the investigation was complete. In an update, the company said in a statement on X that another investigation found there had been other breach points: "We are still gathering the facts, and will share more directly as we have them." Check Point's Dave said this attack also resembled a hack on crypto exchange platform Bitget in September in which $388m (£289m) was lost: "This implies that attackers no longer need the vault keys. They target the systems and people with authority to use them." In a series of posts, Yi He, Binance's co-chief executive, thanked various cryptocurrency issuers for freezing the assets. "Safety first: withdrawals are currently disabled until the environment is confirmed to be secure," she said. Two other major crypto platforms, Tether and Circle, said they had frozen a total of about $2.4bn of assets in response to the potential Binance hack. World Liberty Financial, a crypto company linked to US President Donald Trump and his family, said it has worked with its partners to freeze stolen funds. Crypto exchange Coinbase said it was unaffected by the incident and was monitoring the situation. Several crypto industry observers had flagged concerns about a potential hack on Binance hours before the exchange confirmed the security issue. Bitcoin dropped by more than 4% following the alerts. The price of other major cryptocurrencies including Ethereum and Solana also fell sharply. sources.title: Crypto giant Binance hit by $6.3bn hack suspected to be largest in history - BBC
passages: Cryptocurrency giant Binance said on Thursday that $6.3bn (£4.7bn) of digital assets have been impacted by what is thought to be the biggest crypto hack on record.
The lab's global head of policy Ari Redbord told the BBC the Binance hack is a "watershed moment" that is unlike anything the industry has seen.
Check Point's chief information security officer Jayant Dave said the losses estimated by Binance made it "the largest crypto theft on record".
Two other major crypto platforms, Tether and Circle, said they had frozen a total of about $2.4bn of assets in response to the potential Binance hack.

Binance did not directly respond to BBC questions about the incident's potential links to North Korea but said: "We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice."
Several crypto industry observers had flagged concerns about a potential hack on Binance hours before the exchange confirmed the security issue.
AI-powered investigations company TRM Labs said in a report that several elements of the Binance attack resemble earlier North Korean-linked incidents, including the Bybit hack.
Binance, which was founded in China in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide.
Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said the company's initial investigation suggested the hack started with a compromised engineer's laptop.
Chainalysis, a crypto analytics firm, also said it has "high confidence" that the North Korean group are linked to the hack.
Crypto exchange Coinbase said it was unaffected by the incident and was monitoring the situation.
In a series of posts, Yi He, Binance's co-chief executive, thanked various cryptocurrency issuers for freezing the assets.

extraction.body: Cryptocurrency giant Binance said on Thursday that $6.3bn (£4.7bn) of digital assets have been impacted by what is thought to be the biggest crypto hack on record. The world's biggest crypto exchange said about half of those assets had been frozen but that many remained in the hands of the hackers, adding that it will "cover all losses". The company said while initial checks suggested an engineer's laptop had been compromised, allowing an attacker to make unauthorised withdrawals, "our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach". Two analytics firms have attributed the incident, which eclipses a record-setting $1.5bn hack on the Bybit exchange in 2025, to a North Korean hacking unit called TraderTraitor. Cyber-security firm Check Point said the unit is also known in the industry as Lazarus Group, which has been blamed for the 2025 hack. Check Point's chief information security officer Jayant Dave said the losses estimated by Binance made it "the largest crypto theft on record". AI-powered investigations company TRM Labs said in a report that several elements of the Binance attack resemble earlier North Korean-linked incidents, including the Bybit hack. The lab's global head of policy Ari Redbord told the BBC the Binance hack is a "watershed moment" that is unlike anything the industry has seen. The attacker still holds an enormous sum of stolen assets, meaning efforts to trace and recover the funds are far from over, Redbord added. Binance, which was founded in China in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide. The company said in 2024 that it has more than $160bn in assets under its custody. The exchange has been subject of regulatory scrutiny around the world. Chainalysis, a crypto analytics firm, also said it has "high confidence" that the North Korean group are linked to the hack. For the last few years North Korea-linked operatives have focussed on attacking cryptocurrency companies for large thefts of digital tokens. Eric Jardine, Chainalysis' Head of Research, urged every exchange to remain vigilant as the platforms are attractive targets for hackers due to the sheer value of assets. Binance did not directly respond to BBC questions about the incident's potential links to North Korea but said: "We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice." The incident concerns Binance.com - while much smaller crypto platform Binance.US, which provides trading services specifically for American residents - said its platform is not affected by the issue. Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said the company's initial investigation suggested the hack started with a compromised engineer's laptop. "That gave an attacker access to a service container, where they submitted unauthorized withdrawal transactions," he said in a statement. "To be clear: the attacker did not simply use one engineer's permissions, and this was not a single 'one-click' action. It involved a more complex attack process. Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual. So far, we have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak." He said a detailed "post-mortem" would be shared once the investigation was complete. In an update, the company said in a statement on X that another investigation found there had been other breach points: "We are still gathering the facts, and will share more directly as we have them." Check Point's Dave said this attack also resembled a hack on crypto exchange platform Bitget in September in which $388m (£289m) was lost: "This implies that attackers no longer need the vault keys. They target the systems and people with authority to use them." In a series of posts, Yi He, Binance's co-chief executive, thanked various cryptocurrency issuers for freezing the assets. "Safety first: withdrawals are currently disabled until the environment is confirmed to be secure," she said. Two other major crypto platforms, Tether and Circle, said they had frozen a total of about $2.4bn of assets in response to the potential Binance hack. World Liberty Financial, a crypto company linked to US President Donald Trump and his family, said it has worked with its partners to freeze stolen funds. Crypto exchange Coinbase said it was unaffected by the incident and was monitoring the situation. Several crypto industry observers had flagged concerns about a potential hack on Binance hours before the exchange confirmed the security issue. Bitcoin dropped by more than 4% following the alerts. The price of other major cryptocurrencies including Ethereum and Solana also fell sharply. The Binance hack has thrust cryptocurrencies back into headlines - but what are they and how do they work? BBC business reporter Archana Shukla explains more about what is suspected to be the largest hack in history. Prosecutors had accused Pleterski of stealing tens of millions of dollars of investor funds to buy himself a range of luxuries.

sources.title: Hackers steal $6.3 billion from Binance in world's biggest crypto heist - Yahoo Finance
passages: SINGAPORE/TOKYO Oct 30 (Reuters) - Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a record theft that analysts pinned on North Korea and said could shake faith in digital assets.

TRM said the attackers were able to order wallets that Binance uses to empty into hacker-controlled wallets, mirroring a 2025 heist at crypto exchange Bybit, which the US Federal Bureau of Investigation attributed to North Korea.

World Liberty Financial said it ​worked with custodian BitGo to freeze funds, and Binance co-founder ​Yi He said $27 million in stablecoins and about $2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen.
Crypto firm Ripple also froze roughly $200 million in funds, Yi said.

BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down 5% over the past 24 hours at $709.70, according to CoinGecko, while shaky ​confidence ​hit listed crypto exchange shares.
Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, ​has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of its 2025 annual report.
Binance runs a secure asset fund for users, a $1 billion bitcoin reserve designed to protect customer assets in the event of security breaches, according to its website.
Cryptocurrency prices fell on the news, while Binance halted withdrawals and said it would cover the losses.
"This was a complex attack, and we are doing all we can in coordination with law enforcement to resolve it," Binance ‌said in a post on X.
"Our security team is tracing the full attack path through the compromised computer which may be the entry point of the incident," Binance said.
Later, the company added it had uncovered additional points of breach.

Mark Karpeles, former chief of defunct Tokyo-based bitcoin exchange Mt Gox, which collapsed a dozen years ago after $500 million in bitcoin was stolen, said attackers probably accessed private keys for at least two Binance wallets.
"Binance appears to have split its assets across multiple systems, ensuring a hack can only affect a part of the assets, but even so a single hack is a large loss," he said.
"It's the biggest hack in history," Aravind Srinivasan at market maker GSR said as crypto prices fell broadly.

An initial investigation suggested the breach ‌may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of Binance's engineers, which let an attacker gain access to one of its systems and make unauthorized withdrawals, Binance said.

extraction.body: By Ankur Banerjee, Rocky Swift and Summer Zhen SINGAPORE/TOKYO Oct 30 (Reuters) - Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a record theft that analysts pinned on North Korea and said could shake faith in digital assets. Cryptocurrency prices fell on the news, while Binance halted withdrawals and said it would cover the losses. About half the stolen assets were quickly frozen ‌by stablecoin issuers such as Tether, Circle and the Trump-backed World Liberty Financial. "This was a complex attack, and we are doing all we can in coordination with law enforcement to resolve it," Binance ‌said in a post on X. The exchange said customer funds were safe and that it was working with partners to freeze some of the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It expects to resume withdrawal services in the next 45 hours. It did not mention ​the status of the remaining $3.3 billion. Binance runs a secure asset fund for users, a $1 billion bitcoin reserve designed to protect customer assets in the event of security breaches, according to its website. Co-CEO Teng said that "and company funds" would cover losses. The bulk of the heist unfolded in around 20 minutes beginning late on Thursday and bore similarities to previous large attacks blamed on North Korea, according to US blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis. TRM said the attackers were able to order wallets that Binance uses to empty into hacker-controlled wallets, mirroring a 2025 heist at crypto exchange Bybit, which the US Federal Bureau of Investigation attributed to North Korea. "TRM attributes the attack to ... North Korea's elite hacking unit," the firm said in ‌an analysis of the hack posted to its website. Both TRM and Chainalysis ⁠said they were highly confident North Korea was responsible. North Korea routinely denies that. Its mission in Geneva and embassy in China did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment. "Your money ⁠is safe and we're covering every loss," Teng said on X. Notorious previous episodes of theft and fraud among fallen crypto giants such as FTX and Mt. Gox set the stage for protracted bear markets, bruises the industry has worked to put behind it in US President Donald Trump’s promised new era of regulatory clarity for cryptocurrencies. This comes days ahead of the US midterm elections taking place next week, when Democrats could potentially retake one or both chambers of Congress and open the door to greater regulatory scrutiny for the industry. Exchange thefts and malfeasance have been an ever-present backdrop of crypto’s almost two-decade ascent, the most famous of which was the collapse of Sam Bankman-Fried’s FTX in November 2022. In what remains perhaps the most notorious hacking incident, Japan-based Bitcoin exchange Mt. Gox was struck in 2011. Gox eventually went bankrupt. “It’s a huge damage to crypto because of the consistent successful hacks in the space,” said Tian Zeng, chief executive officer of crypto hedge fund Third Eye. “The fact that exploits keep happening makes it dangerous in the age of newest AI models being released every two weeks.” The Binance incident came on the same day event-contract venue Polymarket halted trading on its international exchange for an hour after it said that a third-party software provider was compromised. South Korea’s Daishin Securities disclosed a data leak affecting about 38,000 customers this week, and Mirae Asset Global Investments reported a hacking incident, Yonhap reported. In Japan, hackers on Tuesday threatened to release data of traders using a GMO Internet Group cloud service for foreign-exchange trading. About half the stolen assets were quickly frozen by stablecoin issuers such as Tether, Circle and the Trump-backed World Liberty Financial. The bulk of the heist unfolded in around 20 minutes beginning late on Thursday and bore similarities to previous large attacks blamed on North Korea, according to U.S. blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis. TRM said the attackers were able to order wallets that Binance uses to empty into hacker-controlled wallets, mirroring a 2025 heist at crypto exchange Bybit, which the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation had attributed to Pyongyang. North Korea’s elite hacking unit,” the firm said in an analysis of the hack posted to its website. Both TRM and Chainalysis said they were highly confident North Korea was responsible. ‘Biggest hack in history’ North Korea has ​for years ⁠used state-linked cyber units for espionage, financial theft and revenue, according to U.S. and South Korean authorities as well ⁠as cybersecurity ​experts. Binance said user funds were safe and that it was working with partners to freeze some of the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It did not mention the status of the remaining $3.3 billion. “Your money is safe and we’re covering every loss,” co-CEO Richard Teng said on X. “Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual.” “It’s the biggest hack in history,” Aravind Srinivasan at market maker GSR said as crypto prices fell broadly. BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down 5 per cent over the past 24 hours at $709.70, according to CoinGecko, while shaky confidence hit listed crypto exchange shares. Shares in crypto exchange Coinbase Global, which said it was unaffected, slid 4.8 per cent, while those of bitcoin buyer Strategy MSTR.O fell nearly 6 per cent in extended U.S. trading. Compromised laptop An initial investigation suggested the breach may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of Binance’s engineers, which let an attacker gain access to one of its systems and make unauthorized withdrawals, Binance said. “Our security team is tracing the full attack path through the compromised computer which may be the entry point of the incident,” Binance said. Mark Karpeles, former chief of defunct Tokyo-based bitcoin exchange Mt Gox, which collapsed a dozen years ago after $500 million in bitcoin was stolen, said attackers probably accessed private keys for at least two Binance wallets. “Binance appears to have split its assets across multiple systems, ensuring a hack can only affect a part of the assets, but even so a single hack is a large loss,” he said. Beyond the potential loss of assets, the security breach was likely to have wider ramifications for crypto, which had already been under pressure due to higher U.S. interest rates and softer demand from exchange-traded fund buyers, analysts said. “It may further dampen risk appetite and prompt investors to reassess the safety of assets held on centralized exchanges,” said Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group, based in Hong Kong. Hack size tops Binance secure asset fund Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of the exchange’s 2025 annual report. The crypto exchange runs a secure asset fund for users, which is a $1 billion reserve held entirely in bitcoin that is intended to protect user assets in cases of security breaches, according to its website. Co-CEO Teng said that “and company funds” will cover losses. Stablecoin issuer Tether said it had frozen nearly $1.57 billion in assets linked to the incident, while Circle froze more than $800 million. World Liberty Financial said it worked with custodian BitGo to freeze funds, and Binance co-founder Yi He said $27 million in stablecoins and about $2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen. Crypto firm Ripple also froze roughly $200 million in funds, Yi said. The incident adds to a string of crypto thefts. Last year, attackers stole $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks, according to researchers at TRM Labs. In September, cryptocurrency exchange Bitget said roughly $350 million in crypto had been stolen from its platform, underscoring the industry’s vulnerability to hackers.

coreStoryFacts.text: SINGAPORE/TOKYO Oct 30 (Reuters) - Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a record theft that analysts pinned on North Korea and said could shake faith in digital assets.

TRM said the attackers were able to order wallets that Binance uses to empty into hacker-controlled wallets, mirroring a 2025 heist at crypto exchange Bybit, which the US Federal Bureau of Investigation attributed to North Korea.

World Liberty Financial said it ​worked with custodian BitGo to freeze funds, and Binance co-founder ​Yi He said $27 million in stablecoins and about $2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen.
Crypto firm Ripple also froze roughly $200 million in funds, Yi said.

BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down 5% over the past 24 hours at $709.70, according to CoinGecko, while shaky ​confidence ​hit listed crypto exchange shares.
Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, ​has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of its 2025 annual report.
Binance runs a secure asset fund for users, a $1 billion bitcoin reserve designed to protect customer assets in the event of security breaches, according to its website.
Cryptocurrency prices fell on the news, while Binance halted withdrawals and said it would cover the losses.
"This was a complex attack, and we are doing all we can in coordination with law enforcement to resolve it," Binance ‌said in a post on X.
"Our security team is tracing the full attack path through the compromised computer which may be the entry point of the incident," Binance said.
Later, the company added it had uncovered additional points of breach.

Mark Karpeles, former chief of defunct Tokyo-based bitcoin exchange Mt Gox, which collapsed a dozen years ago after $500 million in bitcoin was stolen, said attackers probably accessed private keys for at least two Binance wallets.
"Binance appears to have split its assets across multiple systems, ensuring a hack can only affect a part of the assets, but even so a single hack is a large loss," he said.
"It's the biggest hack in history," Aravind Srinivasan at market maker GSR said as crypto prices fell broadly.

An initial investigation suggested the breach ‌may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of Binance's engineers, which let an attacker gain access to one of its systems and make unauthorized withdrawals, Binance said.
Crypto exchange Binance has suffered a $6.3 billion hack, the largest to hit the digital-asset industry and the latest in a slew of security incidents afflicting the financial sector.
Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange, said $6.3 billion of funds are involved in what the industry is describing as crypto’s biggest-ever hack.
Before now, the biggest publicly known crypto hack occurred at exchange Bybit in February 2025, in which attackers made off with almost $1.5 billion of tokens.
For crypto faithful who’d been basking in a two-month-long price rebound, the Binance incident is a potential setback.
The two biggest stablecoin issuers said they took steps to freeze missing currency.
“The estimated total impact sits at around $6.3B,” Binance said in a post on X.
“We have worked with blockchain partners to freeze affected assets, with ~$3 billion frozen on-chain so far.”
“The rumored Binance hack is definitely driving down coin prices,” said Fredrick Collins, chief executive and co-founder of crypto data platform Velo Data.

“Binance is such a behemoth in crypto that any hit to confidence in them is a hit to confidence in the industry as a whole, especially as people have already been skittish over the increasing cyber capabilities of AI.”

extraction.body: By Ankur Banerjee, Rocky Swift and Summer Zhen SINGAPORE/TOKYO Oct 30 (Reuters) - Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a record theft that analysts pinned on North Korea and said could shake faith in digital assets. Cryptocurrency prices fell on the news, while Binance halted withdrawals and said it would cover the losses. About half the stolen assets were quickly frozen ‌by stablecoin issuers such as Tether, Circle and the Trump-backed World Liberty Financial. "This was a complex attack, and we are doing all we can in coordination with law enforcement to resolve it," Binance ‌said in a post on X. The exchange said customer funds were safe and that it was working with partners to freeze some of the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It expects to resume withdrawal services in the next 45 hours. It did not mention ​the status of the remaining $3.3 billion. Binance runs a secure asset fund for users, a $1 billion bitcoin reserve designed to protect customer assets in the event of security breaches, according to its website. Co-CEO Teng said that "and company funds" would cover losses. The bulk of the heist unfolded in around 20 minutes beginning late on Thursday and bore similarities to previous large attacks blamed on North Korea, according to US blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis. TRM said the attackers were able to order wallets that Binance uses to empty into hacker-controlled wallets, mirroring a 2025 heist at crypto exchange Bybit, which the US Federal Bureau of Investigation attributed to North Korea. "TRM attributes the attack to ... North Korea's elite hacking unit," the firm said in ‌an analysis of the hack posted to its website. Both TRM and Chainalysis ⁠said they were highly confident North Korea was responsible. North Korea routinely denies that. Its mission in Geneva and embassy in China did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment. "Your money ⁠is safe and we're covering every loss," Teng said on X. "Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual." "It's the biggest hack in history," Aravind Srinivasan at market maker GSR said as crypto prices fell broadly. Bitcoin hit a six-week low of $76,368 and ether fell more than 3% to a two-month low of $2,178 before markets stabilised. BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down 5% over the past 24 hours at $709.70, according to CoinGecko, while shaky ​confidence ​hit listed crypto exchange shares. Shares in crypto exchange Coinbase Global, which said it was unaffected, slid 4.8%, while those of bitcoin buyer ​Strategy fell nearly 6% in extended US trading. An initial investigation suggested the breach ‌may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of Binance's engineers, which let an attacker gain access to one of its systems and make unauthorized withdrawals, Binance said. "Our security team is tracing the full attack path through the compromised computer which may be the entry point of the incident," Binance said. Later, the company added it had uncovered additional points of breach. Mark Karpeles, former chief of defunct Tokyo-based bitcoin exchange Mt Gox, which collapsed a dozen years ago after $500 million in bitcoin was stolen, said attackers probably accessed private keys for at least two Binance wallets. "Binance appears to have split its assets across multiple systems, ensuring a hack can only affect a part of the assets, but even so a single hack is a large loss," he said. Beyond the potential loss of assets, the security breach was likely to have wider ramifications for the crypto sector, which had already been under pressure ‌due to higher US interest rates and softer demand from exchange-traded fund buyers, analysts said. "It may further dampen risk appetite and ​prompt investors to reassess the safety of assets held on centralised exchanges," said Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group, based in Hong ​Kong. Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, ​has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of its 2025 annual report. Stablecoin issuer Tether said it had frozen nearly $1.57 billion in assets ‌linked to the incident, while Circle froze more than $800 million. World Liberty Financial said it ​worked with custodian BitGo to freeze funds, and Binance co-founder ​Yi He said $27 million in stablecoins and about $2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen. Crypto firm Ripple also froze roughly $200 million in funds, Yi said. The incident adds to a string of crypto thefts. Last year, attackers stole $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks, according to researchers at TRM Labs. In September, Bitget said roughly $350 million in crypto had been stolen from its platform, underscoring the industry's ​vulnerability to hackers. "The broader credit and industry implications will depend on the ultimate ‌losses, affected counterparties, asset recovery, and importantly, whether the incident leads to wider disruption or loss of confidence across the digital-asset ecosystem," said Cristiano Ventricelli, vice president, digital assets at Moody's Ratings.

extraction.body: SINGAPORE/TOKYO -- Hackers stole US$6.3 billion from Binance, the world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a record theft that analysts pinned on North Korea and said could shake faith in digital assets. Cryptocurrency prices fell on the news, while Binance halted withdrawals and said it would cover the losses. About half the stolen assets were quickly frozen by stablecoin issuers such as Tether, Circle and the Trump-backed World Liberty Financial. The bulk of the heist unfolded in around 20 minutes beginning late on Thursday and bore similarities to previous large attacks blamed on North Korea, according to U.S. blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis. TRM said the attackers were able to order wallets that Binance uses to empty into hacker-controlled wallets, mirroring a 2025 heist at crypto exchange Bybit, which the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation had attributed to Pyongyang. North Korea’s elite hacking unit,” the firm said in an analysis of the hack posted to its website. Both TRM and Chainalysis said they were highly confident North Korea was responsible. ‘Biggest hack in history’ North Korea has ​for years ⁠used state-linked cyber units for espionage, financial theft and revenue, according to U.S. and South Korean authorities as well ⁠as cybersecurity ​experts. Binance said user funds were safe and that it was working with partners to freeze some of the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It did not mention the status of the remaining $3.3 billion. “Your money is safe and we’re covering every loss,” co-CEO Richard Teng said on X. “Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual.” “It’s the biggest hack in history,” Aravind Srinivasan at market maker GSR said as crypto prices fell broadly. BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down 5 per cent over the past 24 hours at $709.70, according to CoinGecko, while shaky confidence hit listed crypto exchange shares. Shares in crypto exchange Coinbase Global, which said it was unaffected, slid 4.8 per cent, while those of bitcoin buyer Strategy MSTR.O fell nearly 6 per cent in extended U.S. trading. Compromised laptop An initial investigation suggested the breach may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of Binance’s engineers, which let an attacker gain access to one of its systems and make unauthorized withdrawals, Binance said. “Our security team is tracing the full attack path through the compromised computer which may be the entry point of the incident,” Binance said. Mark Karpeles, former chief of defunct Tokyo-based bitcoin exchange Mt Gox, which collapsed a dozen years ago after $500 million in bitcoin was stolen, said attackers probably accessed private keys for at least two Binance wallets. “Binance appears to have split its assets across multiple systems, ensuring a hack can only affect a part of the assets, but even so a single hack is a large loss,” he said. Beyond the potential loss of assets, the security breach was likely to have wider ramifications for crypto, which had already been under pressure due to higher U.S. interest rates and softer demand from exchange-traded fund buyers, analysts said. “It may further dampen risk appetite and prompt investors to reassess the safety of assets held on centralized exchanges,” said Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group, based in Hong Kong. Hack size tops Binance secure asset fund Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of the exchange’s 2025 annual report. The crypto exchange runs a secure asset fund for users, which is a $1 billion reserve held entirely in bitcoin that is intended to protect user assets in cases of security breaches, according to its website. Co-CEO Teng said that “and company funds” will cover losses. Stablecoin issuer Tether said it had frozen nearly $1.57 billion in assets linked to the incident, while Circle froze more than $800 million. World Liberty Financial said it worked with custodian BitGo to freeze funds, and Binance co-founder Yi He said $27 million in stablecoins and about $2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen. Crypto firm Ripple also froze roughly $200 million in funds, Yi said. The incident adds to a string of crypto thefts. Last year, attackers stole $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks, according to researchers at TRM Labs. In September, cryptocurrency exchange Bitget said roughly $350 million in crypto had been stolen from its platform, underscoring the industry’s vulnerability to hackers.

Reddit will no longer allow logged out users or those without an account to view content on its platform, CEO Steve Huffman shared in an update . The change, which the company said will initially be tested in "select markets" outside the US, comes as the company says that search traffic has declined significantly. "A key piece of work to retain new audiences is shifting Reddit to a logged-in-only experience," Huffman wrote in a shareholder letter. "Moving to primarily logged-in will ensure our users have the best Reddit experience possible, and can find the content and communities most relevant to them." The change is the most dramatic shift the company has made as it battles AI scraping and changes to internet search. It will also likely rattle users, some of whom are already frustrated with recent moves like restrictions on Old Reddit . Huffman said that it was a "big change" but necessary for the company. "It is better for our business because we will have more signals for ads targeting, and being logged-in leads to higher engagement generally," he wrote. "It also allows us to protect access to Reddit's extremely valuable corpus of data, and helps us better adapt to emerging regulations around the world." Huffman didn't explicitly mention age verification laws, but requiring users to log in would presumably help the company comply with such measures. Huffman said the company is still working on figuring out exactly when logged out users will encounter a "hard prompt" to log in. "We need to find the right boundary," he said during the company's third-quarter earnings call. "Whether they're coming from a shared link or maybe from search ... there'll be some version of Reddit accessible for those moments before we do that hard prompt." Reddit's CEO, who has been clearly frustrated with the state of online search and Google's AI overviews for a while, was more explicit in his criticism. "The reality is, the AI mode does not drive traffic, not for us and not to anybody, as far as I know," he said. "So that's just a fundamental shift in how Google works. It used to be a traffic driver, now it's not." The company reported that search traffic was "down meaningfully" in the most recent quarter, with the company seeing referrals from search drop by more than 1 million each week during the month of October. Reddit's relationship with Google is also complicated. The company has a licensing deal with the search giant so it can access the platform's data for AI training. That deal is reportedly worth about $60 million a year. More recently, there are reports that Reddit may be reconsidering this arrangement. When asked about it on the call, Huffman said there are "active discussions" but didn't share specifics. "What's most important is that any deal we do needs to advance our long-term strategy, it has to be a fair exchange of value," he said. Huffman hinted at some other product changes the company is considering to help it grow engagement with logged in users. The Reddit founder said the company is working on adding "more organization" to its main feed to make it "more consistent" and "less grab bag-ey" than it currently is. He also suggested that an "incognito mode" could be in the works. He speculated that adding "private browsing" could help the company address users who repeatedly uninstall and reinstall the Reddit app.

extraction.body: The company is starting with tests outside of the US. Reddit will no longer allow logged out users or those without an account to view content on its platform, CEO Steve Huffman shared in an update . The change, which the company said will initially be tested in "select markets" outside the US, comes as the company says that search traffic has declined significantly. "A key piece of work to retain new audiences is shifting Reddit to a logged-in-only experience," Huffman wrote in a shareholder letter. "Moving to primarily logged-in will ensure our users have the best Reddit experience possible, and can find the content and communities most relevant to them." The change is the most dramatic shift the company has made as it battles AI scraping and changes to internet search. It will also likely rattle users, some of whom are already frustrated with recent moves like restrictions on Old Reddit . Huffman said that it was a "big change" but necessary for the company. "It is better for our business because we will have more signals for ads targeting, and being logged-in leads to higher engagement generally," he wrote. "It also allows us to protect access to Reddit's extremely valuable corpus of data, and helps us better adapt to emerging regulations around the world." Huffman didn't explicitly mention age verification laws, but requiring users to log in would presumably help the company comply with such measures. Huffman said the company is still working on figuring out exactly when logged out users will encounter a "hard prompt" to log in. "We need to find the right boundary," he said during the company's third-quarter earnings call. "Whether they're coming from a shared link or maybe from search ... there'll be some version of Reddit accessible for those moments before we do that hard prompt." Reddit's CEO, who has been clearly frustrated with the state of online search and Google's AI overviews for a while, was more explicit in his criticism. "The reality is, the AI mode does not drive traffic, not for us and not to anybody, as far as I know," he said. "So that's just a fundamental shift in how Google works. It used to be a traffic driver, now it's not." The company reported that search traffic was "down meaningfully" in the most recent quarter, with the company seeing referrals from search drop by more than 1 million each week during the month of October. Reddit's relationship with Google is also complicated. The company has a licensing deal with the search giant so it can access the platform's data for AI training. That deal is reportedly worth about $60 million a year. More recently, there are reports that Reddit may be reconsidering this arrangement. When asked about it on the call, Huffman said there are "active discussions" but didn't share specifics. "What's most important is that any deal we do needs to advance our long-term strategy, it has to be a fair exchange of value," he said. Huffman hinted at some other product changes the company is considering to help it grow engagement with logged in users. The Reddit founder said the company is working on adding "more organization" to its main feed to make it "more consistent" and "less grab bag-ey" than it currently is. He also suggested that an "incognito mode" could be in the works. He speculated that adding "private browsing" could help the company address users who repeatedly uninstall and reinstall the Reddit app.

passages: SINGAPORE/TOKYO Oct 30 (Reuters) - Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a record theft that analysts pinned on North Korea and said could shake faith in digital assets.

TRM said the attackers were able to order wallets that Binance uses to empty into hacker-controlled wallets, mirroring a 2025 heist at crypto exchange Bybit, which the US Federal Bureau of Investigation attributed to North Korea.

World Liberty Financial said it ​worked with custodian BitGo to freeze funds, and Binance co-founder ​Yi He said $27 million in stablecoins and about $2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen.
Crypto firm Ripple also froze roughly $200 million in funds, Yi said.

BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down 5% over the past 24 hours at $709.70, according to CoinGecko, while shaky ​confidence ​hit listed crypto exchange shares.
Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, ​has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of its 2025 annual report.
Binance runs a secure asset fund for users, a $1 billion bitcoin reserve designed to protect customer assets in the event of security breaches, according to its website.
Cryptocurrency prices fell on the news, while Binance halted withdrawals and said it would cover the losses.
"This was a complex attack, and we are doing all we can in coordination with law enforcement to resolve it," Binance ‌said in a post on X.
"Our security team is tracing the full attack path through the compromised computer which may be the entry point of the incident," Binance said.
Later, the company added it had uncovered additional points of breach.

Mark Karpeles, former chief of defunct Tokyo-based bitcoin exchange Mt Gox, which collapsed a dozen years ago after $500 million in bitcoin was stolen, said attackers probably accessed private keys for at least two Binance wallets.
"Binance appears to have split its assets across multiple systems, ensuring a hack can only affect a part of the assets, but even so a single hack is a large loss," he said.
"It's the biggest hack in history," Aravind Srinivasan at market maker GSR said as crypto prices fell broadly.

An initial investigation suggested the breach ‌may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of Binance's engineers, which let an attacker gain access to one of its systems and make unauthorized withdrawals, Binance said.

extraction.body: By Ankur Banerjee, Rocky Swift and Summer Zhen SINGAPORE/TOKYO Oct 30 (Reuters) - Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a record theft that analysts pinned on North Korea and said could shake faith in digital assets. Cryptocurrency prices fell on the news, while Binance halted withdrawals and said it would cover the losses. About half the stolen assets were quickly frozen ‌by stablecoin issuers such as Tether, Circle and the Trump-backed World Liberty Financial. "This was a complex attack, and we are doing all we can in coordination with law enforcement to resolve it," Binance ‌said in a post on X. The exchange said customer funds were safe and that it was working with partners to freeze some of the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It expects to resume withdrawal services in the next 45 hours. It did not mention ​the status of the remaining $3.3 billion. Binance runs a secure asset fund for users, a $1 billion bitcoin reserve designed to protect customer assets in the event of security breaches, according to its website. Co-CEO Teng said that "and company funds" would cover losses. The bulk of the heist unfolded in around 20 minutes beginning late on Thursday and bore similarities to previous large attacks blamed on North Korea, according to US blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis. TRM said the attackers were able to order wallets that Binance uses to empty into hacker-controlled wallets, mirroring a 2025 heist at crypto exchange Bybit, which the US Federal Bureau of Investigation attributed to North Korea. "TRM attributes the attack to ... North Korea's elite hacking unit," the firm said in ‌an analysis of the hack posted to its website. Both TRM and Chainalysis ⁠said they were highly confident North Korea was responsible. North Korea routinely denies that. Its mission in Geneva and embassy in China did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment. "Your money ⁠is safe and we're covering every loss," Teng said on X. "Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual." "It's the biggest hack in history," Aravind Srinivasan at market maker GSR said as crypto prices fell broadly. Bitcoin hit a six-week low of $76,368 and ether fell more than 3% to a two-month low of $2,178 before markets stabilised. BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down 5% over the past 24 hours at $709.70, according to CoinGecko, while shaky ​confidence ​hit listed crypto exchange shares. Shares in crypto exchange Coinbase Global, which said it was unaffected, slid 4.8%, while those of bitcoin buyer ​Strategy fell nearly 6% in extended US trading. An initial investigation suggested the breach ‌may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of Binance's engineers, which let an attacker gain access to one of its systems and make unauthorized withdrawals, Binance said. "Our security team is tracing the full attack path through the compromised computer which may be the entry point of the incident," Binance said. Later, the company added it had uncovered additional points of breach. Mark Karpeles, former chief of defunct Tokyo-based bitcoin exchange Mt Gox, which collapsed a dozen years ago after $500 million in bitcoin was stolen, said attackers probably accessed private keys for at least two Binance wallets. "Binance appears to have split its assets across multiple systems, ensuring a hack can only affect a part of the assets, but even so a single hack is a large loss," he said. Beyond the potential loss of assets, the security breach was likely to have wider ramifications for the crypto sector, which had already been under pressure ‌due to higher US interest rates and softer demand from exchange-traded fund buyers, analysts said. "It may further dampen risk appetite and ​prompt investors to reassess the safety of assets held on centralised exchanges," said Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group, based in Hong ​Kong. Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, ​has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of its 2025 annual report. Stablecoin issuer Tether said it had frozen nearly $1.57 billion in assets ‌linked to the incident, while Circle froze more than $800 million. World Liberty Financial said it ​worked with custodian BitGo to freeze funds, and Binance co-founder ​Yi He said $27 million in stablecoins and about $2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen. Crypto firm Ripple also froze roughly $200 million in funds, Yi said. The incident adds to a string of crypto thefts. Last year, attackers stole $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks, according to researchers at TRM Labs. In September, Bitget said roughly $350 million in crypto had been stolen from its platform, underscoring the industry's ​vulnerability to hackers. "The broader credit and industry implications will depend on the ultimate ‌losses, affected counterparties, asset recovery, and importantly, whether the incident leads to wider disruption or loss of confidence across the digital-asset ecosystem," said Cristiano Ventricelli, vice president, digital assets at Moody's Ratings.

passages: NEW YORK: Cryptocurrency platform Binance said on Thursday it had been hit by a major hack affecting about $6.3 billion in funds, around half of which has been frozen to prevent theft.

The world’s largest crypto exchange by daily trading volume posted a series of sometimes contradictory messages on X, saying “user funds are completely safe” but also that it would “cover all losses”.
That is four times the previous record for such an attack, the $1.5 billion stolen from the Bybit platform in February last year, which was attributed to hackers linked to North Korea.

Tether chief Paolo Ardoino said his company had frozen about $1.6 billion of its USDT stablecoin “related to a potential Binance exchange hack”, and Circle chief Jeremy Allaire said his firm had frozen more than $800 million in USDC.
Stablecoins are digital currencies pegged to a traditional currency, in this case the US dollar.
The US Justice Department and FBI did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
The figure “may continue to increase” as it works to trace and freeze more assets, it said.
An initial investigation suggested the hackers used a compromised laptop belonging to a “DevOps engineer” to access a “service container” and carry out unauthorized withdrawals, Binance said.
“We have found no evidence of any private key leaks from wallets,” it said, promising a detailed technical analysis once the investigation is complete.
“It does look like a hack on Binance,” said former chief executive Changpeng Zhao, who remains majority shareholder.
Most major cryptocurrencies fell on the news.

At about 0400 GMT, bitcoin and Ethereum were down 0.8 percent, after falling nearly 5 percent and 6 percent respectively, while Binance’s BNB token was up 2.7 percent after a plunge of nearly 10 percent. — AFP

coreStoryFacts.text: SINGAPORE/TOKYO Oct 30 (Reuters) - Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a record theft that analysts pinned on North Korea and said could shake faith in digital assets.

TRM said the attackers were able to order wallets that Binance uses to empty into hacker-controlled wallets, mirroring a 2025 heist at crypto exchange Bybit, which the US Federal Bureau of Investigation attributed to North Korea.

World Liberty Financial said it ​worked with custodian BitGo to freeze funds, and Binance co-founder ​Yi He said $27 million in stablecoins and about $2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen.
Crypto firm Ripple also froze roughly $200 million in funds, Yi said.

BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down 5% over the past 24 hours at $709.70, according to CoinGecko, while shaky ​confidence ​hit listed crypto exchange shares.
Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, ​has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of its 2025 annual report.
Binance runs a secure asset fund for users, a $1 billion bitcoin reserve designed to protect customer assets in the event of security breaches, according to its website.
Cryptocurrency prices fell on the news, while Binance halted withdrawals and said it would cover the losses.
"This was a complex attack, and we are doing all we can in coordination with law enforcement to resolve it," Binance ‌said in a post on X.
"Our security team is tracing the full attack path through the compromised computer which may be the entry point of the incident," Binance said.
Later, the company added it had uncovered additional points of breach.

Mark Karpeles, former chief of defunct Tokyo-based bitcoin exchange Mt Gox, which collapsed a dozen years ago after $500 million in bitcoin was stolen, said attackers probably accessed private keys for at least two Binance wallets.
"Binance appears to have split its assets across multiple systems, ensuring a hack can only affect a part of the assets, but even so a single hack is a large loss," he said.
"It's the biggest hack in history," Aravind Srinivasan at market maker GSR said as crypto prices fell broadly.

An initial investigation suggested the breach ‌may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of Binance's engineers, which let an attacker gain access to one of its systems and make unauthorized withdrawals, Binance said.
Crypto exchange Binance has suffered a $6.3 billion hack, the largest to hit the digital-asset industry and the latest in a slew of security incidents afflicting the financial sector.
The world’s largest crypto trading platform suspended all withdrawals Friday and pledged to cover all losses.
Binance has temporarily suspended all withdrawals, which it expects to resume within 48 hours, co-founder Yi He said in a post on X.
The company said it will cover all losses and “user funds are safe.”
Before now, the biggest publicly known crypto hack occurred at exchange Bybit in February 2025, in which attackers made off with almost US$1.5 billion of tokens.
For crypto faithful who’d been basking in a two-month-long price rebound, the Binance incident is a potential setback.

“The rumored Binance hack is definitely driving down coin prices,” said Fredrick Collins, chief executive and co-founder of crypto data platform Velo Data.

“Binance is such a behemoth in crypto that any hit to confidence in them is a hit to confidence in the industry as a whole, especially as people have already been skittish over the increasing cyber capabilities of AI.”

Cryptocurrency prices fell on the news, while Binance halted withdrawals and said it would cover the losses. About half the stolen assets were quickly frozen ‌by stablecoin issuers such as Tether, Circle and the Trump-backed World Liberty Financial. "This was a complex attack, and we are doing all we can in coordination with law enforcement to resolve it," Binance ‌said in a post on X. The exchange said customer funds were safe and that it was working with partners to freeze some of the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It expects to resume withdrawal services in the next 45 hours. It did not mention ​the status of the remaining $3.3 billion. Binance runs a secure asset fund for users, a $1 billion bitcoin reserve designed to protect customer assets in the event of security breaches, according to its website. Co-CEO Teng said that "and company funds" would cover losses. The bulk of the heist unfolded in around 20 minutes beginning late on Thursday and bore similarities to previous large attacks blamed on North Korea, according to US blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis. TRM said the attackers were able to order wallets that Binance uses to empty into hacker-controlled wallets, mirroring a 2025 heist at crypto exchange Bybit, which the US Federal Bureau of Investigation attributed to North Korea. "TRM attributes the attack to ... North Korea's elite hacking unit," the firm said in ‌an analysis of the hack posted to its website. Both TRM and Chainalysis ⁠said they were highly confident North Korea was responsible. North Korea routinely denies that. Its mission in Geneva and embassy in China did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment. "Your money ⁠is safe and we're covering every loss," Teng said on X. "Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual." "It's the biggest hack in history," Aravind Srinivasan at market maker GSR said as crypto prices fell broadly. Shares in crypto exchange Coinbase Global, which said it was unaffected, slid 4.8%, while those of bitcoin buyer ​Strategy fell nearly 6% in extended US trading. An initial investigation suggested the breach ‌may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of Binance's engineers, which let an attacker gain access to one of its systems and make unauthorized withdrawals, Binance said. "Our security team is tracing the full attack path through the compromised computer which may be the entry point of the incident," Binance said. Later, the company added it had uncovered additional points of breach. Mark Karpeles, former chief of defunct Tokyo-based bitcoin exchange Mt Gox, which collapsed a dozen years ago after $500 million in bitcoin was stolen, said attackers probably accessed private keys for at least two Binance wallets. "Binance appears to have split its assets across multiple systems, ensuring a hack can only affect a part of the assets, but even so a single hack is a large loss," he said. Beyond the potential loss of assets, the security breach was likely to have wider ramifications for the crypto sector, which had already been under pressure ‌due to higher US interest rates and softer demand from exchange-traded fund buyers, analysts said. "It may further dampen risk appetite and ​prompt investors to reassess the safety of assets held on centralised exchanges," said Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group, based in Hong ​Kong. Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, ​has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of its 2025 annual report. Stablecoin issuer Tether said it had frozen nearly $1.57 billion in assets ‌linked to the incident, while Circle froze more than $800 million. World Liberty Financial said it ​worked with custodian BitGo to freeze funds, and Binance co-founder ​Yi He said $27 million in stablecoins and about $2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen. Last year, attackers stole $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks, according to researchers at TRM Labs. In September, Bitget said roughly $350 million in crypto had been stolen from its platform, underscoring the industry's ​vulnerability to hackers. “Binance is such a behemoth in crypto that any hit to confidence in them is a hit to confidence in the industry as a whole, especially as people have already been skittish over the increasing cyber capabilities of AI.”

“We have worked with blockchain partners to freeze affected assets, with ~US$3 billion frozen on-chain so far.”

An emergency insurance and reserve fund from Binance called the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) was established in 2018 to serve a backstop for customers in “extreme situations,” according to the exchange.
The SAFU is generally maintained at around US$1 billion, but has fluctuated in the past in tandem with market movements, Binance said in 2024.

The company said it will cover all losses and “user funds are safe.” Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs said North Korea was behind the heist, which it called “the largest crypto theft on record.” “TRM attributes the attack to TraderTraitor, North Korea’s elite hacking unit, based on robust on and off-chain intelligence,” the firm said. “We make this judgment with high confidence.” Before now, the biggest publicly known crypto hack occurred at exchange Bybit in February 2025, in which attackers made off with almost US$1.5 billion of tokens. They seemingly gained access to the exchange’s systems and used internal software to authorise transfers across 10 different blockchains, including Bitcoin and Ethereum, it said. Binance said the incident may involve a compromised software engineer’s laptop. “We have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak,” the company said. An emergency insurance and reserve fund from Binance called the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) was established in 2018 to serve a backstop for customers in “extreme situations,” according to the exchange. The SAFU is generally maintained at around US$1 billion, but has fluctuated in the past in tandem with market movements, Binance said in 2024. The two biggest stablecoin issuers said they took steps to freeze missing currency. Paolo Ardoino, the chief executive officer of Tether, said in an X post that it froze more than US$1.5 billion of the stablecoin “related to a potential Binance exchange hack.” Jeremy Allaire, who runs Circle Internet Group, said US$800 million of its coin had been frozen amid “reports of a potential exploit involving Binance.” Sentiment was already fragile after a spate of crypto security incidents. In recent months, hundreds of millions of dollars were drained from Bitget , while tampering tied to Ledger devices also led to millions of dollars in losses. “Attackers are operating at unprecedented speed and scale” but “the tools to track and trace operate at that speed too,” said Ari Redbord, global head of policy at TRM Labs. “Stablecoin issuers freeze within hours. Investigators follow funds across chains in real time.” Traders had already been bracing for greater volatility in the crypto market this week, with US$11 billion in options set to expire on Friday. This comes days ahead of the US midterm elections taking place next week, when Democrats could potentially retake one or both chambers of Congress and open the door to greater regulatory scrutiny for the industry. Exchange thefts and malfeasance have been an ever-present backdrop of crypto’s almost two-decade ascent, the most famous of which was the collapse of Sam Bankman-Fried’s FTX in November 2022. In what remains perhaps the most notorious hacking incident, Japan-based Bitcoin exchange Mt. Gox was struck in 2011. Over time, the hackers made off with tokens worth billions of dollars based on the current market price. Mt. Gox eventually went bankrupt. “It’s a huge damage to crypto because of the consistent successful hacks in the space,” said Tian Zeng, chief executive officer of crypto hedge fund Third Eye. “The fact that exploits keep happening makes it dangerous in the age of newest AI models being released every two weeks.” The Binance incident came on the same day event-contract venue Polymarket halted trading on its international exchange for an hour after it said that a third-party software provider was compromised. More than 700 Polymarket users were drained of US$2.7 million in funds, said blockchain analytics platform Bubblemaps, in a post on X. A spokesman declined to comment on the numbers. Recent security incidents haven’t been confined to crypto firms. South Korea’s Daishin Securities disclosed a data leak affecting about 38,000 customers this week, and Mirae Asset Global Investments reported a hacking incident, Yonhap reported. passages: NEW YORK: Cryptocurrency platform Binance said on Thursday it had been hit by a major hack affecting about $6.3 billion in funds, around half of which has been frozen to prevent theft.

The world’s largest crypto exchange by daily trading volume posted a series of sometimes contradictory messages on X, saying “user funds are completely safe” but also that it would “cover all losses”.
That is four times the previous record for such an attack, the $1.5 billion stolen from the Bybit platform in February last year, which was attributed to hackers linked to North Korea.

Tether chief Paolo Ardoino said his company had frozen about $1.6 billion of its USDT stablecoin “related to a potential Binance exchange hack”, and Circle chief Jeremy Allaire said his firm had frozen more than $800 million in USDC.
Stablecoins are digital currencies pegged to a traditional currency, in this case the US dollar.
The US Justice Department and FBI did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
The figure “may continue to increase” as it works to trace and freeze more assets, it said.
An initial investigation suggested the hackers used a compromised laptop belonging to a “DevOps engineer” to access a “service container” and carry out unauthorized withdrawals, Binance said.
“We have found no evidence of any private key leaks from wallets,” it said, promising a detailed technical analysis once the investigation is complete.
“It does look like a hack on Binance,” said former chief executive Changpeng Zhao, who remains majority shareholder.
Most major cryptocurrencies fell on the news.

At about 0400 GMT, bitcoin and Ethereum were down 0.8 percent, after falling nearly 5 percent and 6 percent respectively, while Binance’s BNB token was up 2.7 percent after a plunge of nearly 10 percent. — AFP

sources.title: Hackers steal $6.3 billion from Binance in world's biggest crypto heist - Yahoo Finance
passages: SINGAPORE/TOKYO Oct 30 (Reuters) - Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a record theft that analysts pinned on North Korea and said could shake faith in digital assets.

TRM said the attackers were able to order wallets that Binance uses to empty into hacker-controlled wallets, mirroring a 2025 heist at crypto exchange Bybit, which the US Federal Bureau of Investigation attributed to North Korea.

World Liberty Financial said it ​worked with custodian BitGo to freeze funds, and Binance co-founder ​Yi He said $27 million in stablecoins and about $2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen.
Crypto firm Ripple also froze roughly $200 million in funds, Yi said.

BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down 5% over the past 24 hours at $709.70, according to CoinGecko, while shaky ​confidence ​hit listed crypto exchange shares.
Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, ​has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of its 2025 annual report.
Binance runs a secure asset fund for users, a $1 billion bitcoin reserve designed to protect customer assets in the event of security breaches, according to its website.
Cryptocurrency prices fell on the news, while Binance halted withdrawals and said it would cover the losses.
"This was a complex attack, and we are doing all we can in coordination with law enforcement to resolve it," Binance ‌said in a post on X.
"Our security team is tracing the full attack path through the compromised computer which may be the entry point of the incident," Binance said.
Later, the company added it had uncovered additional points of breach.

Mark Karpeles, former chief of defunct Tokyo-based bitcoin exchange Mt Gox, which collapsed a dozen years ago after $500 million in bitcoin was stolen, said attackers probably accessed private keys for at least two Binance wallets.
"Binance appears to have split its assets across multiple systems, ensuring a hack can only affect a part of the assets, but even so a single hack is a large loss," he said.
Last year, attackers stole $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks, according to researchers at TRM Labs.
"It's the biggest hack in history," Aravind Srinivasan at market maker GSR said as crypto prices fell broadly.

An initial investigation suggested the breach ‌may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of Binance's engineers, which let an attacker gain access to one of its systems and make unauthorized withdrawals, Binance said.

extraction.body: By Ankur Banerjee, Rocky Swift and Summer Zhen SINGAPORE/TOKYO Oct 30 (Reuters) - Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a record theft that analysts pinned on North Korea and said could shake faith in digital assets. Cryptocurrency prices fell on the news, while Binance halted withdrawals and said it would cover the losses. About half the stolen assets were quickly frozen ‌by stablecoin issuers such as Tether, Circle and the Trump-backed World Liberty Financial. "This was a complex attack, and we are doing all we can in coordination with law enforcement to resolve it," Binance ‌said in a post on X. The exchange said customer funds were safe and that it was working with partners to freeze some of the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It expects to resume withdrawal services in the next 45 hours. It did not mention ​the status of the remaining $3.3 billion. Binance runs a secure asset fund for users, a $1 billion bitcoin reserve designed to protect customer assets in the event of security breaches, according to its website. Co-CEO Teng said that "and company funds" would cover losses. The bulk of the heist unfolded in around 20 minutes beginning late on Thursday and bore similarities to previous large attacks blamed on North Korea, according to US blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis. TRM said the attackers were able to order wallets that Binance uses to empty into hacker-controlled wallets, mirroring a 2025 heist at crypto exchange Bybit, which the US Federal Bureau of Investigation attributed to North Korea. "TRM attributes the attack to ... North Korea's elite hacking unit," the firm said in ‌an analysis of the hack posted to its website. Both TRM and Chainalysis ⁠said they were highly confident North Korea was responsible. North Korea routinely denies that. Its mission in Geneva and embassy in China did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment. "Your money ⁠is safe and we're covering every loss," Teng said on X. "Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual." "It's the biggest hack in history," Aravind Srinivasan at market maker GSR said as crypto prices fell broadly. Bitcoin hit a six-week low of $76,368 and ether fell more than 3% to a two-month low of $2,178 before markets stabilised. BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down 5% over the past 24 hours at $709.70, according to CoinGecko, while shaky ​confidence ​hit listed crypto exchange shares. Shares in crypto exchange Coinbase Global, which said it was unaffected, slid 4.8%, while those of bitcoin buyer ​Strategy fell nearly 6% in extended US trading. An initial investigation suggested the breach ‌may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of Binance's engineers, which let an attacker gain access to one of its systems and make unauthorized withdrawals, Binance said. "Our security team is tracing the full attack path through the compromised computer which may be the entry point of the incident," Binance said. Later, the company added it had uncovered additional points of breach. "This was a complex attack, and we are doing all we can in coordination with law enforcement to resolve it," Binance ‌said in a post on X.

The exchange said customer funds were safe and that it was working with partners to freeze some of the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It expects to resume withdrawal services in the next 45 hours. It did not mention ​the status of the remaining $3.3 billion.
Binance runs a secure asset fund for users, a $1 billion bitcoin reserve designed to protect customer assets in the event of security breaches, according to its website.
Co-CEO Teng said that "and company funds" would cover losses.

The bulk of the heist unfolded in around 20 minutes beginning late on Thursday and bore similarities to previous large attacks blamed on North Korea, according to US blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis.

"TRM attributes the attack to ... North Korea's elite hacking unit," the firm said in ‌an analysis of the hack posted to its website. Both TRM and Chainalysis ⁠said they were highly confident North Korea was responsible.

"Your money ⁠is safe and we're covering every loss," Teng said on X. "Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual."

An initial investigation suggested the breach ‌may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of Binance's engineers, which let an attacker gain access to one of its systems and make unauthorized withdrawals, Binance said.

extraction.body: By Ankur Banerjee, Rocky Swift and Summer Zhen SINGAPORE/TOKYO Oct 30 (Reuters) - Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a record theft that analysts pinned on North Korea and said could shake faith in digital assets. Cryptocurrency prices fell on the news, while Binance halted withdrawals and said it would cover the losses. About half the stolen assets were quickly frozen ‌by stablecoin issuers such as Tether, Circle and the Trump-backed World Liberty Financial. "This was a complex attack, and we are doing all we can in coordination with law enforcement to resolve it," Binance ‌said in a post on X. The exchange said customer funds were safe and that it was working with partners to freeze some of the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It expects to resume withdrawal services in the next 45 hours. It did not mention ​the status of the remaining $3.3 billion. Binance runs a secure asset fund for users, a $1 billion bitcoin reserve designed to protect customer assets in the event of security breaches, according to its website. Co-CEO Teng said that "and company funds" would cover losses. The bulk of the heist unfolded in around 20 minutes beginning late on Thursday and bore similarities to previous large attacks blamed on North Korea, according to US blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis. TRM said the attackers were able to order wallets that Binance uses to empty into hacker-controlled wallets, mirroring a 2025 heist at crypto exchange Bybit, which the US Federal Bureau of Investigation attributed to North Korea. "TRM attributes the attack to ... North Korea's elite hacking unit," the firm said in ‌an analysis of the hack posted to its website. Both TRM and Chainalysis ⁠said they were highly confident North Korea was responsible. North Korea routinely denies that. Its mission in Geneva and embassy in China did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment. "Your money ⁠is safe and we're covering every loss," Teng said on X. "Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual." "It's the biggest hack in history," Aravind Srinivasan at market maker GSR said as crypto prices fell broadly. Bitcoin hit a six-week low of $76,368 and ether fell more than 3% to a two-month low of $2,178 before markets stabilised. BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down 5% over the past 24 hours at $709.70, according to CoinGecko, while shaky ​confidence ​hit listed crypto exchange shares. Shares in crypto exchange Coinbase Global, which said it was unaffected, slid 4.8%, while those of bitcoin buyer ​Strategy fell nearly 6% in extended US trading. An initial investigation suggested the breach ‌may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of Binance's engineers, which let an attacker gain access to one of its systems and make unauthorized withdrawals, Binance said. "Our security team is tracing the full attack path through the compromised computer which may be the entry point of the incident," Binance said. Later, the company added it had uncovered additional points of breach. Mark Karpeles, former chief of defunct Tokyo-based bitcoin exchange Mt Gox, which collapsed a dozen years ago after $500 million in bitcoin was stolen, said attackers probably accessed private keys for at least two Binance wallets. "Binance appears to have split its assets across multiple systems, ensuring a hack can only affect a part of the assets, but even so a single hack is a large loss," he said. Beyond the potential loss of assets, the security breach was likely to have wider ramifications for the crypto sector, which had already been under pressure ‌due to higher US interest rates and softer demand from exchange-traded fund buyers, analysts said. "It may further dampen risk appetite and ​prompt investors to reassess the safety of assets held on centralised exchanges," said Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group, based in Hong ​Kong. Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, ​has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of its 2025 annual report. "This was a complex attack, and we are doing all we can in coordination with law enforcement to resolve it," Binance ‌said in a post on X.

Binance runs a secure asset fund for users, a $1 billion bitcoin reserve designed to protect customer assets in the event of security breaches, according to its website.
Co-CEO Teng said that "and company funds" would cover losses.

"TRM attributes the attack to ... North Korea's elite hacking unit," the firm said in ‌an analysis of the hack posted to its website. Both TRM and Chainalysis ⁠said they were highly confident North Korea was responsible.

"Your money ⁠is safe and we're covering every loss," Teng said on X. "Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual."
