TRM said the attackers were able to order wallets that Binance uses to empty into hacker-controlled wallets, mirroring a 2025 heist at crypto exchange Bybit, which the US Federal Bureau of Investigation attributed to North Korea.

World Liberty Financial said it ​worked with custodian BitGo to freeze funds, and Binance co-founder ​Yi He said $27 million in stablecoins and about $2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen.

BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down 5% over the past 24 hours at $709.70, according to CoinGecko, while shaky ​confidence ​hit listed crypto exchange shares.
Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, ​has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of its 2025 annual report.
Binance runs a secure asset fund for users, a $1 billion bitcoin reserve designed to protect customer assets in the event of security breaches, according to its website.
Cryptocurrency prices fell on the news, while Binance halted withdrawals and said it would cover the losses.
"This was a complex attack, and we are doing all we can in coordination with law enforcement to resolve it," Binance ‌said in a post on X.
"Our security team is tracing the full attack path through the compromised computer which may be the entry point of the incident," Binance said.
Later, the company added it had uncovered additional points of breach.

Mark Karpeles, former chief of defunct Tokyo-based bitcoin exchange Mt Gox, which collapsed a dozen years ago after $500 million in bitcoin was stolen, said attackers probably accessed private keys for at least two Binance wallets.
"Binance appears to have split its assets across multiple systems, ensuring a hack can only affect a part of the assets, but even so a single hack is a large loss," he said.
"It's the biggest hack in history," Aravind Srinivasan at market maker GSR said as crypto prices fell broadly.

An initial investigation suggested the breach ‌may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of Binance's engineers, which let an attacker gain access to one of its systems and make unauthorized withdrawals, Binance said.

extraction.body: The world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange said investigations into the 'security incident' are ongoing The world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, Binance, is believed to have become the victim of the largest hack in history. The company announced that a 'security incident' had led to cybercriminals swiping digital assets worth more than six billion dollars - although it has insisted 'user funds are safe' and that it will 'cover all losses'. It is believed to be one of the most significant security incidents on record and has left crypto investors quaking. Binance, which is an online platform where people can buy, sell and trade virtual currencies, announced it had been compromised on Thursday (29 October). According to its website, more than 335 million people across the world are registered users. In a series of social media posts, the firm which describes itself as the 'worlds most trusted' cryptocurrency exchange explained what it knows so far. It was not immediately clear the extent of the damage hackers might have been able to cause, and Binance had not explicitly confirmed that funds had been taken. The company said its teams are 'working around the clock' to resolve the issue which forced it to temporarily suspend deposits and withdrawals. A Binance spokesperson said: "Rest assured that user funds are completely safe. "Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information." In a post shared to X last night, Binance said initial investigations suggest that a 'compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop' is believed to be to blame. This 'allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorised withdrawal transactions', according to the crypto giant. The statement went on: "We have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak. We will share a detailed technical post-mortem once the investigation is complete and the facts are fully verified. "The estimated total impact sits at around $6.3B. We have worked with blockchain partners to freeze affected assets, with ~$3 billion frozen on-chain so far. "Binance will cover all losses from the SAFU fund and the company’s funds. User funds are safe. We will also publish an updated Proof of Reserves once the remediation is complete." Users were urged to 'remain cautious of scams' and wary of 'unofficial links, messages, or requests for account information' Binance explained it has temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals, revoked the affected address authorisation, while calling upon law enforcement and blockchain intelligence partners to trace and recover the funds 'as an immediate precaution'. The cryptocurrency exchange said it will share more technical details once the investigation is complete and when the facts are 'fully verified'. Crypto firm Ripple also froze roughly $200 million in funds, Yi said.

Binance runs a secure asset fund for users, a $1 billion bitcoin reserve designed to protect customer assets in the event of security breaches, according to its website.

Mark Karpeles, former chief of defunct Tokyo-based bitcoin exchange Mt Gox, which collapsed a dozen years ago after $500 million in bitcoin was stolen, said attackers probably accessed private keys for at least two Binance wallets.
"Binance appears to have split its assets across multiple systems, ensuring a hack can only affect a part of the assets, but even so a single hack is a large loss," he said.

TRM said the attackers were able to order wallets that Binance uses to empty into hacker-controlled wallets, mirroring a 2025 heist at crypto exchange Bybit, which the US Federal Bureau of Investigation attributed to North Korea. "TRM attributes the attack to ... North Korea's elite hacking unit," the firm said in ‌an analysis of the hack posted to its website. Both TRM and Chainalysis ⁠said they were highly confident North Korea was responsible. North Korea routinely denies that. Its mission in Geneva and embassy in China did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment. "Your money ⁠is safe and we're covering every loss," Teng said on X. An initial investigation suggested the breach ‌may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of Binance's engineers, which let an attacker gain access to one of its systems and make unauthorized withdrawals, Binance said. "Our security team is tracing the full attack path through the compromised computer which may be the entry point of the incident," Binance said. The company announced that a 'security incident' had led to cybercriminals swiping digital assets worth more than six billion dollars - although it has insisted 'user funds are safe' and that it will 'cover all losses'. It is believed to be one of the most significant security incidents on record and has left crypto investors quaking. Binance, which is an online platform where people can buy, sell and trade virtual currencies, announced it had been compromised on Thursday (29 October). According to its website, more than 335 million people across the world are registered users. In a series of social media posts, the firm which describes itself as the 'worlds most trusted' cryptocurrency exchange explained what it knows so far. It was not immediately clear the extent of the damage hackers might have been able to cause, and Binance had not explicitly confirmed that funds had been taken. The company said its teams are 'working around the clock' to resolve the issue which forced it to temporarily suspend deposits and withdrawals. A Binance spokesperson said: "Rest assured that user funds are completely safe. "Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information." In a post shared to X last night, Binance said initial investigations suggest that a 'compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop' is believed to be to blame. This 'allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorised withdrawal transactions', according to the crypto giant. The statement went on: "We have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak. We will share a detailed technical post-mortem once the investigation is complete and the facts are fully verified. "The estimated total impact sits at around $6.3B. We have worked with blockchain partners to freeze affected assets, with ~$3 billion frozen on-chain so far. "Binance will cover all losses from the SAFU fund and the company’s funds. User funds are safe. We will also publish an updated Proof of Reserves once the remediation is complete." Users were urged to 'remain cautious of scams' and wary of 'unofficial links, messages, or requests for account information' Binance explained it has temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals, revoked the affected address authorisation, while calling upon law enforcement and blockchain intelligence partners to trace and recover the funds 'as an immediate precaution'. The cryptocurrency exchange said it will share more technical details once the investigation is complete and when the facts are 'fully verified'. extraction.body: French AI company Mistral has released the weights for its trillion-parameter open source AI model Mistral Large 4 (ML4), allowing businesses and governments to download and deploy the system themselves. Nicknamed “Le Chonk,” the model was first introduced earlier this month . The release comes as competition between open-weight AI developers like Mistral and closed-model providers like OpenAI and Anthropic heats up, with the former arguing that businesses and governments shouldn’t have to rely on outside AI companies for access to advanced capabilities. That argument may hold more weight in cybersecurity, where organizations want more control over their data and systems. Or, as Mistral’s CEO, Arthur Mensch, explained, AI should “be a tool for empowerment, not dominance.” With Chonk, Mistral doubles down on that position, arguing that it’s able to achieve “state-of-the-art performance” at a “fraction of the compute and capital committed by closed labs.” The release of the model’s weights — the numerical training that animates the system — ensures that other companies and government agencies will now be able to deploy ML4 for their own purposes. Mistral says that its model is comparable in terms of performance with a Chinese open-weight competitor, GLM-5.3, which was previously considered one of the best open-weight models in the world — particularly when it comes to cyber work. However, Mistral’s model uses 47 percent fewer tokens per task, making it significantly more economical than GLM-5.3. The company also claims that the model outranks all other open models when it comes to agentic coding tasks on Artificial Analysis’ Coding Agent Index, an AI benchmarking site. “Amid growing cyber threats, ML4 brings state-of-the-art sovereign cyber defense capabilities to enterprises and governments globally,” the company said Thursday. “Enterprise and public sector institutions can now download, deploy, and own frontier AI to detect, analyze, and respond to threats across code and IT infrastructure.” The weights for ML4 are being made available on Hugging Face and via its API. Pierre Stock, Vice President of Science at Mistral, told TechCrunch that the release of the model’s weights meant that organizations will have more control over how they use AI to defend themselves. “Concretely, it means that, for instance, as a business company or as a government, you’re able to have access to frontier intelligence to defend yourselves against cyberattacks. Access that can’t be cut off by definition because the model is open-weighted,” he said. Stock added that the model could be used to “identify, coordinate, and respond in real time to major security incidents, and that the open sourcing means that companies can deploy this model on-prem in their own ecosystem. While advances in AI cybersecurity are helping security professionals to find bugs at a much higher rate than before, Stock continued, he believes it’s important for companies to “provide [this same] capability to everyone…as soon as possible to ramp up and to strengthen the ecosystem,” given that “some malicious actors might try to actually leverage their own technology to attack.” Separately, Stock addressed concerns about recent incidents involving rogue AI agents, acknowledging the risks but cautioning against overreacting. “We don’t want to fearmonger people. We think it’s a problem that is solvable. It’s a hard problem to have good security,” he said. The company published the open-weight model as a 1 trillion-parameter, natively multimodal system, and its pitch leans hard on cyber defense instead of general chat.
Mistral reported that Large 4 scores 51% on the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index, a third-party benchmark.
Independent indices carry more weight than a lab’s internal tests, so this figure deserves attention.
A raw percentage still tells you little without the comparison set, and the fact sheet we hold does not include scores for rival models on the same index.
Open-weight releases have become the main battleground between labs that sell hosted access and labs that hand customers the files.
This analysis walks through what Mistral confirmed, what the numbers do and do not prove, and who gains or loses from putting a cyber-capable model in everyone’s hands.
A staged rollout like that gives a lab time to gather feedback, harden safeguards and brief partners before the files become permanent public property.
It also lets competitors read the preview and prepare responses.
Mistral built its reputation in Europe by shipping open models while US rivals kept their best systems behind APIs.
Large 4 pushes that approach to the trillion-parameter scale and adds an explicit cyber focus.
Open-weight AI has moved from a hobbyist niche to a core piece of national and corporate strategy within a few years.
Open weights build trust and adoption, while the API and enterprise support line up the revenue.
The company has not published financial details about Large 4, and we make no claims about them.
Several questions remain open at publication time.
Mistral’s cited materials give no API price.
We also found no independent reproduction of the 82% vulnerability result or the 96.6% refusal figure.
Those two sentences capture the whole debate.
Stock defends openness as a principle, and he concedes that a downloaded file cannot be recalled.
Mistral calls the model “Le Chonk” in its own announcement.
It first previewed the system on October 6, so the gap between preview and public weights came to 23 days.
Mistral described Large 4 as “one of the world’s strongest AI models for cybersecurity.” It also says the model tells defensive security tasks apart from malicious, offensive ones.
That second claim carries most of the weight in the sales pitch, because a model that helps a defender patch a bug can, in principle, help an attacker write an exploit for the same bug.
We hold no verified head-to-head scores, so we will not invent a leaderboard.
Benchmarks will decide how fast that pressure builds.
If independent labs confirm the 51% and 82% figures, procurement teams will start adding Large 4 to shortlists.
If the numbers shrink under neutral testing, the launch will read as a strong marketing move on top of a decent model.
A common pattern is a hosted frontier model for general work and a self-hosted open model for anything that touches secrets, source code or incident data.
That split shapes who actually benefits from the open weights in the first year.
The honest framing is that open weights trade vendor-side guardrails for customer-side control, and each buyer must decide which risk they fear more.
You can see that framing in the ZDNET report on the weights release .
The confirmed hardware-agnostic specs are short but significant.
That design lets a lab claim a trillion parameters without paying the compute bill of a dense trillion-parameter model on every request.
It also handles text and other inputs natively, rather than bolting a vision module onto a language model afterward.
If large customers self-host, hyperscalers still win GPU rental revenue, but they lose the model margin that sits on top.
Expect cloud platforms to list Large 4 in their model catalogs quickly, since refusing to would push customers elsewhere.
Readers should treat the number as a snapshot.
Benchmarks in this area move quickly, since labs tune for them and new tasks get added.
A 51% score means the model passes about half of what the index asks, and the index itself defines what counts as success.

extraction.body: Mistral AI put the weights of Mistral Large 4 online on October 29, 2026, and the French lab aimed the release squarely at security teams. The company published the open-weight model as a 1 trillion-parameter, natively multimodal system, and its pitch leans hard on cyber defense instead of general chat. Reuters reported the release under the headline Mistral AI publicly releases Large 4, targets cybersecurity users . Mistral calls the model “Le Chonk” in its own announcement. It first previewed the system on October 6, so the gap between preview and public weights came to 23 days. That timing matters. Open-weight releases have become the main battleground between labs that sell hosted access and labs that hand customers the files. Our open-weight model license comparison covered six families before this launch, and Large 4 now adds a new heavyweight to that list. This analysis walks through what Mistral confirmed, what the numbers do and do not prove, and who gains or loses from putting a cyber-capable model in everyone’s hands. The release has two parts. Mistral posted the model weights for download on Hugging Face, and it also serves the same model through its own API. Developers who want to run the system on their own hardware can pull the files. Teams that prefer a hosted endpoint can call it the usual way. Mistral framed the move in plain terms in its announcement: “We release the weights of Le Chonk, advancing the frontier of open models in agentic coding and cybersecurity.” The sentence names two target workloads, and neither is casual conversation. Agentic coding means a model that writes, runs and fixes code across many steps. Cybersecurity means finding, reproducing and patching software flaws. Mistral also described the model as the best open agentic coding model in the world, according to its official materials. It said enterprises and governments get “frontier AI cyber defence capabilities they can fully own and control.” Those are company claims, and independent reviewers will need weeks to test them. Still, the framing tells you who Mistral wants as customers: security operations teams, public agencies and regulated firms that cannot send sensitive code to a third-party cloud. One detail remains unconfirmed. Mistral’s cited release materials do not state a price for API access, so any per-token figure circulating today lacks a source. We will update this report if Mistral publishes rates. The confirmed hardware-agnostic specs are short but significant. Large 4 uses a Mixture-of-Experts architecture, which means only part of the network activates for each token. That design lets a lab claim a trillion parameters without paying the compute bill of a dense trillion-parameter model on every request. It also handles text and other inputs natively, rather than bolting a vision module onto a language model afterward. A 1M context window changes what a security workflow can look like. A reviewer can feed an entire mid-sized codebase, its dependency manifest and a stack of recent advisories into one prompt. Whether the model keeps its accuracy at that length is a separate question that only independent testing will answer. Mistral has not published a long-context accuracy curve in the materials we reviewed. The size also sets a practical floor for self-hosting. A model with a trillion parameters needs serious multi-GPU infrastructure even when only a fraction of the experts fire per token. Small teams will most likely use the API, while governments, large banks and telecom carriers can justify the cluster. That split shapes who actually benefits from the open weights in the first year. Mistral described Large 4 as “one of the world’s strongest AI models for cybersecurity.” It also says the model tells defensive security tasks apart from malicious, offensive ones. That second claim carries most of the weight in the sales pitch, because a model that helps a defender patch a bug can, in principle, help an attacker write an exploit for the same bug. Mistral co-founder Guillaume Lample made the strategic case in launch coverage. He said the cyber defense capabilities will let enterprises and governments defend themselves against threat actors who are jailbreaking closed models to perform cyberattacks. The argument runs like this: attackers already have access to capable models through jailbreaks, so defenders deserve a model they can run, inspect and tune on their own terms. Based on Mistral’s official framing, three buyer groups stand out. Security operations centers want faster triage and patch drafting. Software vendors want automated bug reproduction before a release ships. Government agencies want a model that never leaves their network. Each group values control over raw leaderboard rank, which explains why Mistral led with ownership language instead of a speed claim. Mistral reported that Large 4 scores 51% on the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index, a third-party benchmark. Independent indices carry more weight than a lab’s internal tests, so this figure deserves attention. A raw percentage still tells you little without the comparison set, and the fact sheet we hold does not include scores for rival models on the same index. It assumes the refusal rate is a simple average across the test prompts. Even if that is true, a defender can live with a small leak, while a determined attacker only needs one useful answer. A model has to read the bug report, build or locate a failing input and prove the flaw triggers, and only then write a fix that removes it without breaking the rest of the program. That end-to-end shape matters more than a multiple-choice security quiz. Real defenders spend most of their time on exactly this loop. They confirm that a reported flaw is real, they judge its reach and they ship a patch that maintainers will accept. Lample’s point about jailbreaks is real, and our report on DeepSeek and Moonshot’s use of GPT-6 Astra showed how capabilities travel even when access is gated. Neither route gives perfect control. A model has to read the bug report, build or locate a failing input and prove the flaw triggers, and only then write a fix that removes it without breaking the rest of the program.

That end-to-end shape matters more than a multiple-choice security quiz. Real defenders spend most of their time on exactly this loop. They confirm that a reported flaw is real, they judge its reach and they ship a patch that maintainers will accept. A model that automates even part of it could cut the queue of open advisories that every security team complains about.

Closed models face their own leak. Lample’s point about jailbreaks is real, and our report on DeepSeek and Moonshot’s use of GPT-6 Astra showed how capabilities travel even when access is gated. Neither route gives perfect control. The honest framing is that open weights trade vendor-side guardrails for customer-side control, and each buyer must decide which risk they fear more.

Mistral executives did not dodge the downside. Pierre Stock, Mistral’s Vice President of Science, told Reuters: “I’m not comfortable living in a world in which open weights do not exist.” He also acknowledged the flip side of a public release. Once the model is out, he said, “it’s impossible to contain access.”

Those two sentences capture the whole debate. Stock defends openness as a principle, and he concedes that a downloaded file cannot be recalled. Fortune reported a related claim from him after the launch, that Large 4 is the best open-weight model on cyber and coding. Read together, the comments show a company that knows the trade and has decided to accept it, in a Fortune report on the launch that frames the model as a top open option for agentic coding and cyber defense.

Governments are watching the same trade from the other side. Our piece on China’s open-weight AI as weapon or armour lays out how one major power treats open releases as strategy. A Western lab shipping a cyber-capable trillion-parameter model changes the terms of that argument, because the same capability now sits in both camps.

The practical effect is a faster diffusion of skill. Before this week, a mid-tier attacker needed to rent hosted access or jailbreak it. Now the attacker can download a strong model, though running one at this size still takes real hardware and money. That cost barrier filters out hobbyists but not funded groups, and defenders should plan accordingly.

Many large buyers will end up with both. A common pattern is a hosted frontier model for general work and a self-hosted open model for anything that touches secrets, source code or incident data. Large 4 gives that second slot a credible occupant for the first time at this capability tier.

ZDNET’s headline on the launch says Mistral’s Le Chonk is now a top open model for coding, ranking alongside Codex GPT-6.1 Terra. You can see that framing in the ZDNET report on the weights release . The comparison puts an open model in the same sentence as a leading closed coding product, which would have sounded optimistic a year ago.

We hold no verified head-to-head scores, so we will not invent a leaderboard. What we can say is that the open-weight field now has several serious entrants. Our earlier DeepSeek vs Qwen vs Mistral comparison mapped the options before Large 4 landed, and the new release raises the bar for all three families.

The competitive pressure runs in two directions. Open-weight rivals must now answer on cyber tasks specifically, an area many of them skipped in their launch material. Closed vendors must justify their premium to buyers who can see a near-peer they can run themselves. Neither group can ignore a trillion-parameter model with a 1M window and a published cyber score.

Benchmarks will decide how fast that pressure builds. If independent labs confirm the 51% and 82% figures, procurement teams will start adding Large 4 to shortlists. If the numbers shrink under neutral testing, the launch will read as a strong marketing move on top of a decent model.

Mistral previewed Large 4 on October 6, 2026, and shipped the weights 23 days later. A staged rollout like that gives a lab time to gather feedback, harden safeguards and brief partners before the files become permanent public property. It also lets competitors read the preview and prepare responses.

The release also fits a longer pattern. Mistral built its reputation in Europe by shipping open models while US rivals kept their best systems behind APIs. Large 4 pushes that approach to the trillion-parameter scale and adds an explicit cyber focus. Open-weight AI has moved from a hobbyist niche to a core piece of national and corporate strategy within a few years.

Cybersecurity makes the move sharper than a general model release. A chatbot that writes a clumsy poem harms nobody. A model that can reproduce and patch a real vulnerability sits near the same tools that find and weaponize one. That dual-use shadow explains why the same week produced both enthusiastic coverage and pointed questions about containment.

Cloud providers face a subtler effect. If large customers self-host, hyperscalers still win GPU rental revenue, but they lose the model margin that sits on top. Expect cloud platforms to list Large 4 in their model catalogs quickly, since refusing to would push customers elsewhere. We could not confirm any such listing at publication time, so treat that as an expectation and not a report.

Mistral itself gets a different payoff. Open weights build trust and adoption, while the API and enterprise support line up the revenue. The company has not published financial details about Large 4, and we make no claims about them.

Several questions remain open at publication time. Mistral’s cited materials give no API price. They do not list rival scores on the Cyber Index in the sources we reviewed. We also found no independent reproduction of the 82% vulnerability result or the 96.6% refusal figure.

Mistral framed the move in plain terms in its announcement: “We release the weights of Le Chonk, advancing the frontier of open models in agentic coding and cybersecurity.” The sentence names two target workloads, and neither is casual conversation. Agentic coding means a model that writes, runs and fixes code across many steps. Cybersecurity means finding, reproducing and patching software flaws. Mistral also described the model as the best open agentic coding model in the world, according to its official materials. We will update this report if Mistral publishes rates. The confirmed hardware-agnostic specs are short but significant. passages: Bitcoin fell on Friday as concerns over a $6.3 billion hack at cryptocurrency exchange Binance, by far the biggest in crypto on record, rattled digital asset markets.
Ether , the second-largest cryptocurrency by market capitalization, dropped 4% to $2,239.80 while Binance's native token, BNB, tumbled 5% to $702.28.
Binance co-founder Yi He said deposits remained unaffected and continued to operate normally, while the exchange was working on enhancements to its withdrawal service and related address controls.
It expects to begin resuming withdrawal services within the next 48 hours.
—CNBC's Jenny Lee, Liz Napolitano and Davis Giangiulio contributed to this report.

extraction.body: Bitcoin fell on Friday as concerns over a $6.3 billion hack at cryptocurrency exchange Binance, by far the biggest in crypto on record, rattled digital asset markets. The world's largest cryptocurrency fell 4% to $77,465.05. Ether , the second-largest cryptocurrency by market capitalization, dropped 4% to $2,239.80 while Binance's native token, BNB, tumbled 5% to $702.28. Defying the broader sell-off, Hyperliquid's HYPE token surged 9% to $92.67. Binance said Friday that a security incident had an estimated impact of $6.3 billion, with around $3 billion in cryptocurrency assets frozen so far, and pledged to cover all losses. The world's largest crypto exchange said an initial investigation suggests "the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions." Binance co-founder Yi He said deposits remained unaffected and continued to operate normally, while the exchange was working on enhancements to its withdrawal service and related address controls. It expects to begin resuming withdrawal services within the next 48 hours. The developments have renewed concerns over security vulnerabilities in the cryptocurrency industry, which has suffered a string of major breaches in recent years. In 2025, cryptocurrency exchange Bybit suffered a roughly $1.5 billion hack, while rival Bitget more recently lost over $350 million in digital assets to cyber theft. —CNBC's Jenny Lee, Liz Napolitano and Davis Giangiulio contributed to this report. sources.title: Binance hack rattles markets as BNB falls 8%, Bitcoin nears $77K - TradingView
passages: Cryptocurrency markets extended their decline early Friday following the Binance hack, with BNB down more than 8% over 24 hours and Bitcoin trading near $77,000.
BNB, the native token of BNB Chain, traded near $693, down around 8.2%, according to CoinGecko data at the time of writing.
Bitcoin fell 4.8% to about $77,131, while Ether declined 5.7% to about $2,217.
Binance pledged to cover all losses from the hack and suspended all deposits and withdrawals while conducting security checks.
In a subsequent update, the exchange put the verified total of frozen assets at around $3 billion, up from its earlier figure of $2.54 billion.

Binance pledged to cover all losses from the hack and suspended all deposits and withdrawals while conducting security checks. In a subsequent update, the exchange put the verified total of frozen assets at around $3 billion, up from its earlier figure of $2.54 billion. Decentralized finance tokens also declined. sources.title: Binance hack could be the biggest in history; here's what we know
passages: BNB, the token initially launched as Binance Coin for paying Binance fees, saw a decrease of over 8% in the past 24 hours, trading at $694, according to market aggregator CoinGecko.The potential hacking incident, which analytics firm Chainalysis suggests could be the largest cryptocurrency heist to date, had an immediate impact on the market during early Asian trading on Friday.In extended US trading, crypto exchange Coinbase Global dropped by 4.8%, and shares of bitcoin buyer Strategy fell nearly 6%.

This action was taken in conjunction with stablecoin issuers Circle and Tether, who also froze related assets.Binance indicated that the amount of frozen assets could rise as it collaborates with law enforcement agencies, token issuers, blockchain intelligence firms, and other industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets.Changpeng Zhao, founder of Binance, who is no longer in charge of the company, remarked in a post on X that the situation "looked like a hack."As per a Reuters report, with over 335 million registered users worldwide, Binance facilitates the buying, selling, and trading of digital assets and reported approximately $160 billion in assets under custody in its 2024 annual report.

As part of the initial agreement, Binance incurred penalties amounting to $4.3 billion, while Zhao faced a personal fine of $50 million.In November 2024, FTX lodged a lawsuit against Binance Holdings Ltd., Zhao, and several other Binance executives, aiming to reclaim nearly $1.8 billion that FTX claims was fraudulently diverted.This case revolves around a stock repurchase transaction from July 2021, during which Binance divested its interests approximately 20% of FTX's international division and 18.4% of its US entity to FTX co-founder Sam Bankman-Fried.Nevertheless, following extensive lobbying efforts with the US Administration, President Donald Trump granted a complete presidential pardon to Changpeng Zhao in October 2025.

In September, the cryptocurrency exchange Bitget reported that approximately $350 million in crypto had been stolen from its platform, highlighting the industry's susceptibility to cybercriminals.Authorities have cautioned that organized crime syndicates are increasingly utilizing cryptocurrencies to transfer funds internationally, circumventing the conventional financial system.Binance.US, a distinct cryptocurrency exchange, stated that it was not impacted by the security breach.

extraction.body: Bitcoin fell on Friday as concerns over a $6.3 billion hack at cryptocurrency exchange Binance, by far the biggest in crypto on record, rattled digital asset markets. The world's largest cryptocurrency fell 4% to $77,465.05. Ether , the second-largest cryptocurrency by market capitalization, dropped 4% to $2,239.80 while Binance's native token, BNB, tumbled 5% to $702.28. Defying the broader sell-off, Hyperliquid's HYPE token surged 9% to $92.67. Binance said Friday that a security incident had an estimated impact of $6.3 billion, with around $3 billion in cryptocurrency assets frozen so far, and pledged to cover all losses. The world's largest crypto exchange said an initial investigation suggests "the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions." Binance co-founder Yi He said deposits remained unaffected and continued to operate normally, while the exchange was working on enhancements to its withdrawal service and related address controls. It expects to begin resuming withdrawal services within the next 48 hours. The developments have renewed concerns over security vulnerabilities in the cryptocurrency industry, which has suffered a string of major breaches in recent years. In 2025, cryptocurrency exchange Bybit suffered a roughly $1.5 billion hack, while rival Bitget more recently lost over $350 million in digital assets to cyber theft. —CNBC's Jenny Lee, Liz Napolitano and Davis Giangiulio contributed to this report. sources.title: Bitcoin tumbles as Binance hack rattles crypto markets - CNBC
passages: Bitcoin fell on Friday as concerns over a $6.3 billion hack at cryptocurrency exchange Binance, by far the biggest in crypto on record, rattled digital asset markets.
Ether , the second-largest cryptocurrency by market capitalization, dropped 4% to $2,239.80 while Binance's native token, BNB, tumbled 5% to $702.28.
Binance co-founder Yi He said deposits remained unaffected and continued to operate normally, while the exchange was working on enhancements to its withdrawal service and related address controls.
It expects to begin resuming withdrawal services within the next 48 hours.
—CNBC's Jenny Lee, Liz Napolitano and Davis Giangiulio contributed to this report.

extraction.body: Bitcoin fell on Friday as concerns over a $6.3 billion hack at cryptocurrency exchange Binance, by far the biggest in crypto on record, rattled digital asset markets. The world's largest cryptocurrency fell 4% to $77,465.05. Ether , the second-largest cryptocurrency by market capitalization, dropped 4% to $2,239.80 while Binance's native token, BNB, tumbled 5% to $702.28. Defying the broader sell-off, Hyperliquid's HYPE token surged 9% to $92.67. Binance said Friday that a security incident had an estimated impact of $6.3 billion, with around $3 billion in cryptocurrency assets frozen so far, and pledged to cover all losses. The world's largest crypto exchange said an initial investigation suggests "the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions." Binance co-founder Yi He said deposits remained unaffected and continued to operate normally, while the exchange was working on enhancements to its withdrawal service and related address controls. It expects to begin resuming withdrawal services within the next 48 hours. The developments have renewed concerns over security vulnerabilities in the cryptocurrency industry, which has suffered a string of major breaches in recent years. In 2025, cryptocurrency exchange Bybit suffered a roughly $1.5 billion hack, while rival Bitget more recently lost over $350 million in digital assets to cyber theft. —CNBC's Jenny Lee, Liz Napolitano and Davis Giangiulio contributed to this report. passages: Cryptocurrency markets extended their decline early Friday following the Binance hack, with BNB down more than 8% over 24 hours and Bitcoin trading near $77,000.
BNB, the native token of BNB Chain, traded near $693, down around 8.2%, according to CoinGecko data at the time of writing.

Binance pledged to cover all losses from the hack and suspended all deposits and withdrawals while conducting security checks.

extraction.body: Bitcoin fell on Friday as concerns over a $6.3 billion hack at cryptocurrency exchange Binance, by far the biggest in crypto on record, rattled digital asset markets. The world's largest cryptocurrency fell 4% to $77,465.05. Ether , the second-largest cryptocurrency by market capitalization, dropped 4% to $2,239.80 while Binance's native token, BNB, tumbled 5% to $702.28. Defying the broader sell-off, Hyperliquid's HYPE token surged 9% to $92.67. Binance said Friday that a security incident had an estimated impact of $6.3 billion, with around $3 billion in cryptocurrency assets frozen so far, and pledged to cover all losses. The world's largest crypto exchange said an initial investigation suggests "the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions." Binance co-founder Yi He said deposits remained unaffected and continued to operate normally, while the exchange was working on enhancements to its withdrawal service and related address controls. It expects to begin resuming withdrawal services within the next 48 hours. The developments have renewed concerns over security vulnerabilities in the cryptocurrency industry, which has suffered a string of major breaches in recent years. In 2025, cryptocurrency exchange Bybit suffered a roughly $1.5 billion hack, while rival Bitget more recently lost over $350 million in digital assets to cyber theft. —CNBC's Jenny Lee, Liz Napolitano and Davis Giangiulio contributed to this report. extraction.body: Binance has frozen assets and halted withdrawals after a security breach impacted an estimated $6.3 billion, prompting intervention from stablecoin issuers to contain the fallout. Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, reported an estimated $6.3 billion impact following a major security breach, marking the most significant financial loss in the history of digital asset platforms. The incident, which the company initially described as a potential security issue, triggered immediate market turbulence and forced the exchange to suspend trading and withdrawals while investigators trace the stolen funds. The breach came to light on October 29, 2026, when on-chain data revealed unauthorized outflows from one of the exchange's hot wallets. According to blockchain analysts, approximately $2.8 billion was rapidly drained from the compromised wallet before Binance could secure its infrastructure. The company subsequently revised its total impact estimate to $6.3 billion, reflecting the broader exposure across multiple asset classes and internal accounts. "We are urgently investigating reports of a potential security issue and are taking immediate action to secure the platform," a Binance spokesperson stated, confirming that the exchange had halted all deposits and withdrawals to prevent further unauthorized transfers. The company has pledged to cover customer losses, a move intended to stabilize user confidence and prevent a broader run on the platform. The sheer scale of the theft prompted rapid intervention from major stablecoin issuers. Circle, the entity behind the USD Coin (USDC), and Tether, the issuer of the dominant USDT stablecoin, confirmed they were actively working to freeze the illicit funds identified on their respective networks. By blacklisting the wallet addresses associated with the hackers, these issuers aim to render the stolen digital assets illiquid and unusable on compliant exchanges. Despite these containment efforts, the broader cryptocurrency market reacted sharply to the news. Bitcoin and other major altcoins experienced immediate price declines as traders priced in the systemic risks associated with centralized exchange custody. The incident has reignited debates over the security protocols of major digital asset custodians, particularly the risks inherent in maintaining large liquidity pools in internet-connected hot wallets. Hot wallets, which are continuously connected to the internet to facilitate rapid trading and withdrawals, have long been considered the weakest link in exchange security architectures. Industry standards dictate that the vast majority of customer assets should be held in offline cold storage, inaccessible to remote cyberattacks. The fact that billions of dollars were exposed in a single hot wallet suggests a significant deviation from standard risk management practices or a catastrophic failure in the exchange's internal authorization controls. Industry veterans have noted that while the $6.3 billion figure is unprecedented for a single exchange hack, it follows a troubling pattern of high-profile breaches that have plagued the sector for over a decade. From the collapse of Mt. Gox to the multi-billion dollar exploits of the Ronin bridge, the crypto industry has repeatedly struggled to secure the infrastructure required to safeguard trillions in user capital. "The final extent of the suspected breach, including any long-term customer losses, is still under investigation," noted one market analyst tracking the on-chain movements. "However, the ability of Binance to absorb this loss without collapsing is a testament to the capital reserves the exchange has built, even if the reputational damage will be severe." Some crypto pioneers have attempted to project calm amid the volatility. One prominent industry figure publicly stated that the hack is "not the end of the world" for the broader ecosystem, arguing that the underlying blockchain networks themselves remain secure and that the failure lies entirely within the centralized intermediary. The hack also underscores the growing sophistication of cybercriminal syndicates targeting financial infrastructure. Security researchers suggest that the attackers may have exploited a vulnerability in the exchange's internal signing protocols or compromised the private keys of senior administrators. The full investigation remains ongoing, with Binance collaborating with global law enforcement and cybersecurity firms to identify the perpetrators. For retail and institutional investors alike, the breach serves as a stark reminder of the counterparty risks embedded in centralized cryptocurrency markets. While the decentralized ethos of blockchain technology promises trustless transactions, the reality of market liquidity relies heavily on a few dominant intermediaries. As regulators worldwide scrutinize the incident, the pressure on exchanges to adopt institutional-grade custody solutions and transparent proof-of-reserves audits is expected to intensify significantly in the coming months. In an industry defined by rapid innovation and extreme volatility, the fallout from this breach will undoubtedly shape the regulatory and operational landscape for digital assets for years to come. extraction.body: The world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, Binance, has estimated the impact of a major security incident at around $6.3 billion after a suspected attack involving unauthorised withdrawal transactions. The company has frozen around $3 billion worth of affected digital assets so far and promised to cover all losses. In its latest update on Friday, Binance said its initial investigation suggested that a DevOps engineer's laptop may have been compromised. Binance said it had found no evidence that any wallet private keys had been leaked. It is continuing its investigation and plans to publish a detailed technical post-mortem once the facts have been verified. Binance's initial investigation suggests that the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions. We have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak. We will share a detailed technical post-mortem once the investigation is complete and the facts are fully verified. The estimated total impact sits at around $6.3B. We have worked with blockchain partners to freeze affected assets, with ~$3 billion frozen on-chain so far. Binance will cover all losses from the SAFU fund and the company’s funds. As an immediate precaution, Binance has: - temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while security checks are completed; - revoked the affected address authorisation; - engaged law enforcement and blockchain intelligence partners to trace and recover funds. Please rely only on official Binance channels for updates. Tether and Circle, two major cryptocurrency companies, have also frozen around $2.4 billion in assets linked to the suspected attack. Bitcoin fell to a six-week low of $77,646 on Friday, while Ether dropped to a two-month low of $2,238.76, according to CoinGecko data cited by Reuters. Binance's native token, BNB, also fell more than 8 per cent over 24 hours to around $694. Binance's initial investigation points to a possible compromise of a DevOps engineer's laptop. According to Binance, the compromised laptop may have allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorised withdrawal transactions. The company has not yet explained how the laptop was compromised or provided a complete technical account of the attack. Importantly, Binance said its investigation had found no evidence of a wallet private-key leak. Private keys are cryptographic credentials that allow users or platforms to authorise transactions and control digital assets stored in blockchain wallets. Binance said it had revoked the affected address authorisation and was working with law enforcement agencies and blockchain intelligence partners to trace and recover the assets. The company will publish a detailed technical post-mortem after its investigation is complete. Binance said the estimated total impact of the incident stood at around $6.3 billion. However, the exchange has so far frozen approximately $3 billion worth of affected assets on-chain. The company is working with blockchain partners, cryptocurrency issuers and law enforcement agencies to identify and freeze additional assets. Two major cryptocurrency companies have also taken action. Tether, the issuer of the USDT stablecoin, said it had frozen around $1.6 billion in assets connected to the potential Binance hack. Circle, which issues the USDC stablecoin, said it had frozen more than $800 million linked to the incident. Together, the two companies have frozen around $2.4 billion in assets. These actions are significant because Tether and Circle issue some of the world's largest dollar-backed stablecoins. Their ability to freeze certain assets can help investigators prevent suspected stolen funds from being moved or converted. The $6.3 billion estimate should not be confused with the amount confirmed as stolen. Binance has not yet provided a final breakdown of the losses, and its investigation is ongoing. Binance has promised to cover all losses arising from the incident. The exchange said it would use its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and its own corporate funds to compensate for any losses.

extraction.body: Binance has frozen assets and halted withdrawals after a security breach impacted an estimated $6.3 billion, prompting intervention from stablecoin issuers to contain the fallout. Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, reported an estimated $6.3 billion impact following a major security breach, marking the most significant financial loss in the history of digital asset platforms. The incident, which the company initially described as a potential security issue, triggered immediate market turbulence and forced the exchange to suspend trading and withdrawals while investigators trace the stolen funds. The breach came to light on October 29, 2026, when on-chain data revealed unauthorized outflows from one of the exchange's hot wallets. According to blockchain analysts, approximately $2.8 billion was rapidly drained from the compromised wallet before Binance could secure its infrastructure. The company subsequently revised its total impact estimate to $6.3 billion, reflecting the broader exposure across multiple asset classes and internal accounts. "We are urgently investigating reports of a potential security issue and are taking immediate action to secure the platform," a Binance spokesperson stated, confirming that the exchange had halted all deposits and withdrawals to prevent further unauthorized transfers. The company has pledged to cover customer losses, a move intended to stabilize user confidence and prevent a broader run on the platform. The sheer scale of the theft prompted rapid intervention from major stablecoin issuers. Circle, the entity behind the USD Coin (USDC), and Tether, the issuer of the dominant USDT stablecoin, confirmed they were actively working to freeze the illicit funds identified on their respective networks. By blacklisting the wallet addresses associated with the hackers, these issuers aim to render the stolen digital assets illiquid and unusable on compliant exchanges. Despite these containment efforts, the broader cryptocurrency market reacted sharply to the news. Bitcoin and other major altcoins experienced immediate price declines as traders priced in the systemic risks associated with centralized exchange custody. The incident has reignited debates over the security protocols of major digital asset custodians, particularly the risks inherent in maintaining large liquidity pools in internet-connected hot wallets. Hot wallets, which are continuously connected to the internet to facilitate rapid trading and withdrawals, have long been considered the weakest link in exchange security architectures. Industry standards dictate that the vast majority of customer assets should be held in offline cold storage, inaccessible to remote cyberattacks. The fact that billions of dollars were exposed in a single hot wallet suggests a significant deviation from standard risk management practices or a catastrophic failure in the exchange's internal authorization controls. Industry veterans have noted that while the $6.3 billion figure is unprecedented for a single exchange hack, it follows a troubling pattern of high-profile breaches that have plagued the sector for over a decade. From the collapse of Mt. Gox to the multi-billion dollar exploits of the Ronin bridge, the crypto industry has repeatedly struggled to secure the infrastructure required to safeguard trillions in user capital. "The final extent of the suspected breach, including any long-term customer losses, is still under investigation," noted one market analyst tracking the on-chain movements. "However, the ability of Binance to absorb this loss without collapsing is a testament to the capital reserves the exchange has built, even if the reputational damage will be severe." Some crypto pioneers have attempted to project calm amid the volatility. passages: Binance said on Thursday that a security breach had affected an estimated $6.3 billion in assets, potentially making it the biggest cryptocurrency heist on record.
The world's largest crypto exchange said it had recovered or frozen about $3 billion, while analysts have pinned the blame for the hack on North Korea.
It expects to resume withdrawal services in the next ​48 hours.

BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down 5% over the past 24 hours at $709.70, according to CoinGecko, while shaky confidence hit listed crypto exchange ‌shares.

TRM said the attackers were able to order wallets that Binance uses to empty into hacker-controlled wallets, mirroring a ⁠2025 heist at crypto exchange Bybit, which the US Federal Bureau of Investigation had attributed to Pyongyang.

Beyond ​the potential loss of assets, the security breach was likely to have wider ramifications for crypto, which had already been under pressure due to ​higher US interest rates and softer demand from exchange-traded fund buyers, analysts said.

World Liberty Financial said it worked with custodian BitGo to freeze funds, and Binance co-founder Yi He said $27 million in ⁠stablecoins and about $2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen.
Crypto firm Ripple also froze roughly $200 million in funds, Yi said.
"Our security team is tracing the full attack path through the compromised computer which may be the entry point of the incident," Binance said.

An initial investigation suggested the breach may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of Binance's engineers, which let an attacker gain ​access to one of its systems and make unauthorized withdrawals, Binance said.

Mark Karpeles, former chief of defunct Tokyo-based bitcoin exchange Mt Gox, which collapsed a dozen years ago after $500 million in bitcoin was stolen, said attackers probably accessed private keys for at least two ​Binance wallets.
"Binance appears to have split its assets across multiple systems, ensuring a hack can only affect a part of the assets, but even so a single hack is a large loss," he said.
Cryptocurrency prices fell on the news, while Binance halted withdrawals and said it would cover the losses.

extraction.body: The world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, Binance, has estimated the impact of a major security incident at around $6.3 billion after a suspected attack involving unauthorised withdrawal transactions. The company has frozen around $3 billion worth of affected digital assets so far and promised to cover all losses. In its latest update on Friday, Binance said its initial investigation suggested that a DevOps engineer's laptop may have been compromised. Binance said it had found no evidence that any wallet private keys had been leaked. It is continuing its investigation and plans to publish a detailed technical post-mortem once the facts have been verified. Binance's initial investigation suggests that the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions. We have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak. We will share a detailed technical post-mortem once the investigation is complete and the facts are fully verified. The estimated total impact sits at around $6.3B. We have worked with blockchain partners to freeze affected assets, with ~$3 billion frozen on-chain so far. Binance will cover all losses from the SAFU fund and the company’s funds. As an immediate precaution, Binance has: - temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while security checks are completed; - revoked the affected address authorisation; - engaged law enforcement and blockchain intelligence partners to trace and recover funds. Please rely only on official Binance channels for updates. Tether and Circle, two major cryptocurrency companies, have also frozen around $2.4 billion in assets linked to the suspected attack. Bitcoin fell to a six-week low of $77,646 on Friday, while Ether dropped to a two-month low of $2,238.76, according to CoinGecko data cited by Reuters. Binance's native token, BNB, also fell more than 8 per cent over 24 hours to around $694. Binance's initial investigation points to a possible compromise of a DevOps engineer's laptop. According to Binance, the compromised laptop may have allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorised withdrawal transactions. The company has not yet explained how the laptop was compromised or provided a complete technical account of the attack. Importantly, Binance said its investigation had found no evidence of a wallet private-key leak. Private keys are cryptographic credentials that allow users or platforms to authorise transactions and control digital assets stored in blockchain wallets. Binance said it had revoked the affected address authorisation and was working with law enforcement agencies and blockchain intelligence partners to trace and recover the assets. The company will publish a detailed technical post-mortem after its investigation is complete. Binance said the estimated total impact of the incident stood at around $6.3 billion. However, the exchange has so far frozen approximately $3 billion worth of affected assets on-chain. The company is working with blockchain partners, cryptocurrency issuers and law enforcement agencies to identify and freeze additional assets. Two major cryptocurrency companies have also taken action. Tether, the issuer of the USDT stablecoin, said it had frozen around $1.6 billion in assets connected to the potential Binance hack. Circle, which issues the USDC stablecoin, said it had frozen more than $800 million linked to the incident. Together, the two companies have frozen around $2.4 billion in assets. These actions are significant because Tether and Circle issue some of the world's largest dollar-backed stablecoins. Their ability to freeze certain assets can help investigators prevent suspected stolen funds from being moved or converted. The $6.3 billion estimate should not be confused with the amount confirmed as stolen. Binance has not yet provided a final breakdown of the losses, and its investigation is ongoing. Binance has promised to cover all losses arising from the incident. The exchange said it would use its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and its own corporate funds to compensate for any losses.

SINGAPORE, Oct 30 (Reuters) – Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, said a security breach had resulted in an estimated $6.3 billion impact that analysts said could amount to the biggest crypto heist ever. Binance said it had worked with partners to freeze the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It gave no update on the status of the remaining $3.3 billion. The possible hacking sent crypto prices lower. Bitcoin hit a six-week low and was last down 3% at $76,469.82, while ether was down more than 3% at $2,185.83. Shares in crypto exchange Coinbase Global slid 4.8% while those of bitcoin ​buyer Strategy fell nearly 6% in extended US trading. Here are some comments from analysts and investors: ERIC JARDINE, HEAD OF RESEARCH AT CHAINALYSIS: “The investigation is ongoing, and we cannot yet confirm the cause of ‌the hack. As of 8:30 p.m. ET (0030 GMT), we have confirmed that at least $5.912 billion was stolen, with funds moving across multiple blockchains, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Tron, Ripple and several Layer 2 networks. “Binance has also confirmed that approximately $3 billion has been frozen. Blockchain transparency and coordination across the industry are helping disrupt the movement of stolen funds. Our investigators are actively identifying additional opportunities to freeze funds and support recovery efforts.” AMANDA HE, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER, CHAINUP INVESTMENT, SINGAPORE: “The initial drop may have been because the hacker was selling the coins. But after 8 a.m. (0000 GMT), as the Asian morning session got underway, that has caused panic sentiment to spread further… Binance is still the largest exchange in the market by trading volume, so it is really at the center of this storm — and at the ‌center of ​market activity. “We don’t have a large position on Binance. It accounts for less than 20% of our overall holdings. But for the positions we do ⁠have there, we’ve sold everything for now. Anything that can be ⁠moved out, we move first. Things that can’t be moved, we sell, shifting into safe-haven assets instead such as stablecoins. Withdrawals have now been suspended.” TIM SUN, SENIOR RESEARCHER, HASHKEY GROUP, HONG KONG: “We believe the implications of the Binance incident could well extend beyond the immediate loss of assets. The incident could rank among the largest security breaches in the history of the cryptocurrency industry. “Our bigger concern is the potential liquidity impact. As the largest digital-asset trading platform globally, any disruption to Binance’s deposit and withdrawal operations could affect market makers’ ability to move capital across venues.” GEOFFREY KENDRICK, HEAD OF DIGITAL ASSETS RESEARCH, STANDARD CHARTERED, LONDON: “I suspect ​the negative price action still has some way to go. Only after assets are unfrozen and more detail of the hack emerges will we find a new base.” ARAVIND SRINIVASAN, HEAD OF SYSTEMATIC OTC BUSINESS AT CRYPTO MARKET MAKER GSR: “It’s the biggest hack in history… ​spreads are wider and liquidity is thin in Binance too on spot. The average bid/ask spread on spot bitcoin was five times wider than normal earlier this morning, and 2.5 times for ether. Spreads have since narrowed slightly.” KENNETH GOH, ​DIRECTOR OF PRIVATE WEALTH MANAGEMENT AT UOB KAY HIAN, SINGAPORE: “Crypto has a long record of exchange thefts. Mt. Gox collapsed in 2014 after losing close to $500 million in bitcoin, ‌and Bybit lost about $1.5 billion only last year. “What stands out this time is where it happened. The world’s largest exchange should have the strongest controls in the industry, and it has still been breached. Investors will now look more closely at where their assets are held and who is responsible when something goes wrong.” MARK KARPELES, CEO OF KARPELES LAB, FORMER HEAD OF MT. GOX: “Binance appears to have split its assets across multiple systems (ensuring a hack can only affect a part of the assets), but even so a single hack is a large loss. It looks like the attacker somehow managed to get a valid delegation for both Binance 14 and Binance 16, which means they likely found the private ⁠key used by those addresses.” YUYA HASEGAWA, MARKET ANALYST, CRYPTOCURRENCY EXCHANGE BITBANK, TOKYO: “The reported scale of the incident is certainly alarming. However, the full extent of the damage remains unclear, particularly as stablecoin issuers have already frozen a substantial portion of the affected assets. “The biggest concern is not necessarily the amount stolen itself, but whether the incident triggers a broader loss of confidence in centralized exchanges, potentially leading to further withdrawals, liquidity disruptions, and forced selling. “That said, ⁠if Binance can demonstrate that customer assets remain secure, cover any losses, and restore ‌normal operations promptly, the market impact could prove relatively short-lived. Bitcoin’s underlying fundamentals have not been directly compromised by this incident.” “I ⁠don’t expect the stolen BTC to add much selling pressure. Bitcoin addresses can’t be frozen, but every coin is traceable on-chain, and Bitcoin has no mixing ​tool as deep or ‌liquid as Tornado Cash. In effect, much of that BTC is likely to stay ‘locked’ and might take years to go to the market. ETH is ​a different story. It ⁠can be laundered far more easily through Tornado Cash, so I would expect ongoing selling pressure and relative weakness in ETH. For perspective, after the Bybit hack, markets took only weeks to recover. “Beyond sentiment, this incident once again highlights the security risks of centralized exchanges, and of the crypto market more broadly amid AI development. That said, the breach appears to stem from how transactions were signed and authorized, not from a smart contract exploit.” JOSHUA CHU, CO-CHAIR OF THE HONG KONG WEB3 ASSOCIATION, HONG KONG: “This incident puts four fronts in play: regulators protecting the public, law enforcement pursuing offenders, civil litigation recovering assets, and ecosystem players ensuring they do not become the getaway route for stolen funds. For crypto players still resisting government cooperation, the contradiction is awkward: regulation is ‘overreach’ while profits flow, but government is ‘not doing enough’ when the money disappears.” (Reporting by Ankur Banerjee, Gregor Stuart Hunter and Rae Wee in Singapore, Rocky Swift in Tokyo and Summer Zhen ​and Jiaxing Li in Hong Kong; Editing by Jamie Freed)

SINGAPORE, Oct 30 (Reuters) – Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, said a security breach had resulted in an estimated $6.3 billion impact that analysts said could amount to the biggest crypto heist ever.
Binance said it had worked with partners to freeze the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It gave no update on the status of the remaining $3.3 billion.
The possible hacking sent crypto prices lower. Bitcoin hit a six-week low and was last down 3% at $76,469.82, while ether was down more than 3% at $2,185.83.
Shares in crypto exchange Coinbase Global slid 4.8% while those of bitcoin ​buyer Strategy fell nearly 6% in extended US trading.
Here are some comments from analysts and investors:
ERIC JARDINE, HEAD OF RESEARCH AT CHAINALYSIS:

“The investigation is ongoing, and we cannot yet confirm the cause of ‌the hack. As of 8:30 p.m. ET (0030 GMT), we have confirmed that at least $5.912 billion was stolen, with funds moving across multiple blockchains, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Tron, Ripple and several Layer 2 networks.

“Binance has also confirmed that approximately $3 billion has been frozen. Blockchain transparency and coordination across the industry are helping disrupt the movement of stolen funds. Our investigators are actively identifying additional opportunities to freeze funds and support recovery efforts.”
AMANDA HE, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER, CHAINUP INVESTMENT, SINGAPORE:

“The initial drop may have been because the hacker was selling the coins. But after 8 a.m. (0000 GMT), as the Asian morning session got underway, that has caused panic sentiment to spread further… Binance is still the largest exchange in the market by trading volume, so it is really at the center of this storm — and at the ‌center of ​market activity.

“We don’t have a large position on Binance. It accounts for less than 20% of our overall holdings. But for the positions we do ⁠have there, we’ve sold everything for now. Anything that can be ⁠moved out, we move first. Things that can’t be moved, we sell, shifting into safe-haven assets instead such as stablecoins. Withdrawals have now been suspended.”
TIM SUN, SENIOR RESEARCHER, HASHKEY GROUP, HONG KONG:

“We believe the implications of the Binance incident could well extend beyond the immediate loss of assets. The incident could rank among the largest security breaches in the history of the cryptocurrency industry.

“Our bigger concern is the potential liquidity impact. As the largest digital-asset trading platform globally, any disruption to Binance’s deposit and withdrawal operations could affect market makers’ ability to move capital across venues.”
GEOFFREY KENDRICK, HEAD OF DIGITAL ASSETS RESEARCH, STANDARD CHARTERED, LONDON:
“I suspect ​the negative price action still has some way to go. Only after assets are unfrozen and more detail of the hack emerges will we find a new base.”
ARAVIND SRINIVASAN, HEAD OF SYSTEMATIC OTC BUSINESS AT CRYPTO MARKET MAKER GSR:

“It’s the biggest hack in history… ​spreads are wider and liquidity is thin in Binance too on spot. The average bid/ask spread on spot bitcoin was five times wider than normal earlier this morning, and 2.5 times for ether. Spreads have since narrowed slightly.”
KENNETH GOH, ​DIRECTOR OF PRIVATE WEALTH MANAGEMENT AT UOB KAY HIAN, SINGAPORE:
“Crypto has a long record of exchange thefts. Mt. Gox collapsed in 2014 after losing close to $500 million in bitcoin, ‌and Bybit lost about $1.5 billion only last year.

“What stands out this time is where it happened. The world’s largest exchange should have the strongest controls in the industry, and it has still been breached. Investors will now look more closely at where their assets are held and who is responsible when something goes wrong.”
MARK KARPELES, CEO OF KARPELES LAB, FORMER HEAD OF MT. GOX:

“Binance appears to have split its assets across multiple systems (ensuring a hack can only affect a part of the assets), but even so a single hack is a large loss. It looks like the attacker somehow managed to get a valid delegation for both Binance 14 and Binance 16, which means they likely found the private ⁠key used by those addresses.”
YUYA HASEGAWA, MARKET ANALYST, CRYPTOCURRENCY EXCHANGE BITBANK, TOKYO:

“The reported scale of the incident is certainly alarming. However, the full extent of the damage remains unclear, particularly as stablecoin issuers have already frozen a substantial portion of the affected assets.

“The biggest concern is not necessarily the amount stolen itself, but whether the incident triggers a broader loss of confidence in centralized exchanges, potentially leading to further withdrawals, liquidity disruptions, and forced selling.

“That said, ⁠if Binance can demonstrate that customer assets remain secure, cover any losses, and restore ‌normal operations promptly, the market impact could prove relatively short-lived. Bitcoin’s underlying fundamentals have not been directly compromised by this incident.”

“I ⁠don’t expect the stolen BTC to add much selling pressure. Bitcoin addresses can’t be frozen, but every coin is traceable on-chain, and Bitcoin has no mixing ​tool as deep or ‌liquid as Tornado Cash. In effect, much of that BTC is likely to stay ‘locked’ and might take years to go to the market. ETH is ​a different story. It ⁠can be laundered far more easily through Tornado Cash, so I would expect ongoing selling pressure and relative weakness in ETH. For perspective, after the Bybit hack, markets took only weeks to recover.

“Beyond sentiment, this incident once again highlights the security risks of centralized exchanges, and of the crypto market more broadly amid AI development. That said, the breach appears to stem from how transactions were signed and authorized, not from a smart contract exploit.”
JOSHUA CHU, CO-CHAIR OF THE HONG KONG WEB3 ASSOCIATION, HONG KONG:

“This incident puts four fronts in play: regulators protecting the public, law enforcement pursuing offenders, civil litigation recovering assets, and ecosystem players ensuring they do not become the getaway route for stolen funds. For crypto players still resisting government cooperation, the contradiction is awkward: regulation is ‘overreach’ while profits flow, but government is ‘not doing enough’ when the money disappears.”
(Reporting by Ankur Banerjee, Gregor Stuart Hunter and Rae Wee in Singapore, Rocky Swift in Tokyo and Summer Zhen ​and Jiaxing Li in Hong Kong; Editing by Jamie Freed)

It gave no update on the status of the remaining $3.3 billion as Binance co-founder Yi He said the company would cover "all hacking losses".An initial investigation suggested the breach may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of its engineers, which let an attacker gain access to one of its systems and make unauthorized withdrawals, Binance said.Markets reacted immediately in early Asian trading on Friday.Bitcoin dropped more than 3% to a six-week low of $76,368 and ether fell more than 3% to a two-month low of $2,178.
Binance's Yi said $27 million in stablecoins and about $2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen.Crypto firm Ripple also froze roughly $200 million in funds, Yi said.

Jack McDonald, senior vice president of stablecoins at Ripple, said the company was closely monitoring reports of a potential exploit involving Binance and was freezing affected funds and coordinating with relevant parties.INCIDENT ADDS TO STRING OF CRYPTO THEFTSMiguel Morel, CEO of blockchain intelligence firm Arkham, said data indicated that billions of dollars appeared to have been hacked from Binance by an unknown actor.The incident adds to a string of crypto thefts.
Last year, attackers stole $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks, according to researchers at TRM Labs.

extraction.body: Binance estimates that a security breach affected $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency. The exchange says partners have frozen about $3 billion in assets and promises to cover all losses. The incident sent cryptocurrency prices lower and raised concerns about exchange security. The world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange said on October 30 that an initial investigation pointed to a possible compromise of a laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer . The attacker may have used access to a service container to submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions. Binance said investigators had found no evidence that wallet private keys had leaked. The company temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while its security teams checked its systems and traced the affected assets. It also revoked authorisation for the affected address and contacted law enforcement agencies. Binance co-founder Yi He said the company would cover all hacking losses through its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and corporate funds. The exchange said customer funds remained safe. It plans to publish a technical report after completing its investigation and update its proof of reserves after remediation. Several cryptocurrency firms helped freeze assets linked to the incident. Tether froze nearly $1.57 billion , while Circle froze more than $800 million . Binance also reported that Ripple had frozen about $200 million . The exchange said roughly $3 billion in affected assets had been frozen or located with help from industry partners. The status of the remaining estimated $3.3 billion was not yet clear. Binance has more than 335 million registered users worldwide. Its 2025 annual report showed about $162.8 billion in assets under custody. The incident triggered a sell-off in cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin fell to a six-week low, while Ether reached its lowest level in two months. Binance-linked BNB also declined. Shares in Coinbase fell 4.8% in extended US trading. Strategy, a company known for its large Bitcoin holdings, lost nearly 6% . Analysts warned that the incident could prompt investors to reconsider the risks of holding digital assets on centralised exchanges. They also raised concerns about counterparty, solvency and liquidity risks. The breach adds to a series of major cryptocurrency thefts. Binance.US and Coinbase said their platforms were not affected by the incident. passages: The world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, Binance, is facing a security incident estimated to have caused $6.3 billion in losses, the highest ever recorded in the history of the digital asset industry.
According to information published on October 30, Binance said it had coordinated with partners to freeze the affected assets, of which about $3 billion had been located.

Before the Binance incident was confirmed, the attack on the Bybit exchange in February 2025 was still regarded as the largest crypto theft ever officially disclosed, with losses of about $1.5 billion.
At the time, hackers took control of a transaction involving Bybit's Ethereum cold wallet and moved a large amount of assets to unauthorized addresses.

For investors, this event reinforces the trend of allocating assets through self-custody wallets and insured custody solutions, while increasing pressure on centralized exchanges to disclose reserve audit processes and infrastructure security standards.

For the industry as a whole, the concentration of risk at bridges and third-party wallet providers continues to be a weakness that must be addressed before institutional capital returns more strongly.

Department of Justice announced the seizure of about 127,271 Bitcoin, then worth nearly $15 billion, related to the criminal case against Chen Zhi, founder of Prince Group, giving rise to disputes over the origin and ownership of the assets.

Binance co-founder Yi He insisted the company will compensate for "all losses caused by the attack." The statement comes as investors question the safety of customer funds held at centralized exchanges and as many are forced to revisit their risk appetite for holding crypto assets.
This incident involved bridge infrastructure rather than a direct breach of the Binance exchange.
