extraction.body: The world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, Binance, is facing a security incident estimated to have caused $6.3 billion in losses, the highest ever recorded in the history of the digital asset industry. According to information published on October 30, Binance said it had coordinated with partners to freeze the affected assets, of which about $3 billion had been located. The exchange has not updated the status of the remaining $3.3 billion. Binance co-founder Yi He insisted the company will compensate for "all losses caused by the attack." The statement comes as investors question the safety of customer funds held at centralized exchanges and as many are forced to revisit their risk appetite for holding crypto assets. Before the Binance incident was confirmed, the attack on the Bybit exchange in February 2025 was still regarded as the largest crypto theft ever officially disclosed, with losses of about $1.5 billion. At the time, hackers took control of a transaction involving Bybit's Ethereum cold wallet and moved a large amount of assets to unauthorized addresses. Notably, the attackers did not break the security mechanism of the Ethereum blockchain but instead exploited the transaction approval system of a third-party wallet provider: the transaction confirmation interface was tampered with so that staff saw an ordinary transfer order, while the actual content was re-signed to change control of the wallet. On February 26, 2025, the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) attributed the incident to a North Korea-linked cyber actor group called TraderTraitor; the stolen funds were subsequently converted into Bitcoin and dispersed across thousands of wallets on multiple blockchain networks. The table below summarizes the largest crypto thefts based on disclosed data: Note: Loss values are calculated at the time of the incident or the time of disclosure; the Binance figure is a preliminary estimate and may change as the investigation expands. Beyond Bybit, the industry's history records many other large-scale incidents. In March 2022, Ronin Network, the blockchain network serving the game Axie Infinity, had 173,600 ETH and 25.5 million USDC stolen, estimated at about $540 million at the time of the attack and rising to more than $600 million when the incident was disclosed due to Ethereum price volatility. The attackers obtained the private keys of 5 of the 9 validation nodes, just enough to meet the threshold needed to approve transactions. The incident occurred on March 23 but was not discovered until March 29, 2022, after a user was unable to execute a withdrawal. U.S. authorities later linked the incident to North Korea's Lazarus hacker group. Before Ronin, in August 2021, Poly Network recorded a smart contract vulnerability that led to about $610 million in assets being moved. What followed was unusual when the perpetrator began returning the money, and by the end of August 2021 the platform announced it had regained control of nearly all the stolen assets, except for a portion of stablecoins that had been frozen. The Binance ecosystem itself had seen several incidents before 2026. In May 2019, the exchange had about 7,000 Bitcoin, equivalent to $41 million at the time, stolen through online phishing and malware; Binance later used its user protection fund to cover the losses. In October 2022, BSC Token Hub, a bridge belonging to BNB Chain, was exploited through a vulnerability to create about 2 million BNB worth more than $550 million; thanks to a network pause and coordinated freezing, most of the funds remained within control, while about $100-130 million was moved to other blockchains. This incident involved bridge infrastructure rather than a direct breach of the Binance exchange. A controversial case is LuBian. In August 2025, blockchain analytics firm Arkham Intelligence published the results of an investigation into the loss of about 127,426 Bitcoin, estimated to be worth $3.5 billion at the time, from wallets linked to this Bitcoin mining group in December 2020. LuBian was said to have carried out more than 1,500 transactions with messages offering to return the Bitcoin, spending about 1.4 BTC just to send the messages. Analysts suspect the vulnerability lay in the private key generation algorithm. The case became more complicated when, in October 2025, the U.S. Department of Justice announced the seizure of about 127,271 Bitcoin, then worth nearly $15 billion, related to the criminal case against Chen Zhi, founder of Prince Group, giving rise to disputes over the origin and ownership of the assets. In Japan, the 2018 Coincheck case was a major milestone when hackers stole NEM worth about $530 million from the exchange's hot wallet. Earlier, the collapse of Mt. Gox in 2014 - an exchange that once handled most global Bitcoin transactions - with losses of about 850,000 Bitcoin, nearly $500 million at the time, forced the exchange to file for bankruptcy and affected tens of thousands of customers. The wave of attacks continued in 2026. In September, the Bitget exchange announced the theft of assets worth about $350 million, a figure later revised to about $387.5 million, showing that initially disclosed losses can change significantly as investigations expand. According to TRM Labs data, in 2025 alone, hackers stole about $2.9 billion in crypto assets through nearly 150 attacks, spanning centralized exchanges, custodial wallets, authentication systems and blockchain bridges. Binance's $6.3 billion scale - if fully confirmed - would far exceed any previous incident, including the $3.5 billion loss at LuBian. The fact that about half the loss value has been frozen somewhat eases concerns about the exchange's solvency, but the question of the fate of the remaining $3.3 billion remains unanswered. For investors, this event reinforces the trend of allocating assets through self-custody wallets and insured custody solutions, while increasing pressure on centralized exchanges to disclose reserve audit processes and infrastructure security standards. For the industry as a whole, the concentration of risk at bridges and third-party wallet providers continues to be a weakness that must be addressed before institutional capital returns more strongly. coreStoryFacts.text: SINGAPORE, Oct 30 (Reuters) – Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, said a security breach had resulted in an estimated $6.3 billion impact that analysts said could amount to the biggest crypto heist ever.
Binance said it had worked with partners to freeze the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far.
It gave no update on the status of the remaining $3.3 billion.
“Binance has also confirmed that approximately $3 billion has been frozen.
Blockchain transparency and coordination across the industry are helping disrupt the movement of stolen funds.
Our investigators are actively identifying additional opportunities to freeze funds and support recovery efforts.”
“Binance appears to have split its assets across multiple systems (ensuring a hack can only affect a part of the assets), but even so a single hack is a large loss.
It looks like the attacker somehow managed to get a valid delegation for both Binance 14 and Binance 16, which means they likely found the private ⁠key used by those addresses.”
“We believe the implications of the Binance incident could well extend beyond the immediate loss of assets.
“That said, ⁠if Binance can demonstrate that customer assets remain secure, cover any losses, and restore ‌normal operations promptly, the market impact could prove relatively short-lived.
Bitcoin’s underlying fundamentals have not been directly compromised by this incident.”
“Our bigger concern is the potential liquidity impact.
As the largest digital-asset trading platform globally, any disruption to Binance’s deposit and withdrawal operations could affect market makers’ ability to move capital across venues.”
“It’s the biggest hack in history… ​spreads are wider and liquidity is thin in Binance too on spot.
The average bid/ask spread on spot bitcoin was five times wider than normal earlier this morning, and 2.5 times for ether.
“The initial drop may have been because the hacker was selling the coins.

SINGAPORE, Oct 30 (Reuters) – Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, said a security breach had resulted in an estimated $6.3 billion impact that analysts said could amount to the biggest crypto heist ever. Binance said it had worked with partners to freeze the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It gave no update on the status of the remaining $3.3 billion. The possible hacking sent crypto prices lower. Bitcoin hit a six-week low and was last down 3% at $76,469.82, while ether was down more than 3% at $2,185.83. Shares in crypto exchange Coinbase Global slid 4.8% while those of bitcoin ​buyer Strategy fell nearly 6% in extended US trading. Here are some comments from analysts and investors: ERIC JARDINE, HEAD OF RESEARCH AT CHAINALYSIS: “The investigation is ongoing, and we cannot yet confirm the cause of ‌the hack. As of 8:30 p.m. ET (0030 GMT), we have confirmed that at least $5.912 billion was stolen, with funds moving across multiple blockchains, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Tron, Ripple and several Layer 2 networks. “Binance has also confirmed that approximately $3 billion has been frozen. Blockchain transparency and coordination across the industry are helping disrupt the movement of stolen funds. Our investigators are actively identifying additional opportunities to freeze funds and support recovery efforts.” AMANDA HE, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER, CHAINUP INVESTMENT, SINGAPORE: “The initial drop may have been because the hacker was selling the coins. But after 8 a.m. (0000 GMT), as the Asian morning session got underway, that has caused panic sentiment to spread further… Binance is still the largest exchange in the market by trading volume, so it is really at the center of this storm — and at the ‌center of ​market activity. “We don’t have a large position on Binance. It accounts for less than 20% of our overall holdings. But for the positions we do ⁠have there, we’ve sold everything for now. Anything that can be ⁠moved out, we move first. Things that can’t be moved, we sell, shifting into safe-haven assets instead such as stablecoins. Withdrawals have now been suspended.” TIM SUN, SENIOR RESEARCHER, HASHKEY GROUP, HONG KONG: “We believe the implications of the Binance incident could well extend beyond the immediate loss of assets. The incident could rank among the largest security breaches in the history of the cryptocurrency industry. “Our bigger concern is the potential liquidity impact. As the largest digital-asset trading platform globally, any disruption to Binance’s deposit and withdrawal operations could affect market makers’ ability to move capital across venues.” GEOFFREY KENDRICK, HEAD OF DIGITAL ASSETS RESEARCH, STANDARD CHARTERED, LONDON: “I suspect ​the negative price action still has some way to go. Only after assets are unfrozen and more detail of the hack emerges will we find a new base.” ARAVIND SRINIVASAN, HEAD OF SYSTEMATIC OTC BUSINESS AT CRYPTO MARKET MAKER GSR: “It’s the biggest hack in history… ​spreads are wider and liquidity is thin in Binance too on spot. The average bid/ask spread on spot bitcoin was five times wider than normal earlier this morning, and 2.5 times for ether. Spreads have since narrowed slightly.” KENNETH GOH, ​DIRECTOR OF PRIVATE WEALTH MANAGEMENT AT UOB KAY HIAN, SINGAPORE: “Crypto has a long record of exchange thefts. Mt. Gox collapsed in 2014 after losing close to $500 million in bitcoin, ‌and Bybit lost about $1.5 billion only last year. “What stands out this time is where it happened. The world’s largest exchange should have the strongest controls in the industry, and it has still been breached. Investors will now look more closely at where their assets are held and who is responsible when something goes wrong.” MARK KARPELES, CEO OF KARPELES LAB, FORMER HEAD OF MT. GOX: “Binance appears to have split its assets across multiple systems (ensuring a hack can only affect a part of the assets), but even so a single hack is a large loss. It looks like the attacker somehow managed to get a valid delegation for both Binance 14 and Binance 16, which means they likely found the private ⁠key used by those addresses.” YUYA HASEGAWA, MARKET ANALYST, CRYPTOCURRENCY EXCHANGE BITBANK, TOKYO: “The reported scale of the incident is certainly alarming. However, the full extent of the damage remains unclear, particularly as stablecoin issuers have already frozen a substantial portion of the affected assets. “The biggest concern is not necessarily the amount stolen itself, but whether the incident triggers a broader loss of confidence in centralized exchanges, potentially leading to further withdrawals, liquidity disruptions, and forced selling. “That said, ⁠if Binance can demonstrate that customer assets remain secure, cover any losses, and restore ‌normal operations promptly, the market impact could prove relatively short-lived. Bitcoin’s underlying fundamentals have not been directly compromised by this incident.” “I ⁠don’t expect the stolen BTC to add much selling pressure. Bitcoin addresses can’t be frozen, but every coin is traceable on-chain, and Bitcoin has no mixing ​tool as deep or ‌liquid as Tornado Cash. In effect, much of that BTC is likely to stay ‘locked’ and might take years to go to the market. ETH is ​a different story. It ⁠can be laundered far more easily through Tornado Cash, so I would expect ongoing selling pressure and relative weakness in ETH. For perspective, after the Bybit hack, markets took only weeks to recover. “Beyond sentiment, this incident once again highlights the security risks of centralized exchanges, and of the crypto market more broadly amid AI development. That said, the breach appears to stem from how transactions were signed and authorized, not from a smart contract exploit.” JOSHUA CHU, CO-CHAIR OF THE HONG KONG WEB3 ASSOCIATION, HONG KONG: “This incident puts four fronts in play: regulators protecting the public, law enforcement pursuing offenders, civil litigation recovering assets, and ecosystem players ensuring they do not become the getaway route for stolen funds. For crypto players still resisting government cooperation, the contradiction is awkward: regulation is ‘overreach’ while profits flow, but government is ‘not doing enough’ when the money disappears.” (Reporting by Ankur Banerjee, Gregor Stuart Hunter and Rae Wee in Singapore, Rocky Swift in Tokyo and Summer Zhen ​and Jiaxing Li in Hong Kong; Editing by Jamie Freed)

“It’s the biggest hack in history… ​spreads are wider and liquidity is thin in Binance too on spot. The average bid/ask spread on spot bitcoin was five times wider than normal earlier this morning, and 2.5 times for ether. Spreads have since narrowed slightly.”
KENNETH GOH, ​DIRECTOR OF PRIVATE WEALTH MANAGEMENT AT UOB KAY HIAN, SINGAPORE:
“Crypto has a long record of exchange thefts. Mt. Gox collapsed in 2014 after losing close to $500 million in bitcoin, ‌and Bybit lost about $1.5 billion only last year.

“What stands out this time is where it happened. The world’s largest exchange should have the strongest controls in the industry, and it has still been breached. Investors will now look more closely at where their assets are held and who is responsible when something goes wrong.”
MARK KARPELES, CEO OF KARPELES LAB, FORMER HEAD OF MT. GOX:

“Binance appears to have split its assets across multiple systems (ensuring a hack can only affect a part of the assets), but even so a single hack is a large loss. It looks like the attacker somehow managed to get a valid delegation for both Binance 14 and Binance 16, which means they likely found the private ⁠key used by those addresses.”
YUYA HASEGAWA, MARKET ANALYST, CRYPTOCURRENCY EXCHANGE BITBANK, TOKYO:

“The reported scale of the incident is certainly alarming. However, the full extent of the damage remains unclear, particularly as stablecoin issuers have already frozen a substantial portion of the affected assets.

“The biggest concern is not necessarily the amount stolen itself, but whether the incident triggers a broader loss of confidence in centralized exchanges, potentially leading to further withdrawals, liquidity disruptions, and forced selling.

“That said, ⁠if Binance can demonstrate that customer assets remain secure, cover any losses, and restore ‌normal operations promptly, the market impact could prove relatively short-lived. Bitcoin’s underlying fundamentals have not been directly compromised by this incident.”

“I ⁠don’t expect the stolen BTC to add much selling pressure. Bitcoin addresses can’t be frozen, but every coin is traceable on-chain, and Bitcoin has no mixing ​tool as deep or ‌liquid as Tornado Cash. In effect, much of that BTC is likely to stay ‘locked’ and might take years to go to the market. ETH is ​a different story. It ⁠can be laundered far more easily through Tornado Cash, so I would expect ongoing selling pressure and relative weakness in ETH. For perspective, after the Bybit hack, markets took only weeks to recover.

“Beyond sentiment, this incident once again highlights the security risks of centralized exchanges, and of the crypto market more broadly amid AI development. That said, the breach appears to stem from how transactions were signed and authorized, not from a smart contract exploit.”
JOSHUA CHU, CO-CHAIR OF THE HONG KONG WEB3 ASSOCIATION, HONG KONG:

“This incident puts four fronts in play: regulators protecting the public, law enforcement pursuing offenders, civil litigation recovering assets, and ecosystem players ensuring they do not become the getaway route for stolen funds. For crypto players still resisting government cooperation, the contradiction is awkward: regulation is ‘overreach’ while profits flow, but government is ‘not doing enough’ when the money disappears.”
(Reporting by Ankur Banerjee, Gregor Stuart Hunter and Rae Wee in Singapore, Rocky Swift in Tokyo and Summer Zhen ​and Jiaxing Li in Hong Kong; Editing by Jamie Freed)

extraction.body: Binance estimates that a security breach affected $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency. The exchange says partners have frozen about $3 billion in assets and promises to cover all losses. The incident sent cryptocurrency prices lower and raised concerns about exchange security. The world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange said on October 30 that an initial investigation pointed to a possible compromise of a laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer . The attacker may have used access to a service container to submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions. Binance said investigators had found no evidence that wallet private keys had leaked. The company temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while its security teams checked its systems and traced the affected assets. It also revoked authorisation for the affected address and contacted law enforcement agencies. Binance co-founder Yi He said the company would cover all hacking losses through its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and corporate funds. The exchange said customer funds remained safe. It plans to publish a technical report after completing its investigation and update its proof of reserves after remediation. Several cryptocurrency firms helped freeze assets linked to the incident. Tether froze nearly $1.57 billion , while Circle froze more than $800 million . Binance also reported that Ripple had frozen about $200 million . The exchange said roughly $3 billion in affected assets had been frozen or located with help from industry partners. The status of the remaining estimated $3.3 billion was not yet clear. Binance has more than 335 million registered users worldwide. Its 2025 annual report showed about $162.8 billion in assets under custody. The incident triggered a sell-off in cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin fell to a six-week low, while Ether reached its lowest level in two months. Binance-linked BNB also declined. Shares in Coinbase fell 4.8% in extended US trading. Strategy, a company known for its large Bitcoin holdings, lost nearly 6% . Analysts warned that the incident could prompt investors to reconsider the risks of holding digital assets on centralised exchanges. They also raised concerns about counterparty, solvency and liquidity risks. The breach adds to a series of major cryptocurrency thefts. Binance.US and Coinbase said their platforms were not affected by the incident. extraction.body: The world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, Binance, is facing a security incident estimated to have caused $6.3 billion in losses, the highest ever recorded in the history of the digital asset industry. According to information published on October 30, Binance said it had coordinated with partners to freeze the affected assets, of which about $3 billion had been located. The exchange has not updated the status of the remaining $3.3 billion. Binance co-founder Yi He insisted the company will compensate for "all losses caused by the attack." The statement comes as investors question the safety of customer funds held at centralized exchanges and as many are forced to revisit their risk appetite for holding crypto assets. Before the Binance incident was confirmed, the attack on the Bybit exchange in February 2025 was still regarded as the largest crypto theft ever officially disclosed, with losses of about $1.5 billion. At the time, hackers took control of a transaction involving Bybit's Ethereum cold wallet and moved a large amount of assets to unauthorized addresses. Notably, the attackers did not break the security mechanism of the Ethereum blockchain but instead exploited the transaction approval system of a third-party wallet provider: the transaction confirmation interface was tampered with so that staff saw an ordinary transfer order, while the actual content was re-signed to change control of the wallet. On February 26, 2025, the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) attributed the incident to a North Korea-linked cyber actor group called TraderTraitor; the stolen funds were subsequently converted into Bitcoin and dispersed across thousands of wallets on multiple blockchain networks. The table below summarizes the largest crypto thefts based on disclosed data: Note: Loss values are calculated at the time of the incident or the time of disclosure; the Binance figure is a preliminary estimate and may change as the investigation expands. Beyond Bybit, the industry's history records many other large-scale incidents. In March 2022, Ronin Network, the blockchain network serving the game Axie Infinity, had 173,600 ETH and 25.5 million USDC stolen, estimated at about $540 million at the time of the attack and rising to more than $600 million when the incident was disclosed due to Ethereum price volatility. The attackers obtained the private keys of 5 of the 9 validation nodes, just enough to meet the threshold needed to approve transactions. The incident occurred on March 23 but was not discovered until March 29, 2022, after a user was unable to execute a withdrawal. U.S. authorities later linked the incident to North Korea's Lazarus hacker group. Before Ronin, in August 2021, Poly Network recorded a smart contract vulnerability that led to about $610 million in assets being moved. What followed was unusual when the perpetrator began returning the money, and by the end of August 2021 the platform announced it had regained control of nearly all the stolen assets, except for a portion of stablecoins that had been frozen. The Binance ecosystem itself had seen several incidents before 2026. In May 2019, the exchange had about 7,000 Bitcoin, equivalent to $41 million at the time, stolen through online phishing and malware; Binance later used its user protection fund to cover the losses. In October 2022, BSC Token Hub, a bridge belonging to BNB Chain, was exploited through a vulnerability to create about 2 million BNB worth more than $550 million; thanks to a network pause and coordinated freezing, most of the funds remained within control, while about $100-130 million was moved to other blockchains. This incident involved bridge infrastructure rather than a direct breach of the Binance exchange. A controversial case is LuBian. In August 2025, blockchain analytics firm Arkham Intelligence published the results of an investigation into the loss of about 127,426 Bitcoin, estimated to be worth $3.5 billion at the time, from wallets linked to this Bitcoin mining group in December 2020. LuBian was said to have carried out more than 1,500 transactions with messages offering to return the Bitcoin, spending about 1.4 BTC just to send the messages. Analysts suspect the vulnerability lay in the private key generation algorithm. The case became more complicated when, in October 2025, the U.S. Department of Justice announced the seizure of about 127,271 Bitcoin, then worth nearly $15 billion, related to the criminal case against Chen Zhi, founder of Prince Group, giving rise to disputes over the origin and ownership of the assets. In Japan, the 2018 Coincheck case was a major milestone when hackers stole NEM worth about $530 million from the exchange's hot wallet. Earlier, the collapse of Mt. Gox in 2014 - an exchange that once handled most global Bitcoin transactions - with losses of about 850,000 Bitcoin, nearly $500 million at the time, forced the exchange to file for bankruptcy and affected tens of thousands of customers. The wave of attacks continued in 2026. In September, the Bitget exchange announced the theft of assets worth about $350 million, a figure later revised to about $387.5 million, showing that initially disclosed losses can change significantly as investigations expand. According to TRM Labs data, in 2025 alone, hackers stole about $2.9 billion in crypto assets through nearly 150 attacks, spanning centralized exchanges, custodial wallets, authentication systems and blockchain bridges. Binance's $6.3 billion scale - if fully confirmed - would far exceed any previous incident, including the $3.5 billion loss at LuBian. The fact that about half the loss value has been frozen somewhat eases concerns about the exchange's solvency, but the question of the fate of the remaining $3.3 billion remains unanswered. For investors, this event reinforces the trend of allocating assets through self-custody wallets and insured custody solutions, while increasing pressure on centralized exchanges to disclose reserve audit processes and infrastructure security standards. For the industry as a whole, the concentration of risk at bridges and third-party wallet providers continues to be a weakness that must be addressed before institutional capital returns more strongly. U.S. authorities later linked the incident to North Korea's Lazarus hacker group.

Before Ronin, in August 2021, Poly Network recorded a smart contract vulnerability that led to about $610 million in assets being moved. What followed was unusual when the perpetrator began returning the money, and by the end of August 2021 the platform announced it had regained control of nearly all the stolen assets, except for a portion of stablecoins that had been frozen.

The Binance ecosystem itself had seen several incidents before 2026. In May 2019, the exchange had about 7,000 Bitcoin, equivalent to $41 million at the time, stolen through online phishing and malware; Binance later used its user protection fund to cover the losses. In October 2022, BSC Token Hub, a bridge belonging to BNB Chain, was exploited through a vulnerability to create about 2 million BNB worth more than $550 million; thanks to a network pause and coordinated freezing, most of the funds remained within control, while about $100-130 million was moved to other blockchains. This incident involved bridge infrastructure rather than a direct breach of the Binance exchange.

A controversial case is LuBian. In August 2025, blockchain analytics firm Arkham Intelligence published the results of an investigation into the loss of about 127,426 Bitcoin, estimated to be worth $3.5 billion at the time, from wallets linked to this Bitcoin mining group in December 2020. LuBian was said to have carried out more than 1,500 transactions with messages offering to return the Bitcoin, spending about 1.4 BTC just to send the messages. Analysts suspect the vulnerability lay in the private key generation algorithm. The case became more complicated when, in October 2025, the U.S. Department of Justice announced the seizure of about 127,271 Bitcoin, then worth nearly $15 billion, related to the criminal case against Chen Zhi, founder of Prince Group, giving rise to disputes over the origin and ownership of the assets.

In Japan, the 2018 Coincheck case was a major milestone when hackers stole NEM worth about $530 million from the exchange's hot wallet. Earlier, the collapse of Mt. Gox in 2014 - an exchange that once handled most global Bitcoin transactions - with losses of about 850,000 Bitcoin, nearly $500 million at the time, forced the exchange to file for bankruptcy and affected tens of thousands of customers.

The wave of attacks continued in 2026. In September, the Bitget exchange announced the theft of assets worth about $350 million, a figure later revised to about $387.5 million, showing that initially disclosed losses can change significantly as investigations expand. According to TRM Labs data, in 2025 alone, hackers stole about $2.9 billion in crypto assets through nearly 150 attacks, spanning centralized exchanges, custodial wallets, authentication systems and blockchain bridges.

Binance's $6.3 billion scale - if fully confirmed - would far exceed any previous incident, including the $3.5 billion loss at LuBian. The fact that about half the loss value has been frozen somewhat eases concerns about the exchange's solvency, but the question of the fate of the remaining $3.3 billion remains unanswered. For investors, this event reinforces the trend of allocating assets through self-custody wallets and insured custody solutions, while increasing pressure on centralized exchanges to disclose reserve audit processes and infrastructure security standards. For the industry as a whole, the concentration of risk at bridges and third-party wallet providers continues to be a weakness that must be addressed before institutional capital returns more strongly.

relevantPassages.text: The world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, Binance, is facing a security incident estimated to have caused $6.3 billion in losses, the highest ever recorded in the history of the digital asset industry.
According to information published on October 30, Binance said it had coordinated with partners to freeze the affected assets, of which about $3 billion had been located.

Before the Binance incident was confirmed, the attack on the Bybit exchange in February 2025 was still regarded as the largest crypto theft ever officially disclosed, with losses of about $1.5 billion.
At the time, hackers took control of a transaction involving Bybit's Ethereum cold wallet and moved a large amount of assets to unauthorized addresses.

For investors, this event reinforces the trend of allocating assets through self-custody wallets and insured custody solutions, while increasing pressure on centralized exchanges to disclose reserve audit processes and infrastructure security standards.

For the industry as a whole, the concentration of risk at bridges and third-party wallet providers continues to be a weakness that must be addressed before institutional capital returns more strongly.

Department of Justice announced the seizure of about 127,271 Bitcoin, then worth nearly $15 billion, related to the criminal case against Chen Zhi, founder of Prince Group, giving rise to disputes over the origin and ownership of the assets.

Binance co-founder Yi He insisted the company will compensate for "all losses caused by the attack." The statement comes as investors question the safety of customer funds held at centralized exchanges and as many are forced to revisit their risk appetite for holding crypto assets.
This incident involved bridge infrastructure rather than a direct breach of the Binance exchange.

extraction.body: Binance put a number on its worst day. The exchange said the Binance $6.3 billion security incident carries an estimated total impact of roughly $6.3 billion, and that about $3 billion of affected assets are already frozen with blockchain partners. Reuters, CNBC and Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty all reported the story on October 30, 2026, and analysts immediately started asking whether this is the largest crypto theft ever recorded. The honest answer is that nobody can prove that yet. Binance calls the event a “security incident,” its founder Changpeng Zhao says it “does look like a hack,” and the frozen figure has already moved between $3 billion and $2.54 billion depending on the update. We tracked the earlier versions of this story in our piece on the first $2.54 billion freeze and the developer safeguards it prompted . This article takes the next step: it separates what Binance has confirmed from what analysts are inferring, and it asks what the numbers mean for anyone who keeps assets on a centralized exchange. Everything below comes from the reported fact record for October 30. Where a detail is missing, we say so instead of filling the gap. That matters here more than usual, because the headline figure, the frozen figure and the cause have all been reported in slightly different ways within hours of each other. Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions. Binance reported an estimated total impact of approximately $6.3 billion from a security incident dated October 30, 2026. It said roughly $3 billion in affected assets had been frozen with blockchain partners. The exchange also temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals, revoked authorization for the affected address, and brought in law-enforcement and blockchain-intelligence partners. A Binance spokesperson called the event a “security incident” and said, “Binance will cover all losses.” The company said it would draw on its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and on company funds to do so. That promise is the single most important sentence for ordinary users, because it shifts the question from “will I lose money” to “can Binance afford what it just promised.” On the cause, Binance said its initial investigation points to a possible compromise of a DevOps engineer’s laptop. It also said it found no evidence of a wallet private-key leak. Both statements are early findings, not a final forensic report, and the wording (“possible,” “initial”) signals that the company is not locking in a conclusion yet. Four figures define the story, and they do not all measure the same thing. The $6.3 billion is an estimated total impact. The $3 billion is the amount Binance says it froze. The $1.57 billion and $800 million figures come from the two stablecoin issuers that froze tokens. The table below lays them side by side with their reported status. The gap between $6.3 billion and $3 billion is the part readers should watch. It implies that roughly half of the estimated impact has not been frozen, though Binance has not said how it built the $6.3 billion estimate or how much of it represents movement versus loss. We will not guess at that split. Our earlier explainer on the gap between a headline estimate and a frozen total covers why those two numbers rarely match in the first 24 hours. Reports disagree on the frozen amount. Binance’s statement cited approximately $3 billion, while another update cited a verified figure of $2.54 billion. That is a difference of about $460 million, and it deserves a plain explanation instead of a shrug. There are ordinary reasons for this kind of drift. An initial figure often counts everything a team has flagged or requested to freeze. A verified figure counts only what an issuer or partner has confirmed. Tokens can also move between wallets while a freeze request travels from one party to another. None of those explanations is confirmed for this case, and Binance has not said which one applies. Treat $3 billion as the company’s approximate claim and $2.54 billion as the more conservative figure until a final accounting appears. The same lever carries a cost. Every freeze is a reminder that stablecoin holders depend on an issuer’s willingness to act and on its list of blocked addresses. For institutional treasuries that hold large stablecoin balances, this episode will feed the argument that issuer risk belongs in the same spreadsheet as exchange risk. Three gaps stand out. Binance has not named its law-enforcement or intelligence partners, has not published a timeline for resuming withdrawals, and has not said how or when users will be made whole. Each gap is normal in the first hours of an incident. Each also becomes a trust problem if it lasts more than a few days. Binance said its initial investigation points to a possible compromise of a DevOps engineer’s laptop, and that it saw no evidence of a wallet private-key leak. Read together, those two lines describe an attack path that runs through a person’s workstation rather than through the cryptography that protects the wallets. In plain terms, the company is saying the keys themselves did not leak, but someone may have reached systems that could act on them. Tim Sun, a senior researcher at HashKey Group, framed the effect on sentiment. He said the incident “may further dampen risk appetite” and would likely push investors to reassess centralized-exchange, counterparty, solvency and liquidity risks. His list matters, because it names four separate risks that investors often lump into one. Counterparty risk asks who holds your asset. Solvency risk asks whether they can pay. Liquidity risk asks whether they can pay today. Zhao, Binance’s founder, offered a more measured read. He said the incident “does look like a hack,” a phrase that stops short of a confirmed conclusion, while the company’s own spokesperson stuck to the term “security incident.” The difference in vocabulary between a founder and a spokesperson is small but telling. The company’s formal language is cautious, and its founder is already treating the event as an attack. Our earlier note on Zhao’s first statement and the floor figure reported then shows how that language evolved. Several outlets described the event as potentially the world’s largest cryptocurrency hack, but only as a possibility or an analyst assessment. Nobody with authority has confirmed it. Three reasons argue for restraint. The HashKey view points to the likely channel of damage. A shock of this size rarely shows up first as a single price move. It shows up as a change in how much risk people will carry. Traders hold less on exchanges, treasuries ask harder questions of custodians, and market makers widen spreads when they cannot tell which venue will be next to pause withdrawals. We do not have a verified price reaction to cite for October 30, so we are not offering one. What we can say is that the incident arrives in a week already crowded with security news. Coinbase disclosed a separate third-party incident that touched contact data and, per our report on the Coinbase Amplitude incident , no funds were affected. Investors will compare the two events even though they differ enormously in scale. The medium-term question is where users move their assets. Some will shift to self-custody, which brings its own risks. Our look at two hardware wallet failures and their fix paths is a useful reminder that self-custody removes exchange risk without removing all risk. Large exchange incidents follow a recognizable arc. A first statement arrives within hours, usually with a cautious label. A number appears, then gets revised. A cause is named as “initial” and later refined. Compensation is promised, and the market waits to see whether the promise holds. The Binance event is following that arc on a larger scale than the cases we remember, though we will not cite specific past totals without a source in hand. Recent weeks have shown how crowded the threat picture is. We covered three bridge hacks in seven days , plus smaller exchange incidents such as the Prabang hot wallet breach and a Korean exchange data exposure, and each followed the same disclosure rhythm. The difference with Binance is size. A venue of this scale does not just lose money in an incident like this. It moves the whole market’s sense of what a bad day looks like. One lesson repeats across these cases. The weakest point is rarely the cryptography. It is the human and operational layer around it, which is exactly where an engineer’s laptop sits. If Binance’s initial finding holds up, this incident will join that pattern. You do not need to run an exchange to learn from this. Any team with production access, cloud credentials or signing authority can act on the initial finding today. The steps below come from general security practice and not from any Binance disclosure. AI-assisted tooling adds a new wrinkle. Agents that act on a developer’s behalf inherit that developer’s access, which raises the stakes of a compromised machine. Our write-up on zero trust for AI agents after login lays out how to limit what an agent can do once someone signs in. For wider context, the security section collects our ongoing incident coverage. These are our own assessments, not reported facts, and we label them as such. Each rests on how past incidents have played out and on the statements Binance made on October 30. Any of these could turn out wrong. If Binance’s investigation overturns the laptop finding, prediction two changes shape. If the freeze figure collapses, the market reaction changes with it. We will update this analysis as the company releases more detail. The facts that hold up today are narrow. Binance reported a roughly $6.3 billion estimated impact, said about $3 billion is frozen, paused deposits and withdrawals, and promised to cover all losses through SAFU and company funds. Tether froze nearly $1.57 billion and Circle more than $800 million. Binance’s initial view is a possible DevOps laptop compromise with no sign of a private-key leak. Everything else is open. The total loss, the exact frozen amount, the attack path and the timing of repayment all await confirmation. Users with balances on the exchange should watch Binance’s official channels for status updates, avoid links in unsolicited messages (scammers follow every large incident), and keep their own records of balances. Investors should track the four risks Sun named, namely centralized-exchange, counterparty, solvency and liquidity risk, and decide how much of each they want to carry. Binance reported an estimated total impact of about $6.3 billion from an incident dated October 30, 2026. That is an estimate, and the company has not said how much of it was stolen, moved or recovered. Binance said approximately $3 billion in affected assets is frozen with blockchain partners. Another update cited a verified figure of $2.54 billion, so the exact amount is unconfirmed. Tether froze nearly $1.57 billion and Circle more than $800 million. A Binance spokesperson said, “Binance will cover all losses,” and the company said it would use SAFU and company funds. No payout schedule has been published, so users should follow official updates. Binance’s initial investigation points to a possible compromise of a DevOps engineer’s laptop. The company said it found no evidence of a wallet private-key leak. These are early findings and could change. Analysts such as GSR’s Aravind Srinivasan have used that language, but it remains unconfirmed. The loss figure is an estimate, the frozen total is disputed, and Binance itself calls the event a security incident. Binance temporarily suspended both. The reports we reviewed give no resumption time, so check the exchange’s official announcements for current status. His background is in cryptography and security engineering.

sources.title: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance says it's investigating reports of a potential security incident - NewsChannel20
passages: LOS ANGELES (AP) — Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, said Thursday it’s investigating reports of a potential security issue as its founder said the incident “does look like a hack on Binance.”

“Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information,” the statement continued.
“Rest assured that user funds are completely safe,” a Binance spokesperson said in a statement.

It wasn’t immediately clear the extent of the damage hackers might have been able to accomplish and Binance had not explicitly confirmed that funds had been pilfered, but stablecoin issuers quickly froze funds Thursday evening.

sources.title: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance says it's investigating reports of a potential security incident - NewsChannel20
passages: LOS ANGELES (AP) — Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, said Thursday it’s investigating reports of a potential security issue as its founder said the incident “does look like a hack on Binance.”

“Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information,” the statement continued.
“Rest assured that user funds are completely safe,” a Binance spokesperson said in a statement.

It wasn’t immediately clear the extent of the damage hackers might have been able to accomplish and Binance had not explicitly confirmed that funds had been pilfered, but stablecoin issuers quickly froze funds Thursday evening.

See our Mission > Binance says a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop may have enabled an attacker to submit unauthorized withdrawals in a security incident with an estimated impact of $6.3 billion. The cryptocurrency exchange says it has frozen approximately $3 billion in affected assets on-chain and pledged to cover all losses. Withdrawals remain suspended while Binance overhauls its withdrawal service and related addresses. In its latest service update, the company said deposits are operating normally and that it expects withdrawals to resume within 48 hours. Preliminary findings, disclosed on October 30, suggest the attacker accessed a service container through the engineer’s compromised computer . Binance said it has found no evidence that wallet private keys were leaked. TRM Labs has attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, a North Korean state-sponsored hacking group, with high confidence based on on-chain and off-chain intelligence. The blockchain intelligence firm says the group was also responsible for the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025. Binance operates a cryptocurrency exchange where customers buy, sell, and hold digital assets. The incident has disrupted customers’ ability to move funds out of the platform while the company investigates how unauthorized transactions passed through its withdrawal infrastructure. The company’s initial account points to an intrusion involving the infrastructure used to process withdrawals. A service container is an isolated environment used to run software, although Binance has not yet described the affected container’s specific role or the permissions available to the attacker. In its subsequent update, Binance said multiple factors contributed to the incident and that its security team is tracing the full attack path through the compromised computer, which may have been the entry point. The exchange has not disclosed how the laptop was compromised, how it gained access to the container, or which controls failed to prevent the transactions. It plans to release a detailed technical post-mortem once investigators have established and verified the facts. As part of its immediate response, Binance revoked authorization for the affected address and engaged law enforcement and blockchain intelligence partners to trace and recover assets. Binance says a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop may have enabled an attacker to submit unauthorized withdrawals in a security incident with an estimated impact of $6.3 billion.
The cryptocurrency exchange says it has frozen approximately $3 billion in affected assets on-chain and pledged to cover all losses.

Withdrawals remain suspended while Binance overhauls its withdrawal service and related addresses. In its latest service update, the company said deposits are operating normally and that it expects withdrawals to resume within 48 hours.

Preliminary findings, disclosed on October 30, suggest the attacker accessed a service container through the engineer’s compromised computer . Binance said it has found no evidence that wallet private keys were leaked.

TRM Labs has attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, a North Korean state-sponsored hacking group, with high confidence based on on-chain and off-chain intelligence. The blockchain intelligence firm says the group was also responsible for the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025.

Binance operates a cryptocurrency exchange where customers buy, sell, and hold digital assets. The incident has disrupted customers’ ability to move funds out of the platform while the company investigates how unauthorized transactions passed through its withdrawal infrastructure.

The company’s initial account points to an intrusion involving the infrastructure used to process withdrawals. A service container is an isolated environment used to run software, although Binance has not yet described the affected container’s specific role or the permissions available to the attacker.

In its subsequent update, Binance said multiple factors contributed to the incident and that its security team is tracing the full attack path through the compromised computer, which may have been the entry point.

The exchange has not disclosed how the laptop was compromised, how it gained access to the container, or which controls failed to prevent the transactions. It plans to release a detailed technical post-mortem once investigators have established and verified the facts.
As part of its immediate response, Binance revoked authorization for the affected address and engaged law enforcement and blockchain intelligence partners to trace and recover assets.

Binance said it is working with token issuers, blockchain intelligence firms, law enforcement agencies, and other industry partners to identify and freeze additional assets. Its latest verified frozen total is approximately $3 billion.
That figure describes assets frozen on-chain and should not be treated as an amount already returned to the exchange. Binance has not provided a final recovery total.

The company says it will cover losses with its SAFU fund and corporate funds and has repeatedly assured customers their funds are safe. It also plans to publish an updated Proof of Reserves after remediation is complete.

Earlier announcements described a precautionary suspension of both deposits and withdrawals. The latest update clarifies that deposits are functioning normally, while withdrawals remain paused pending security work. The stated 48-hour resumption window remains an estimate.

Customers should check Binance’s official announcements for service updates and use its established support channels for account questions. Avoid unsolicited recovery offers or messages asking for account credentials, private keys, or payments to unlock withdrawals.

“Rest assured that user funds are completely safe.” Binance also said on X that Binance Alpha trading had been temporarily suspended, and that “the current verified total frozen is $2.54 billion.”

Crypto data provider Arkham Intelligence linked nearly $6 billion in digital assets — including bitcoin, ether, solana and various stablecoins — to 55 wallet addresses it has linked to the potential exploit.
In 2025, Bybit suffered roughly $1.5 billion in losses due to a hack.
Over the past several years, bad actors have also drained billions of dollars in crypto from decentralized exchanges.
Binance co-founder Yi He said deposits remained unaffected and continued to operate normally, while the exchange was working on enhancements to its withdrawal service and related address controls.
It expects to begin resuming withdrawal services within the next 48 hours.
“We have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak.
We will share a detailed technical post-mortem once the investigation is complete and the facts are fully verified,” Binance said.
Bitcoin fell more than 4% to $77,994.96 on Friday as the hack weighed on crypto markets.
The announcement followed moves by several crypto firms, including Circle Internet Group, Tether and Ripple, to freeze funds tied to the hack.

passages: Binance said on October 30, 2026, that it had temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while responding to a security incident.
The company estimated the total impact at about $6.3 billion and said approximately $3 billion in affected assets had been frozen on-chain.
The estimate is not a confirmed final loss figure.
Binance described a potentially compromised DevOps laptop as a preliminary explanation for unauthorized withdrawal requests and said it had found no evidence of a private-key leak.
That account remained a preliminary theory in the company’s update.
The Associated Press reported that Binance had not explicitly confirmed how much, if any, of the affected funds had been stolen at the time of its report.
Binance said it would cover losses using its Secure Asset Fund for Users and company funds.

extraction.body: Binance said Friday that a security incident had an estimated impact of $6.3 billion, with around $3 billion in cryptocurrency assets frozen so far, and pledged to cover all losses. The company's co-CEO Richard Teng said the exchange would cover all losses from the $6.3 billion hack using its SAFU fund and company funds, with about $3 billion in stolen assets frozen on-chain so far. The world's largest crypto exchange said an initial investigation suggests "the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions." Later in the day, Teng said the attack involved a complex process rather than the misuse of a single engineer's permissions, underscoring that the investigation had not attributed responsibility to any individual. He added that there was no evidence of any wallet private key leak. Binance has temporarily suspended withdrawals while it overhauls its withdrawal security systems and has revoked the affected address authorizations, Teng said. The exchange is also working with law enforcement and blockchain intelligence firms to trace and recover the stolen funds, while deposits remain unaffected. Binance co-founder Yi He said deposits remained unaffected and continued to operate normally, while the exchange was working on enhancements to its withdrawal service and related address controls. It expects to begin resuming withdrawal services within the next 48 hours. The exchange said it would cover all losses using its Secure Asset Fund for Users and company funds, adding that customer funds remained safe. Binance also temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals, revoked the affected address authorization and enlisted law enforcement and blockchain intelligence firms to trace and recover funds. The company said it would publish a technical report, and an updated Proof of Reserves after remediation efforts. "We have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak. We will share a detailed technical post-mortem once the investigation is complete and the facts are fully verified," Binance said. The announcement followed moves by several crypto firms, including Circle Internet Group , Tether and Ripple, to freeze funds tied to the hack. Bitcoin fell more than 4% to $77,994.96 on Friday as the hack weighed on crypto markets. Shares of Circle tumbled about 5% in after-hours trading on Thursday. "Our teams are aware of reports of a potential security issue and are actively investigating," a Binance spokesperson said. "Rest assured that user funds are completely safe." Binance also said on X that Binance Alpha trading had been temporarily suspended, and that "the current verified total frozen is $2.54 billion." Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire said Thursday evening in a social media post that the company had frozen more than 800 million in USD Coin associated with the incident. USDT stablecoin issuer Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino also said in on X that his firm had frozen more than 1.5 billion of its stablecoin that may have been related to a potential breach. Jack McDonald, Ripple's senior vice president of stablecoins, said it was actively freezing affected funds held in RLUSD, its U.S. dollar-backed stablecoin. Later, Yi He said in a statement that the XRP and RLUSD-tied firm Ripple helped halt the movement of $200 million of funds linked to the possible attack. But those frozen funds could represent only part of those impacted. Crypto data provider Arkham Intelligence linked nearly $6 billion in digital assets — including bitcoin , ether , solana and various stablecoins — to 55 wallet addresses it has linked to the potential exploit. Arkham identifies, tracks and flags crypto wallets by analyzing publicly available blockchain data. It also solicits tips from its community members. Exploits are not uncommon in the crypto space. In 2025, Bybit suffered roughly $1.5 billion in losses due to a hack. More recently, Bitget lost more than $350 million worth of digital assets in a cyber theft incident. That account remained a preliminary theory in the company’s update.

Binance said it would cover losses using its Secure Asset Fund for Users and company funds.
